articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

A Macquarie Research note flagged potential regulatory headwinds for data-centre development following election outcomes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where proposals to impose moratoriums or restrictions on new projects could affect the industry.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

articles.title: Air pollution over 50 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category while many parts of the city continued to reel under “severe” air quality

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 50 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, official data showed.

The level of PM2.5 (a major pollutant) in Akshardham was 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data. This is about 50.73 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic meter for a 24-hour period.

PM2.5 (Particulate Matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.
The level of PM2.5 in Anand Vihar was 767 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per DPCC data — This is about 51.13 times the WHO permissible limit.
The level of PM2.5 in Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium was 702 micrograms per cubic meter, as per DPCC data, which is about 46.8 times the WHO permissible limit.
The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category while many parts of the city continued to reel under “severe” air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 50 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, official data showed.

The level of PM2.5 (a major pollutant) in Akshardham was 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data. This is about 50.73 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic meter for a 24-hour period.

The level of PM2.5 in Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium was 702 micrograms per cubic meter, as per DPCC data, which is about 46.8 times the WHO permissible limit.

The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category while many parts of the city continued to reel under “severe” air quality.

articles.title: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen evacuated, Embassy says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe

Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen's Hodeidah and Sana'a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country, the Indian Embassy in Yemen said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

“All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals,” the mission said in a post on X.

The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe.

Mr. Saree had said the yacht was carrying 14 Indian nationals and that Houthi forces were rescuing them.
The incident came amid renewed escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, with attacks and counterattacks reported in recent days.

Saudi Arabia has intercepted Houthi missiles and drones, while Saudi-led coalition forces have carried out airstrikes in Yemen, raising fears of a return to wider conflict after relative calm under a 2022 truce.

articles.title: Fire engulfs Jammu’s Nehru Market, guts around 12 shops
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Another blaze was reported in the border district of Kathua, where, a store room at the district police lines went up in flames

Fire gutted at least a dozen shops in the historic Nehru Market in the heart of Jammu city on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, while a separate blaze broke out at the district police lines in Kathua district, officials said.
No casualties were reported in either incident, which occurred amid widespread bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali.
All the same, the exact cause of the blazes is yet to be ascertained.
A massive fire swept the Warehouse Nehru Market, one of Jammu's oldest wholesale hubs of food grains, essential commodities and other daily-use items.
The Fire and Emergency Services Department said the fire began in one of the shops at around 9.15 p.m. and spread quickly to adjoining establishments due to storage of edible oil.
The market has been serving traders, retailers and consumers since the 1950s.

Fire tenders from several stations across Jammu city were rushed to the spot, officials said. At the site, Divisional Commissioner, Jammu, Vikas Kundal, said the fire had been largely brought under control.

"Fire and Emergency Services personnel, police teams and the civil administration are present at the spot. The fire has been brought under control, and efforts are underway to extinguish the remaining flames in the last one or two shops," he told reporters.
Warehouse Association president Deepak Gupta blamed the delayed response of the fire and emergency services for the spread of the flames.

"What started as a small fire has engulfed around 15 shops and threatens to spread further. This is a complete failure and gross negligence on the part of the fire brigade. Despite the fire station being barely five minutes away, only two fire engines arrived after an hour and a half," he alleged.

articles.title: Egypt train collision kills 7, injures 112: Health Ministry
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday (November 8, 2026), derailing several carriages, killing seven people and injuring more than 100 others, according to the authorities.
Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
The Health Ministry said 112 people were injured and were now being treated in hospitals around the Giza area.
The Ministry said the injuries ranged from bruises and abrasions to fractures of the limbs, pelvis and vertebrae, as well as head and facial lacerations and chest injuries.
Forty-five patients had been discharged after receiving treatment, while seven others were expected to be released later.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.
Witnesses described chaotic rescue efforts after the collision, as villagers, first responders and railway workers scrambled to reach passengers trapped inside overturned carriages.
Abdel Wahed Mohamed, 31, who was sitting at a nearby cafe when the collision occurred, said the Aswan-bound train had stopped, when the Fayoum-bound train crashed into it.
“The train overturned at around 1:30 pm. Six carriages overturned,” he said, adding that victims suffered a range of injuries, including head wounds and broken limbs.
Another witness, Ahmed Moussa, 25, said rescuers dug beneath one overturned carriage to reach trapped passengers.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia turns to Syria for help as fighting with Houthis escalates
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week

Syria is preparing to send fighters to Saudi Arabia to deploy along its border and potentially help it fight Iranian-backed rebels in neighbouring Yemen, three officials with knowledge of the plans told The Associated Press .

Syrian military advisers have already deployed to Saudi Arabia, but no fighters have been sent to Yemen, according to a regional official and two Syrian officials, all of whom spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.
Officials in Saudi Arabia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Fighting escalated this summer in Yemen between the Houthi rebels and the government's Saudi-backed forces. The Houthis have also launched direct and deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia in what is the latest front in the regional conflict that began in February when the US and Israel attacked Iran.
Syria, which has a supply of battle-hardened fighters after a long civil war, has so far stayed on the sidelines.
Saudi Arabia has an array of U.S.-supplied fighter jets and missile defences but has been unable to defeat the Houthis in past rounds of conflict.

While Saudi Arabia’s other allies have been reluctant to commit ground forces to its fight with the Houthis, the Syrian government is beholden to it. The Saudis provided funds to Syrian rebels during that country's civil war and have promised much-needed financial assistance for Syria's postwar reconstruction.
A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week.

The official said that a Syrian delegation led by Khaled Khattab, commander of the 82nd Division, had recently made a two-week visit to Saudi Arabia. A second Syrian official said 36 Syrian military officials visited a command and operations room in Jeddah staffed by Saudi and Yemeni officials and received briefings on the different front lines and areas of operation.
A regional official with knowledge of the discussions said Syria had already deployed a “small number of advisers” to Saudi Arabia, where they helped train Yemeni forces inside the kingdom.

articles.title: Trump and his Justice Department stand defiant as Democrats ready an investigative blitz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable”

U.S. President Donald Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their election victories in the midterms, signalling intense conflict to come as lawmakers prepare aggressive investigations into the executive branch next year.
Mr. Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable.”
Attorney General Todd Blanche echoed the Republican president and said criminal investigations of Democrats are possible.

“They are not allowed to just go around threatening existing members of the administration, to go around threatening companies, and that's what President Trump is extremely worried about and he should be,” Mr. Blanche said as he and congressional Democrats appeared on the Sunday news shows to discuss the repercussions from last week's elections.

Rep. Robert Garcia, who is poised to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee in the next Congress, is preparing investigations into what he calls the “Trump crime family.” He said Democrats are not going to be intimidated.
“The days of us not fighting back are over,” said Mr. Garcia, D-Calif.

The early rhetoric sets up a showdown ahead that will likely define Mr. Trump's remaining two years in office and test the power of Congress to put a check on the White House. About seven in 10 voters nationally say Congress is not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the presidency, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of more than 1,00,000 midterm voters.
Democrats have made clear that impeachment is an option.

If there are people who have been "shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people, or stealing from the American people, then they need to be held accountable in a manner consistent with Congress' role, constitutionally,” said Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York.

U.S. President Donald Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their election victories in the midterms, signalling intense conflict to come as lawmakers prepare aggressive investigations into the executive branch next year.

Mr. Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable.”

Attorney General Todd Blanche echoed the Republican president and said criminal investigations of Democrats are possible.

“They are not allowed to just go around threatening existing members of the administration, to go around threatening companies, and that's what President Trump is extremely worried about and he should be,” Mr. Blanche said as he and congressional Democrats appeared on the Sunday news shows to discuss the repercussions from last week's elections.

Rep. Robert Garcia, who is poised to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee in the next Congress, is preparing investigations into what he calls the “Trump crime family.” He said Democrats are not going to be intimidated.

“The days of us not fighting back are over,” said Mr. Garcia, D-Calif.

The early rhetoric sets up a showdown ahead that will likely define Mr. Trump's remaining two years in office and test the power of Congress to put a check on the White House. About seven in 10 voters nationally say Congress is not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the presidency, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of more than 1,00,000 midterm voters.

Democrats have made clear that impeachment is an option.

If there are people who have been "shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people, or stealing from the American people, then they need to be held accountable in a manner consistent with Congress' role, constitutionally,” said Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Water released from Shenbagathoppu dam due to rain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tiruvannamalai Collector Vandhana Garg has warned residents in Cheyyar, Arani, Vandavasi, and Polur towns along Kamandalam Naganathi river against crossing the waterbody as the waterflow in the river is on the rise
Due to continuous rain, water from Shenbagathoppu dam in Tiruvannamalai was released.

Officials of Water Resources Department (WRD), which maintains the dam, said around 100 cusecs of water per second from Shenbagathoppu dam was released as the dam reached around 80 percent of its total storage capacity.

At present, the water level in the dam is 56.24 ft as against its total storage capacity of 62.32 ft. “As per norms, excess rainwater should be released when the dam nears 80% of its total storage capacity, to ensure safety of the structure. Catchment areas, especially Jawadhu Hills that is the primary water source of the dam, have been receiving steady rains,” A. Raja Ganapathy, Assistant Engineer (AE), WRD, told T he Hindu.

Tiruvannamalai Collector Vandhana Garg has warned residents in Cheyyar, Arani, Vandavasi, and Polur towns along Kamandalam Naganathi river against crossing the waterbody as the waterflow in the river is on the rise.

At present, excess water from the dam is discharged into 48 tanks—Polur (18), Arani (12), Arcot (9), Cheyyar (8), and Vandavasi (1)—through four check dams in the district, including Alliyabhad and Karnakur, thereby recharging the water table in and around these villages.
On Saturday, rain lashed Vellore, Gudiyatham, Arcot, Ambur, Vaniyambadi, Chengam and surrounding villages in Vellore, Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai, and Tirupattur districts.

articles.title: Renovated bus terminus in Ranipet town opened for public use
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Work to restore the terminus was started in 2022
After more than four years of renovation work, the restored ₹13.55-crore integrated bus terminus on the Ranipet-Walajah Main Road was opened for public use, ahead of Deepavali.

Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters. “The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses. The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter.

Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality.

Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri.

Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days.

Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus.

Work to restore the terminus was started in 2022

After more than four years of renovation work, the restored ₹13.55-crore integrated bus terminus on the Ranipet-Walajah Main Road was opened for public use, ahead of Deepavali.

Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters. “The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses. The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter.

Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality.

Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri.

Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days.

Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus.

articles.title: Two youths arrested for possessing narcotics in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs
Two youths were arrested by Vellore South police for possession of 1300 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near the fort complex in Vellore town on Saturday.
The police identified them as R. Vinoth, 23, and his friend B. Manimaran, 23. They were residents of Vellore town.

Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Vellore SP N.U. Sivaraman, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places in the district. During a surprise check near the fort complex, the team apprehended the suspects.

They checked the duo and their bags, where they found a huge quantity of pharmaceutical drugs in them. Investigation found that the gang had placed an order for tablets with pharmacies online. The tablets were sent by couriers to them.

The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs. A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way.

articles.title: Gang held near Vaniyambadi for burglary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences

A gang of five persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur on Saturday for stealing 52 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects and around ₹20,000 lakh cash from the house of a painter recently.

The arrested persons were identified as K. Naveen, 26, T. Parthiban, 30, S. Gopinath, 39, G. Manikandan, 40, and C. Sarathkumar, 25. They are previous offenders and have theft cases against them in Salem, Dharmapuri, Tirupattur, Thanjavur, and Pudukottai.

Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, R. Prabhakaran, 39, was living with his family including wife Geetha (34) and mother Ambika (65) in the house near Vaniyambadi town a few days ago when the gang barged into the house. The police said the gang allegedly tied R. Prabhakaran, 39, and his family and stole the valuables from the house before fleeing the spot.

Mr. Prabhakaran managed to untie himself and alerted Vaniyambadi Taluk police. Special teams were formed to nab the suspects. The police also analysed CCTV camera footage to identify suspects. The suspects were traced to a hideout in Thanjavur and were arrested. A car used by the gang was also seized.

The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences. They travel to various parts of the State and stay in a locality before indulging in burglary. A case was registered and a probe is under way.

articles.title: T.N. may be heading towards a water crisis, unless northeast monsoon comes to the rescue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the combined storage was around 92%
Tamil Nadu may be in for a spell of water crisis and lower rice production this time if the current Northeast monsoon does not come to its rescue.

As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the situation was completely different with the combined storage being around 92%.

The State’s largest dam, Mettur, has about 23 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) but this is hardly enough for the authorities to maintain sustained release of water to farmers, beyond a week, in the Cauvery delta.

The rainfall during the Northeast monsoon has been moderate as the State has received around 240 mm of rainfall against the anticipated 236 mm. It should get at least 260 mm more to be considered comfortable, the most of which should materialise in November. Ordinarily, December yields only about 20% of the total rainfall of the monsoon.

In fact, the existing pattern of rainfall registered by the State so far during the season appears to be more in tune with the forecast made by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), which, in late September, predicted that the State would get 438 mm during the entire monsoon against the normal 434 mm, a deviation of one per cent. The Meteorological department, in its outlook at the beginning of October for the season, referred to the southern peninsular region of the country in general and stated that the expected rainfall “ is most likely to be normal (88-112%) of the Long Period Average (LPA).”

The TNAU, which was more specific in its forecast than the Meteorological department, had anticipated only a normal rainfall for the core districts of the Cauvery delta – Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai. Despite the water availability at Mettur not being comfortable and the expectation of a subdued rainfall, farmers have gone in for raising paddy during the samba-thaladi cultivation season to the tune of around 3.62 lakh hectares. Of this, nearly 50% falls under “direct sown“ category of cultivation, which means that seeds are directly sown instead of transplantation. This method is followed in times of water shortage.

But, the problem with water availability seems to be higher in the remaining areas of the State, a reflection of which can be seen in the way the farmers have taken to paddy this time. The paddy coverage in the non-delta areas of the State is about 1.3 lakh hectares shorter than what it was last year. As compared to the previous year’s share (39%) of direct sowing in the overall paddy coverage, this time the method’s share is about 57%. In 2025-26, rice production in the State was 77.5 lakh tonnes, about one lakh tonnes lower than the previous high of 79.07 lakh tonnes during 2021-22.

As part of its efforts for protecting the crop in the Cauvery delta, the State government, at meetings of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) on Friday, demanded that Karnataka release around 20. 7 tmcft including the backlog of about 16.9 tmc ft. However, the Authority ratified the decision of the Committee, which had recommended that Karnataka release 3.88 tmcft to Tamil Nadu through 3,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) per day for 15 days from Saturday (November 7, 2026).

articles.title: T.N. government to withdraw G.O. promoting Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar as temporary Director of Legal Studies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan record the submission that the vacancy would now be filled up as per regular process

Tamil Nadu Government has informed the Madras High Court of its decision to withdraw a Government Order (G.O.) issued on September 8, 2026, temporarily promoting Tamil Nadu Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar Gowri Ramesh as the Director of Legal Studies (DLS). It said, the vacancy shall be filled up through a regular process as contemplated under the Special Rules for the Tamil Nadu Collegiate Educational Service.

Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan recorded the submission made by Advocate General Vijay Narayan and disposed of a writ appeal filed against a single judge’s October 1, 2026 order granting an interim stay of the G.O. The Bench also closed the writ petition pending before the single judge since nothing survived in it pursuant to the government’s decision to withdraw the G.O.

Vellore Government Law College principal M. Rajeswaran had initially filed a writ petition in the High Court in June 2026 challenging a Government Order issued on March 3, 2026 allocating full additional charge of the post of DLS to Ms. Gowri. Then, he had contended that a full-time Registrar of the Law University could not be given additional charge of the full time post of DLS too and that it was against the service rules.

The petitioner contended that the vacancy in the post of DLS could be filled up only through direct recruitment, transfer or by promoting those holding the post of principal in any of the government law colleges spread across the State. Stating that he was senior to Ms. Gowri, the petitioner had wondered how could she attend the Syndicate meetings in her ex-officio capacity as the Registrar of the university and also as the DLS.

Justice P.T. Asha had entertained that writ petition on June 30, 2026 and stayed the operation of the March 3, 2026 G.O. When that stay order was taken on appeal by the State, the A-G told the first Division Bench that the State government intends to commence the regular process of appointing the DLS in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules and complete it within a period of two months.

The Bench disposed of the writ appeal on July 23, 2026 after taking note that the government had also issued a G.O. on July 21, 2026 giving full additional charge of the post of DLS to a joint secretary in the Law department instead of Ms. Gowri.

Thereafter, the September 8, 2026 G.O. was issued temporarily promoting Ms. Gowri as the DLS by invoking the emergency powers conferred on the government under Section 47(1) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016. Hence, Mr. Rajeswaran had filed yet another writ petition in the High Court on September 29, 2026 challenging the latest G.O.

This time, Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar stayed the September 8, 2026 G.O. on the ground that the government ought not to have invoked Section 47(1) of the 2016 Act after having given an undertaking before the Division Bench in July 2026 that the post of DLS would be appointed in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules.

When a State appeal against this stay order came up before the first Bench, the latter recorded A-G’s submission that the latest G.O. shall be withdrawn. “The State shall pursue with the promotion process in accordance with law. The statement of Advocate General that in the meantime, the State will take steps to fill up the post temporarily, as was done when the earlier writ appeal was disposed of, is recorded,” the Bench said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 08 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 T.N. government to withdraw G.O. promoting Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar as temporary Director of Legal Studies

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan record the submission that the vacancy would now be filled up as per regular process

Tamil Nadu Government has informed the Madras High Court of its decision to withdraw a Government Order (G.O.) issued on September 8, 2026, temporarily promoting Tamil Nadu Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar Gowri Ramesh as the Director of Legal Studies (DLS). It said, the vacancy shall be filled up through a regular process as contemplated under the Special Rules for the Tamil Nadu Collegiate Educational Service.

Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan recorded the submission made by Advocate General Vijay Narayan and disposed of a writ appeal filed against a single judge’s October 1, 2026 order granting an interim stay of the G.O. The Bench also closed the writ petition pending before the single judge since nothing survived in it pursuant to the government’s decision to withdraw the G.O.

Vellore Government Law College principal M. Rajeswaran had initially filed a writ petition in the High Court in June 2026 challenging a Government Order issued on March 3, 2026 allocating full additional charge of the post of DLS to Ms. Gowri. Then, he had contended that a full-time Registrar of the Law University could not be given additional charge of the full time post of DLS too and that it was against the service rules.

The petitioner contended that the vacancy in the post of DLS could be filled up only through direct recruitment, transfer or by promoting those holding the post of principal in any of the government law colleges spread across the State. Stating that he was senior to Ms. Gowri, the petitioner had wondered how could she attend the Syndicate meetings in her ex-officio capacity as the Registrar of the university and also as the DLS.

Justice P.T. Asha had entertained that writ petition on June 30, 2026 and stayed the operation of the March 3, 2026 G.O. When that stay order was taken on appeal by the State, the A-G told the first Division Bench that the State government intends to commence the regular process of appointing the DLS in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules and complete it within a period of two months.

The Bench disposed of the writ appeal on July 23, 2026 after taking note that the government had also issued a G.O. on July 21, 2026 giving full additional charge of the post of DLS to a joint secretary in the Law department instead of Ms. Gowri.

Thereafter, the September 8, 2026 G.O. was issued temporarily promoting Ms. Gowri as the DLS by invoking the emergency powers conferred on the government under Section 47(1) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016. Hence, Mr. Rajeswaran had filed yet another writ petition in the High Court on September 29, 2026 challenging the latest G.O.

This time, Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar stayed the September 8, 2026 G.O. on the ground that the government ought not to have invoked Section 47(1) of the 2016 Act after having given an undertaking before the Division Bench in July 2026 that the post of DLS would be appointed in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules.

When a State appeal against this stay order came up before the first Bench, the latter recorded A-G’s submission that the latest G.O. shall be withdrawn. “The State shall pursue with the promotion process in accordance with law. The statement of Advocate General that in the meantime, the State will take steps to fill up the post temporarily, as was done when the earlier writ appeal was disposed of, is recorded,” the Bench said.

It said, the vacancy shall be filled up through a regular process as contemplated under the Special Rules for the Tamil Nadu Collegiate Educational Service.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: When a State appeal against this stay order came up before the first Bench, the latter recorded A-G’s submission that the latest G.O. shall be withdrawn. “The State shall pursue with the promotion process in accordance with law. The statement of Advocate General that in the meantime, the State will take steps to fill up the post temporarily, as was done when the earlier writ appeal was disposed of, is recorded,” the Bench said.

articles.title: Locals burn effigy of Christian priests at Basanti in WB
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A group of locals at Basanti in West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas on Thursday (November 5, 2026) burnt effigy of local Christian priests and submitted a memorandum to the police station against the local priests. Basanti has been on the boil since November 1 after a newly constructed church was vandalised by a mob claiming their allegiance to a Hindutva outfit.

The protest on Thursday (November 5, 2026) was organised by Adivasi Eilya Parishad, a local organisation whose representatives said that Adivasis are being lured for conversion on the promise of curing disease, which should not be allowed.
The West Bengal chapter of National Christian Council (NCC) in a press statement added that effigy of local priests were set on fire at Chowmatha crossing in Basanti.

“Later in the evening, during the Friday prayer service, a group of approximately 20–25 people allegedly surrounded women attending the service. According to the complaints received, the women were forced to break their traditional conch-shell bangles (Shakha) and wipe off their vermilion (Sindoor),” the press statement said.

Father Parimal Kanji, the priest-in-charge at Basanti, stated that the alleged perpetrators were outsiders and not local residents and confirmed that a written complaint had been submitted to the police.

Arpan Rana, State General Secretary of the National Christian Council said that Christian communities in West Bengal do not seek confrontation but justice, equal protection and the rule of law. “The Chief Minister is speaking about religious freedom, yet the practical experience of some minority communities raises serious questions about their safety and protection,” Mr. Rana said.

Herod Mullick, the founding State Secretary of Bangiya Chrisityo Pariseba said that the government and administration’s silence has emboldened attackers, who have shifted from targeting small independent congregations to raiding older, established churches.

“While the police are well aware of the situation and continue to accept written complaints, no legal action is mysteriously being taken against anyone, making the government’s ongoing silence both baffling and suspicious,” he said.
According to Basanti Police Station, an FIR has been registered in connection with the incident of attack on the Church and notices have been issued to some accused.

There has been an increase in attacks on churches and Christian gatherings after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power. According to Christian organisations, U.S.-based research project, India Hate Lab, has documented at least 60 incidents of hate crimes and targeted attacks against Christians in West Bengal across 13 districts between May 13 and September 20 this year.

articles.title: NDA extends winning streak, set to crush YSRCP in ZPTC and MPTC elections as well
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As of 9 p.m., the TDP wins 229 ZPTCs and 4,823 MPTCs, JSP 36 and 644, BJP eight and 130, and YSRCP 20 and 1,050; TDP upsets YSRCP by wresting Pulivendula ZPTC; fruit of good governance, says Lokesh

The TDP and its allies, the JSP and the BJP, continued their stellar performance in the elections to the Zilla and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs and MPTCs) after crushing the YSRCP in the Urban Local Body (ULB) polls. They were all set to pull off another decisive victory over the YSRCP.
Polling was conducted for 582 ZPTCs and 7,767 MPTCs in 28 districts on November 5 following the declaration of 77 and 2,051 ZPTCs and MPTCs respectively as unanimously elected.

As per information furnished by the State Election Commission (SEC) at 9 p.m. on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the TDP won a total of 229 ZPTCs, including 71 unanimous and 158 contested, JSP 36 (2 unanimous and 34 contested) and BJP 8 (three unanimous and 5 contested), whereas the YSRCP managed to win 20 (one unanimous and 19 contested).

In the MPTCs, the TDP won 4,823 (1,780 unanimous and 3,043 conttested), JSP 644 (107 unanimous and 537 contested), the BJP 130 (53 unanimous and 77 contested) and YSRCP 1,050 (89 unanimous and 961 contested).
State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha stated in a press release that the counting process was still underway and progressing peacefully.
The TDP won most of the ZPTCs and MPTCs in Kadapa district, which had been the stronghold of the YSRCP.

After scoring an impressive victory in the elections to the Pulivendula Municipality, the TDP won the Pulivendula ZPTC also, causing a major upset to the YSRCP, which apparently lost the confidence of the people in what had been the stronghold of the Y.S. Rajasekhar Reddy family.
The TDP was in the driver’s seat in the ZPTC seat of Kuppam (Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s home turf) and in a vast majority of the other ZPTCs, and MPTCs in Chittoor and Annamayya districts.

Reacting to the results that were coming in, IT Minister Nara Lokesh described the TDP-led coalition’s overwhelming triumph in the ZPTC and MPTC elections as the “fruits of their good governance and proof of the perfect coordination among the ruling parties.”

TDP State president Palla Srinivasa Rao said the mood was overwhelmingly in favour of his party and its allies due to their good governance, and it was a profound mandate for welfare, development and social justice.

As of 9 p.m., the TDP wins 229 ZPTCs and 4,823 MPTCs, JSP 36 and 644, BJP eight and 130, and YSRCP 20 and 1,050; TDP upsets YSRCP by wresting Pulivendula ZPTC; fruit of good governance, says Lokesh

The TDP and its allies, the JSP and the BJP, continued their stellar performance in the elections to the Zilla and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs and MPTCs) after crushing the YSRCP in the Urban Local Body (ULB) polls. They were all set to pull off another decisive victory over the YSRCP.

Polling was conducted for 582 ZPTCs and 7,767 MPTCs in 28 districts on November 5 following the declaration of 77 and 2,051 ZPTCs and MPTCs respectively as unanimously elected.

As per information furnished by the State Election Commission (SEC) at 9 p.m. on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the TDP won a total of 229 ZPTCs, including 71 unanimous and 158 contested, JSP 36 (2 unanimous and 34 contested) and BJP 8 (three unanimous and 5 contested), whereas the YSRCP managed to win 20 (one unanimous and 19 contested).

In the MPTCs, the TDP won 4,823 (1,780 unanimous and 3,043 conttested), JSP 644 (107 unanimous and 537 contested), the BJP 130 (53 unanimous and 77 contested) and YSRCP 1,050 (89 unanimous and 961 contested).

State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha stated in a press release that the counting process was still underway and progressing peacefully.

The TDP won most of the ZPTCs and MPTCs in Kadapa district, which had been the stronghold of the YSRCP.

After scoring an impressive victory in the elections to the Pulivendula Municipality, the TDP won the Pulivendula ZPTC also, causing a major upset to the YSRCP, which apparently lost the confidence of the people in what had been the stronghold of the Y.S. Rajasekhar Reddy family.

The TDP was in the driver’s seat in the ZPTC seat of Kuppam (Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s home turf) and in a vast majority of the other ZPTCs, and MPTCs in Chittoor and Annamayya districts.

Reacting to the results that were coming in, IT Minister Nara Lokesh described the TDP-led coalition’s overwhelming triumph in the ZPTC and MPTC elections as the “fruits of their good governance and proof of the perfect coordination among the ruling parties.”

TDP State president Palla Srinivasa Rao said the mood was overwhelmingly in favour of his party and its allies due to their good governance, and it was a profound mandate for welfare, development and social justice.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing personnel at key airbase near China frontier, Defence Minister warns of adversaries exploiting ‘vulnerabilities’; he also reviews Army’s LAC infrastructure, operational preparedness and lauds initiatives aimed at strengthening ties with local communities

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh visited members of the armed forces at multiple locations in West Bengal on Saturday (November 7, 2026) and highlighted a changing nature of warfare while describing the northeast as India’s “first edge” rather than its “last edge”.

The security landscape around the country has become increasingly complex and the armed forces must maintain the highest level of operational readiness to effectively counter any threats to national security, he told personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force station. Delivering his message on the eve of Deepavali from the key airbase near the frontier with China in the Eastern sector, Mr. Singh, without naming any country, said the adversary now avoids direct confrontation but seeks to exploit certain "vulnerabilities".

He called upon the armed forces to keep special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience, and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats, according to the Defence Ministry. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma, and other senior officials of the IAF were present on the occasion.

Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important region and a crucial link in India's security framework, Mr. Singh commended the courage and dedication of the defence personnel towards safeguarding national interests. He stated that the Air Force personnel deployed in the region serve as a robust shield for the security of the eastern sector, and their preparedness is fundamental to maintaining stability in the region.

The Defence Minister later reviewed the operational preparedness of the Army’s Trishakti Corps at Sukna, with a focus on infrastructure development along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), deployment of advanced military equipment, and adoption of emerging technologies to enhance combat effectiveness.

Mr. Singh expressed satisfaction with the operational preparedness of the corps and appreciated its contribution to infrastructure development and community welfare initiatives in border areas aimed at strengthening ties with local communities.
Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth, Eastern Army Commander Lt. Gen. VMB Krishnan and Trishakti Corps Commander Lt. Gen. Man Raj Singh Mann were present during the review.

Addressing personnel during a ‘ barakhana ’ on the eve of Deepawali, Mr. Singh commended their courage, professionalism, and dedication in safeguarding the country’s frontiers under challenging operational conditions.

Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, he said security challenges were no longer confined to conventional exchanges of gunfire and artillery but increasingly involved hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyberattacks, drone incursions, and information warfare.

He cautioned that adversaries were using social media to spread rumours, deploying drones to monitor sensitive locations, and attempting to compromise military systems through cyberattacks. He exhorted personnel to remain vigilant and prepared to tackle emerging threats across all domains.

articles.title: Nallur toll plaza on Kolkata National Highway to be moved to Durainallur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National Highways Authority of India has planned to shift the toll plaza at Nallur on the Chennai - Kolkata National Highway. It will be moved to Durainallur, which is about 13 km from the present location. The plaza is notorious for long waits during rush hours.

Motorists fed up with waiting at the Nallur Plaza will get some relief from this move. “Residents of areas such as Karanodai, Janapanchathiram, Nallur and Periyapalayam will find it very convenient when the plaza is removed. There are several colleges in the area and the buses transporting students too wait in queue to cross the plaza on many occasions. Shifting of the plaza has been a long-time demand,” said K. Suresh Kumar, a resident.

Ramesh, another resident, suggested that the width of the road be narrowed at that location. “It is now wider than the road width, making it difficult to cross. It would be helpful if the road stretch is normalised and shops regularised,” he said.

Sources in the NHAI said that the existing location was no longer viable as a number of new roads have been laid in the surroundings making it possible for road users to avoid the plaza. This will lead to loss of revenue. “The plaza is also located inside municipal limits, making it pertinent to shift it outside. The contract of the current agency managing the plaza will get over by May next year. We hope to get the design ready for the new plaza by then,” explained a source.
Around 50,000 passenger car units use that road on a daily basis. The plaza is also likely to be a multi-lane free flow tolling system without toll booths and operators.

articles.title: Ten of 11 stations on Kochi metro’s Pink Line to have entry/exit from both sides of road
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Terminal station at Smart City to have entry/exit only on the right hand side; foot overbridge mulled for members of the public to access the station

With about 70% of the viaduct of the Kochi metro’s 11.20-km Kakkanad extension (Pink Line) complete and the laying of tracks set to begin, pending works on all 11 stations in the corridor are set to gather momentum after an initial lull. This is in keeping with the revised deadline of August 2027, which has been set to complete the works on the extension, official sources said.

Contrary to the perception that a few stations will have entry/exit only from one side of the road, 10 of the 11 stations will have entry/exit from both sides of the road beneath the upcoming metro extension. The terminal station, whose work is set to begin on the Smart City premises, will have entry/exit only on the right hand side, while a foot overbridge will provide a link for members of the public to access the station, they added.

The structural work on the entry/exit of the Chittetukara station is over on both the left hand side and the right hand side of the road, while that of the left-hand side of the KINFRA Park station is over. Work on the right hand side of the Vazhakkala station is over, and architectural work has begun. Structural works on the left hand side entry/exit of the stations at Civil Station Junction and Cochin SEZ are scheduled to be completed by the first week of December.
The foundation works of the entry/exit of the Chembumukku station whose land acquisition suffered delay is over, and rest of the works is set to gather pace on both sides of the road, it is learnt.

Metro sources attributed the delay in commencing work on the right hand side entry/exit of Palarivattom Junction and Padamugal stations to hassles associated with land acquisition. The requisite plots of land for the two stations will be acquired by the end of December. The pending works on most metro stations will gather pace in the coming weeks, since the requisite pre-fabricated structures are ready at the casting yard. They will be transported in lorries and launched at the stations concerned. This will be followed by architectural works, laying of tracks, and installation of signals and telecommunication equipment, lifts and escalators, to name a few.

The first station on the Pink Line is at Palarivattom Junction, followed by stations at Alinchuvadu, Chembumukku, Vazhakkala, Padamugal, Civil Station Junction, Cochin SEZ, Chittettukara, KINFRA Park, Infopark, and Smart City.

articles.title: Trump says he wants UFC chief Dana White for White House press secretary
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. White, ⁠chief executive of ⁠the Ultimate Fighting Championship, is a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Mr. Trump wrote in ​a Truth ‌Social post

Facing an incoming Democratic Congress, U.S. President Donald Trump struck a combative tone Saturday (November 7, 2026), offering friend and “violent fighter” Dana White the White House press secretary job and ordering the Justice Department to investigate his opponents.

Democrats handed Mr. Trump’s Republicans a blowout defeat in the midterm elections this week and will take control of both chambers of Congress in January. They promise robust investigations into Mr. Trump and his administration.
Mr. Trump, however, showed no signs of being chastened.
He offered the press secretary post to Mr. White, a loyal supporter and head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) mixed martial arts organisation.
“Dana, please take the job!” Mr. Trump posted on social media, describing White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior.”

Speaking to reporters following a boxing event in London late Saturday (November 7, 2026), Mr. White said he was flying to Washington “right now” and will meet with Mr. Trump on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. White had earlier shared a photo -- possibly AI-generated -- showing him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”
Mr. Trump on Saturday (November 7, 2026) also ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats for “extortion at the highest level.”
“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” he wrote, adding that he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act.”
Denying that anyone in his administration had committed impeachable offenses, Trump called for prison time for “these EXTORTIONISTS.”

articles.title: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav writes to President, seeks action against DU Professor Sangeet Ragi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Yadav said that Mr. Ragi used the abusive language against Yadav community on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav wrote a letter to President Draupadi Murmu, requesting her to order strict action against Delhi University Professor Sangeet Ragi for allegedly insulting the Yadav community.

Mr. Yadav said that he used the abusive language on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He mentioned that action is necessary so that it serves as an exemplary punishment, ensuring that in a diverse country like India, no one dares to insult any society, class or community in the name of freedom of expression, and thus hurting unity and integrity of the nation.
The three-page letter dated November 6, 2026, was shared with media on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

“I am writing to you in my capacity as a Member of Parliament (Rajyasabha) to express my serious concern regarding the alleged caste-based derogatory remarks made by Professor Sangeet Ragi of the University of Delhi against India’s largest community (Yadav/Ahir) during a televised public debate,” Mr. Yadav stated.

He added, “The controversy surrounding the Professor’s remarks has generated considerable public resentment. According to media reports, the remarks reportedly included the use of expressions such as “gawar” in conjunction with the term “Ahir”. The subsequent controversy has raised serious concerns about the use of caste identity, community genealogy and social stereotypes as instruments of public insult and humiliation.”
Mr. Yadav asserted that the matter is particularly disturbing because the individual concerned occupies a responsible academic position at one of India’s most prestigious public universities.

He further said a university professor, especially one associated with political science, is expected to uphold constitutional morality, democratic values, social equality and respect for the dignity of every community.

“A teacher who must be educating his students against societal stereotypes is here himself strengthening unacceptable caste based derogatory stereotypes. Prof. Ragi has been notorious for habitually making indecent and unacceptable remarks and expletives against women folk, dalit community and whole bahujan community from time to time in TV debates,” Mr. Yadav said,
He mentioned that Mr. Ragi’s remarks have caused considerable resentment among members of the affected communities, students and various civil society organisations.

RJD MP explained that the Yadav/Ahir community has a long and complex social, historical and cultural genealogy adding that its identity, like that of every other community, deserves recognition and respect rather than being subjected to ridicule, social stereotyping or derogatory characterisation.

Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav wrote a letter to President Draupadi Murmu, requesting her to order strict action against Delhi University Professor Sangeet Ragi for allegedly insulting the Yadav community.

Mr. Yadav said that he used the abusive language on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He mentioned that action is necessary so that it serves as an exemplary punishment, ensuring that in a diverse country like India, no one dares to insult any society, class or community in the name of freedom of expression, and thus hurting unity and integrity of the nation.

The three-page letter dated November 6, 2026, was shared with media on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

“I am writing to you in my capacity as a Member of Parliament (Rajyasabha) to express my serious concern regarding the alleged caste-based derogatory remarks made by Professor Sangeet Ragi of the University of Delhi against India’s largest community (Yadav/Ahir) during a televised public debate,” Mr. Yadav stated.

He added, “The controversy surrounding the Professor’s remarks has generated considerable public resentment. According to media reports, the remarks reportedly included the use of expressions such as “gawar” in conjunction with the term “Ahir”. The subsequent controversy has raised serious concerns about the use of caste identity, community genealogy and social stereotypes as instruments of public insult and humiliation.”

Mr. Yadav asserted that the matter is particularly disturbing because the individual concerned occupies a responsible academic position at one of India’s most prestigious public universities.

He further said a university professor, especially one associated with political science, is expected to uphold constitutional morality, democratic values, social equality and respect for the dignity of every community.

“A teacher who must be educating his students against societal stereotypes is here himself strengthening unacceptable caste based derogatory stereotypes. Prof. Ragi has been notorious for habitually making indecent and unacceptable remarks and expletives against women folk, dalit community and whole bahujan community from time to time in TV debates,” Mr. Yadav said,

He mentioned that Mr. Ragi’s remarks have caused considerable resentment among members of the affected communities, students and various civil society organisations.
