articles.title: 42 days of SRFTI protest; classes suspended till December 11
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Students send message of resistance and fight for justice on Deepavali

The agitation at the Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (SRFTI) continued for 42 days as class suspension was extended till December 11, affecting academic life. Students of the film institute on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that “This Diwali we choose to resist”, while authorities said they were “keen" to resume classes.

“Diwali has always been a special occasion at SRFTI... But this year, the familiar celebrations are overshadowed by fear, uncertainty and an ongoing struggle for justice,” an official post by the SRFTI student union said on Saturday (November 7, 2026), a day before Deepavali. They also said that the day they are served justice will be Deepavali for them.

“While the faculty and administration are ready to resume classes, a section of students continues to remain disengaged from academics and disrupt the functioning of the Institute through repeated violations of its rules and orders,” Registrar Deepak Kumar told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026). He further added that they are asking students to come forward for constructive dialogue.

As of November 7, at least 25 students have received show cause notices, with 11 of them receiving them last Thursday (November 5, 2026). Six students have faced rustication, and one FIR has been registered against student union Vice-President Shubham.

Shubham is one of the six students who got the rustication notice for allegedly vandalising the Vice-Chancellor Santosh Ajmeera’s office and manhandling him. However, all of these allegations have been denied by the students.
According to the students, two contractual faculty members, and five resource persons of SRFTI have also been terminated from their jobs for showing solidarity with the students.

As the classes remained suspended, the hostels and mess were also closed for students. Many students have been living under a makeshift tent during the protest, as many of them are from States outside West Bengal.

The impasse at the campus started on September 27 after violence broke out on the film institute’s campus as a right-wing RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat (ABGP) held an event on the campus and clashed with students. Several students were left injured in the clashes.

Since then, students have demanded accountability from the authorities for failing to protect them inside their own campus. However, six of them were served a rustication notice two weeks later, on October 15, for manhandling the VC.
The students are also demanding the VC’s resignation for failing to take action against the violence, which left many students injured.

articles.title: Presidency University expels student for allegedly defacing Vivekananda poster
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The university also barred an ex-student from the campus; SFI condemns expulsion, ABVP welcomes authority action

The Presidency University has expelled two students for allegedly defacing Swami Vivekananda posters inside the campus, official sources said. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad had alleged that Left student factions had vandalised the poster and had filed a police complaint on October 14.

The two female students have been barred from taking admission in any course at the university in the future. The university had formed a committee to investigate the matter and has checked CCTV footage of the campus and heard from various stakeholders to come to a decision. One of them is a current student and the other was an ex-student who had finished her post-graduate course a few months back.

“Two students have been expelled from the studentship/post-studentship academic activities. It has also been decided that they won’t be allowed admission to any future degree program in this university,” official sources said.

“Presidency University always stood for dignified academic discourse and debate on different scientific/socio-political issues. The university is not in a position to tolerate any abuse to any thinkers/ideas/organizations,” Presidency University registrar Debajyoti Konar said.

The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) condemned the expulsion on Saturday (November 7, 2026). “By imposing an expulsion that threatens to destroy the academic lives of these two students, the administration has established a deeply dangerous precedent,” their statement from the SFI Presidency unit added. They also said that students must be punished if they took part in vandalism, but asked for corrective steps and rehabilitation, rather than punitive or retaliatory measures.
Meanwhile, the ABVP student wing welcomed the expulsion and said that such “anti-India” sentiments and anti-national conspiracies do not have a place in the educational institutes.

“If such incidents are repeated in the future, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) will once again stand firmly against them. Our message is clear: ABVP possesses the only vaccine capable of eliminating the Chinese virus of anti-national ideology,” Ananta Barui, State Media In-charge, ABVP told T he Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

The ABVP student wing had previously alleged that the Left student wings were conducting the vandalism of their posters. However, the Left student wings of Presidency had issued a statement and denied the allegations.
“ABVP has started the work of cleaning the Tukde-Tukde gang from Jadavpur and Presidency. This work must be continued,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said.

This comes as both Jadavpur University and Presidency University, two of the top-ranking educational institutes of the State, remained embroiled in repeated controversies and face-offs with the right-wing student group. A massive fight had erupted at JU in August as left- and right-wing student groups clashed.

fullParagraphs: A German publication ranked Bihar Museum among the best in the world. Mayank Kumar visits to understand what went into the making of the museum and what visitors think of its contribution to the development of Indian civilization

On November 3, Soumya Pathak, 23, a final-year medical student studying at a medical college in Ambala, Haryana, is exploring exhibits showcasing relics from prehistoric times at the Bihar Museum in Patna. Pathak belongs to Muzaffarpur in Bihar, and is looking at some coins from the Mauryan (321–185 B.C.E) and Gupta ages (early 4th to mid-6th Century C.E.).

She passes through interactive galleries which highlight Bihar’s pivotal role in shaping two major world religions: Jainism and Buddhism. “I have been thinking of coming here for a long time, but after reading on social media that the museum is ranked the best in Asia, I decided to spend a day here,” she says. Pathak is enroute to Muzaffarpur for the Deepavali holidays and came to the museum directly from Patna’s Jay Prakash Narayan airport, about four kilometres away. Pathak is proud of her State that is often in the news for poverty and violence.
Political & National Report: A bridge between past and present. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Ahead of Deepavali, Chhath festivals, migrants reach Bihar in hordes covering thousands of kilometers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four young men on Saturday (November 7, 2026), from Bengaluru, travelled about 2,200 km riding on an old auto-rickshaw to reach Areraj town, in East Champaran

Ahead of Deepavali and the four-day Chhath festival, migrants are visiting different places of Bihar in hordes. With the flight fares skyrocketing and train ticket charts shown full, migrants are reaching their destination by buses and even riding on old auto-rickshaws covering thousands of kilometres.

Four young men on Saturday (November 7, 2026), from Bengaluru, travelled about 2,200 km riding on an old auto-rickshaw to reach Areraj town, near Someshwarnath Dham temple in Motihari of East Champaran district in Bihar.

Reaching their destination in three days, they told local media persons that it was their “desire to celebrate Deepavali and Chhath festival along with family members” and the air ticket fares had gone beyond their capacity. With train ticket charts shown chock-a-bloc they, eventually, decided to travel to their village in Areraj by riding on the old auto-rickshaw, which one of them runs in Bengaluru for a living. A total of 3,279.57 tonnes of 'banned and non-compliant' food products worth ₹81.80 crore were seized, it said.
Additionally, the regulator issued 10,047 improvement notices to food business operators.
This calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators and e-commerce companies to ensure safe food for consumers.

articles.title: Singapore-based senior IT executive shot dead over parking dispute in Faridabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused fired several rounds at the victim and his son; the victim succumbed to injuries and the son escaped unhurt

A 42-year-old senior executive of a Singapore-based IT services and solutions company was shot dead following a dispute over parking in Faridabad on Friday (November 6, 2026) evening. The police have arrested the accused, identified as Mohan Sharma, a real estate agent who lived on the third floor of the same multi-storey building in Sector 21C where the victim resided with his family.
The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, had returned from Singapore two days ago to attend a family wedding and celebrate Deepavali with his family.

According to the complaint filed by his 19-year-old son, Shaurya, the accused rang the doorbell of their flat around 8.30 p.m. and asked Mr. Dhankhar, who had returned from the gym a few minutes earlier, to come downstairs and move his car. Shaurya also accompanied his father to the parking area.

An argument reportedly broke out between the two men, following which Mr. Sharma allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired several rounds at Mr. Dhankhar. He also fired at Shaurya, who managed to escape unhurt by taking cover behind parked cars. The accused then fled the spot in his vehicle. Mr. Dhankhar succumbed to his bullet injuries.

“About 14-15 rounds were fired, of which eight or nine reportedly hit the victim. His son, who was present at the spot, escaped unhurt,” said Surajkund police station SHO Inspector Pahlad. The SHO said the two men had differences earlier as well and the accused allegedly used to create disturbances after consuming alcohol.

A case was registered at the Surajkund police station under charges of murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy. The accused was subsequently arrested by the Sector 30 Crime Branch team on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

articles.title: Strong earthquake with preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu

A strong earthquake shook central Japan early on Sunday (November 8, 2026), shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.
Japan’s Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.

A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.

Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.

The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m., was located about 40 kilometres below the earth’s surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.
The meteorological agency warned people to brace for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially the next two to three days.
“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.
He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.
The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.

Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes. Authorities frequently instruct people to stock up on bottled water, food and batteries, have plans ready to hide under tables and keep comfortable walking shoes at hand.

articles.title: Deportation of wanted Punjab gangster Afridi secured after 10-month international manhunt
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav said the Punjab government had announced a reward of ₹5 lakh for information leading to his arrest
Punjab Police, with the support of central agencies, has secured the deportation of wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia following a 10-month international manhunt.
Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said the Punjab government had announced a reward of ₹5 lakh for information leading to his arrest.

"In a major breakthrough, Anti-Gangster Task Force (#AGTF) Punjab, in coordination with the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (#OFTEC) of Counter Intelligence, Punjab with the support of central agencies, secures the deportation of Gurwinder alias Afridi, a key kingpin of the Doni Bal-Prabh Dassuwal gang, from Ethiopia following a 10-month-long international manhunt under Operation SHAHID," the DGP said in a post on X.
He said preliminary investigation reveals that the accused was allegedly directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and organised criminal activities in Punjab from abroad.

The operation involved sustained intelligence gathering, surveillance and tracking across multiple countries in Asia, South America and Africa, in close coordination with national and international agencies, DGP said.
"We thank the Ministry of External Affairs and all other central agencies as part of this international cooperation," he said.
He added that Punjab Police remains committed to dismantling gangster networks, preventing organised crime and ensuring peace and security across the State.

The operation involved sustained intelligence gathering, surveillance and tracking across multiple countries in Asia, South America and Africa, in close coordination with national and international agencies, DGP said.

"We thank the Ministry of External Affairs and all other central agencies as part of this international cooperation," he said.

articles.title: Kerala Water Authority intensifies action against encroachments on Pipeline Road
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Pipeline Road is important for the KWA as the transmission main carrying water from Aruvikkara to the capital city passes through it

The Kerala Water Authority (KWA) has kicked off a major drive to rid the Pipeline Road on the Peroorkada-Aruvikkara stretch of encroachments and unauthorised constructions. The water utility said on Saturday that it has intensified action against encroachers.

As part of the drive, illegal structures were removed at the Vazhayila junction on Friday. The effort will continue in the weeks ahead, the KWA said on Saturday. “These measures are being taken to protect the Pipeline Road and the allied KWA assets and to ensure access for carrying out repairs and maintenance works,” the KWA said.
The Pipeline Road is important for the KWA as the transmission main carrying water from Aruvikkara to the capital city passes through it.

The water utility has requested encroachers to vacate the premises voluntarily, so as to avoid action. KWA officials are also serving notices to encroachers under provisions of the KWA (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupation and Removal of Unauthorised Constructions) Regulations, 2014.

If the encroachers fail to vacate the premises within the timeframe stipulated in the notice, the Executive Engineer concerned will issue the final speaking order. Failure to vacate within the 30-day deadline prescribed in that order will attract eviction measures with the assistance of the police, according to KWA.

In August this year, the KWA had ordered that all permanent, semi-permanent and other encroachments be removed from the Pipeline Road in Kochi. The drive in Kochi was held as part of the preliminary measures for the laying of pipelines to the city from a proposed 190-mld water treatment plant.

articles.title: Revanth challenges KCR for debate on Kaleshwaram, El Niño and Godavari waters in the special Assembly session
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy alleged that the previous government had neglected drinking and irrigation water requirements in the region while prioritising the Kaleshwaram project over the Pranahita project

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy challenged BRS president and former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao to participate in a two-day discussion in the Assembly in December on the Kaleshwaram project, Godavari waters and the anticipated El Niño impact.

Interacting with progressive farmers and agricultural scientists after inaugurating the Mega Rythu Mela and Industrial Expo at Hakimpet village in Dudyala mandal of Vikarabad district, Mr. Reddy appealed to Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar to allow the discussion and said Mr. Rao and his family members should attend so that the facts surrounding the irrigation projects and their implementation could be brought out.

Accusing the previous BRS government of failing to complete even one major irrigation project in undivided Mahabubnagar district during its 10-year tenure, he said people had expected the completion of the Kalwakurthy, Bhima, Nettampadu, Koilsagar and Makthal-Narayanpet-Kodangal lift irrigation projects. Had the Congress formed the government in 2014, these projects would have been completed and the aspirations of the region’s people fulfilled, he claimed.

Mr. Reddy alleged that the previous government had neglected drinking and irrigation water requirements in the region while prioritising the Kaleshwaram project over the Pranahita project, despite the Centre’s offer to accord national project status to the latter.

The Chief Minister said then Irrigation Minister T Harish Rao was reluctant to discuss Medigadda while he claimed himself as ‘Kaleshwar Rao’ claiming himself as the man behind its completion. “After it collapsed he is not even mentioning Medigadda,” charged Mr. Reddy
He also accused Mr. Rao of approaching Prime Minister Narendra Modi to delay the CBI investigation ordered by the State government into the alleged irregularities.

Responding to criticism over the functioning of the Kaleshwaram project and demands to operate the Kannnepalli pump houses, the Chief Minister questioned the purpose of constructing Medigadda if water could be lifted through the pumps independently.
Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy interacting with farmers and officials at the Rythu Mela in Hakimpet village in Vikarabad districct on November 7, 2026.

Mr. Reddy also accused the previous government of obstructing development in Kodangal, but the Congress government had expedited the Makthal-Narayanpet lift irrigation project with farmers affected by land acquisition being paid compensation of ₹20 lakh an acre, against less than ₹2 lakh offered by Mr. Rao government.

Drawing a comparison with the development of industrial corridors between Delhi and Noida and Mumbai and Pune, he said the government would develop the Kodangal stretch from Hyderabad airport on similar models.

articles.title: Bombay High Court allows BNS Section 75 charge where complainant identifies as woman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The judge rejected the argument that Section 75 cannot apply because the complainant is a transgender and not a woman

The Bombay High Court has refused to discharge Vishal Ingle and held that Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita can apply when the complainant is a transgender who identifies as a woman. Justice Mehroz Pathan passed the order on November 3.

The judge rejected the argument that Section 75 cannot apply because the complainant is a transgender and not a woman. The judge said the complainant identifies as a woman and has taken medicines for hormone changes.

The FIR contains allegations against the applicant of outraging the modesty of the complainant. The complainant identifies as a woman and has undergone treatment for hormone changes. The judge said the FIR contains allegations against the applicant of outraging the modesty of the complainant, who identifies as a woman after hormone therapy. The judge said Section 75 appears to be made out.
The judge said allegations of assault and outraging the modesty of a woman can be sustained when the victim is a transgender who identifies as a woman.
Mr. Ingle served as an Agniveer. The police registered an offence under Section 75 and Section 296 of the BNS and under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

The judge rejected the argument that Section 18(D) of the Act of 2019 is not made out because the complainant did not have a certificate of identity under the Act. The judge said Section 2(k) shows a person may identify as a transgender even without a certificate of identity. Section 5 provides a route to apply to the District Magistrate for a certificate.

The complainant received a certificate of identity on February 12, 2026. The assault took place on October 28, 2025 and October 30, 2025. The judge said the absence of a certificate at the time of the offence does not bar use of the Act of 2019. The judge said the FIR shows Section 18(D) was invoked and the allegations attract the provisions invoked against the applicant.

articles.title: PM Modi to celebrate Deepavali with forces in Bastar that was once den of Maoists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister said Bastar is an area where Maoism once held sway but now, development is flourishing

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will celebrate Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026) along with security personnel in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, which was freed from the clutches of Maoists after several decades.
"Heading to Bastar to celebrate Diwali with our brave security forces," Mr. Modi said in a post on 'X'.
The Prime Minister said Bastar is an area where Maoism once held sway but now, development is flourishing.
"I am going to salute our brave security personnel for their sacrifices, selfless service and unwavering devotion to the nation," he said.
The Central Armed Police Forces and personnel of the Chhattisgarh Police have been deployed in Bastar. They were deeply involved in the anti-Maoist operations.
On March 31 this year, the government had announced that the country was free from the menace of Maoism after the elimination of many leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.

While conveying Deepavali greetings on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the Prime Minister said that like the previous year, this time also, he would celebrate the festival along with the brave soldiers of the country.
In a video message posted on his social media handles, Mr. Modi had said that like everyone, he will also celebrate Deepavali with great enthusiasm.
"My heartiest greetings to all of you for Deepavali. I wish for peace, prosperity and happiness for all of you in the coming days. I also celebrate Deepavali like you with great enthusiasm," he said.
The Prime Minister said everyone knows that every year he celebrates Deepavali with the brave soldiers of the country.

However, the ‘bluenami’, as it is being called for the Democratic Party’s official colour, is also being studied in South Block for a different reason — for the number of Indian-Americans elected, belonging largely to the Democratic Party in opposition, who are less reticent about criticising the Indian government on issues like civil rights and democratic freedoms.

fullParagraphs: Andhra Pradesh swung from drought to deluge, with two back-to-back cyclones causing an estimated ₹6,500 cr. in damage and leaving at least 17 dead; crops were flattened and coconut trees uprooted, with farmers in the Godavari belt facing at least two years of recovery

A ndhra Pradesh is witnessing two extremes this year: drought and deluge. During the initial monsoon months of June and July, the State declared drought in 388 of its 688 mandals across 28 districts. By the end of October, however, extremely heavy rainfall had battered many of these mandals, except those in Rayalaseema.

Between October 28 and November 3, Andhra Pradesh was hit by two back-to-back cyclones — Very Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Arnab’ and Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ — leaving the coastal districts in ruins.

With wind speeds reaching 140 kmph during Arnab and 110 kmph during Murasu, the two cyclones are estimated to have caused damage worth approximately ₹6,500 crore. They also left at least 17 people dead, uprooted hundreds of electricity poles and damaged roads across the State. Arnab wreaked havoc in the twin Godavari districts of East and West Godavari and in the north coastal region, including Visakhapatnam.

The destruction was immense, with thousands of coconut trees uprooted and paddy, cotton and chilli crops flattened in West Godavari, East Godavari, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Bapatla, Guntur and Palnadu districts. Visakhapatnam, Eluru and East Godavari recorded extremely heavy rainfall of around 260 mm.

Coconut growers in the Godavari belt say it may at least take two years for them to recover the losses. While experts debate whether climate change played a role in these weather events, farmers and fishermen continue to bear the brunt of every disaster.
A similar situation last occurred in 2013, when cyclones Helen and Lehar battered the Andhra Pradesh coast. Before that, the State witnessed similar events in 1987 and 1976.

Mr. Trump on Saturday (November 7, 2026) also ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats for “extortion at the highest level.”
“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” he wrote, adding that he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act.”
Denying that anyone in his administration had committed impeachable offenses, Trump called for prison time for “these EXTORTIONISTS.”

articles.title: Strong earthquake shakes central Japan, shattering store windows, injuring at least 22
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m., was located about 40 kilometres below the earth’s surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions

A strong earthquake shook central Japan early on Sunday (November 8, 2026), shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.
Japan’s Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.

A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.

Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.

The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m., was located about 40 kilometres below the earth’s surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.
The meteorological agency warned people to brace for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially the next two to three days.
“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.
He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.
The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.

Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes. Authorities frequently instruct people to stock up on bottled water, food and batteries, have plans ready to hide under tables and keep comfortable walking shoes at hand.

articles.title: Body of Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota brought to Mansa for last rites
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13
The mortal remains of s lain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder last month triggered protests and a political row, were brought to his native place here on Sunday for last rites.
Following a post-mortem at PGIMER in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026), Jhota's body was taken to his native place, where last rites would be conducted.

Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.
A large number of people turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.
On Saturday (November 7, 2026), a member of the joint action committee had said Jhota's cremation would take place at his native place in Mansa on Sunday.
The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota's murder.
The cremation will be held at Jhota's fields on Chakerian Road in Mansa. Jhota's father, Bhim Singh, on Saturday (November 7, 2026) called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse.

"We will take the body to our residence first and thereafter, between 12 and 1 pm, Jhota will be cremated on Diwali Day," said Singh while speaking to reporters in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Jhota's body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday, after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), Jhota's father said he would go on a fast demanding the immediate transfer of Mansa Senior Superintendent of Police Vaibhav Chaudhary.

articles.title: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the Election Commission of India

The Congress party's receipts from donations above ₹20,000 plunged nearly 75% to ₹130.69 crore in 2025-26, the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows.
The party had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission.
A comparison with the preceding 12 financial years shows that the last steeper fall was in 2015-16, when Congress' disclosed donations dropped roughly 86% from ₹141.46 crore the previous year.

The latest decline follows two years of higher collections. Congress received ₹281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to ₹517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held.

BJP received ₹6,074.02 crore in donations exceeding ₹20,000 in 2024-25, nearly 12 times Congress's collection. BJP's corresponding figure for 2025-26 is not available as the party's contribution report has not been made public by the ECI yet.

articles.title: Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Hari Boxer detained in U.S., extradition process underway
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Rajasthan Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) secured the detention through sustained coordination with international agencies, including the CBI and Interpol, police said

Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Harichand Jat alias Hari Boxer has been detained in the U.S. by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and efforts are underway to bring him to India, Rajasthan Police said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The Rajasthan Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) secured the detention through sustained coordination with international agencies, including the CBI and Interpol, police said.

Hari Boxer (40), a resident of Chatarpura village in Kotputli-Behror district of Rajasthan, was allegedly operating criminal activities in India from abroad and played a key role in supplying weapons to the Lawrence Bishnoi-Rohit Godara gang.
He was involved in extortion threats and firing incidents in Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, including Mumbai and Pune, AGTF ADG Dinesh MN said.
The accused allegedly threatened wealthy businessmen through WhatsApp and Signal-based VoIP calls and resorted to firing at individuals or their family members if extortion demands were not met.

He was also wanted in connection with several firing incidents, including the shooting outside Bollywood director Rohit Shetty's Mumbai residence, following which he allegedly claimed responsibility through a social media post.
More than 22 cases, including attempts to murder, extortion, Arms Act violations and organised crime, are registered against him in various police stations in Rajasthan.

Hari Boxer allegedly fled India in April 2023 using his own passport and travelled through Dubai, the Dominican Republic and Guyana before reaching the U.S. through Mexico via an illegal migration route, police said.
A Red Corner Notice was issued against him through Interpol on November 14, 2024, following coordination with the CBI.

AGTF subsequently shared intelligence and technical inputs with international agencies, including nine Interpol notices to the US between December 2024 and July 2026. A provisional arrest request, updated dossier and fingerprints were also forwarded, police said.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh pays tributes to brave soldiers at Sherethang in Sikkim
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday (November 8, 2026) visited Sherethang near Nathu La in Sikkim, where he paid homage to brave soldiers at a war memorial.

He was received at Sherethang by Gangtok District Collector Rohan Agawane, Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Tsering Namgyal Gyatso and Home Department's Joint Secretary John Gurung along with senior army officials.

Mr. Singh paid homage at the Sherethang War Memorial in East Sikkim, honouring the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation and paid tribute to their courage and valour in safeguarding the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, officials said.
The Minister interacted with defence personnel deployed in the region and hailed their dedication and service in protecting the country's borders under challenging conditions, they said.
Mr. Singh also visited Baba Harbhajan Singh Mandir and paid his respects at the revered shrine, which holds immense significance among army personnel.

fullParagraphs: While headlines scream Ossoff looks more presidential after his Senate win, he remains focused on his State while attacking Donald Trump and his family

There is something of an investigative journalist in Jon Ossoff, who served as managing director and chief executive officer of Insight: The World Investigates, a London-based investigative television production company. During his Senate campaign as Democratic candidate in Georgia and even before, he had been mounting a blistering campaign against corruption. It resonated with the voters struggling with rising food prices and unaffordable fuel.

Mr. Ossoff won the November 3 election against Republican Mike Collins, becoming the only incumbent Senate Democrat to defend a seat in a State President Donald Trump carried in 2024. Ever since his win in the 2021 Senate race in Georgia, the charismatic Mr. Ossoff has been making the lists of possible candidates for the Democratic ticket in the 2028 Presidential election. But, like Barack Obama before his 2004 Senate win and scores of others before him, Mr. Ossoff, now 39, who in 2021 became the youngest U.S. Senator since 1980, has been vehemently denying any such aspiration. The media, however, has been quick in spotting in him similarities with Mr. Obama, especially the former President’s speech delivery.

articles.title: Kremlin hopes U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.
But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbour, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

“There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon,” Mr. Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11) involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
He also praised the “successful humanitarian peace-building efforts” by first lady Melania Trump, adding that “we hope that all of this will continue.”
Last week's limited ceasefire around the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered with her help, allowed for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some residents.
Mr. Peskov shrugged off a question from reporters on whether the new Congress would challenge Mr. Trump's stance on Russia and Ukraine. He called it an “internal matter” for the U.S.
In recent months, Mr. Trump's actions appeared to favour Moscow

Last month, he struck a diesel fuel import deal with Russia in a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on the Kremlin, to the dismay of Ukraine and its European allies. He also claimed that Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries caused a spike in diesel prices in the U.S. He urged Kyiv to halt the strikes, even though rising global energy prices were largely driven by the Iran war.

Mr. Trump also issued an executive order to put on hold sweeping new sanctions that clamped down on the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the national interest. Lawmakers from both parties blasted Mr. Trump's move as benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.

But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbour, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

“There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon,” Mr. Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11) involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

He also praised the “successful humanitarian peace-building efforts” by first lady Melania Trump, adding that “we hope that all of this will continue.”

Last week's limited ceasefire around the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered with her help, allowed for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some residents.

Mr. Peskov shrugged off a question from reporters on whether the new Congress would challenge Mr. Trump's stance on Russia and Ukraine. He called it an “internal matter” for the U.S.

In recent months, Mr. Trump's actions appeared to favour Moscow

Last month, he struck a diesel fuel import deal with Russia in a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on the Kremlin, to the dismay of Ukraine and its European allies. He also claimed that Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries caused a spike in diesel prices in the U.S. He urged Kyiv to halt the strikes, even though rising global energy prices were largely driven by the Iran war.

Mr. Trump also issued an executive order to put on hold sweeping new sanctions that clamped down on the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the national interest. Lawmakers from both parties blasted Mr. Trump's move as benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins

New Zealanders will wait for weeks to discover who will lead the country after Saturday's (November 7, 2026) election failed to deliver a decisive win for the right or the left, leaving fraught negotiations for a wafer-thin governing majority the only apparent path to victory for either side.

The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon's centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins, as voters threw more support behind minor parties on the ideological flanks than before.
On Saturday's (November 7) numbers, minor parties would enter negotiations for a governing deal with leverage to extract deeper policy concessions from a weakened National or Labour.

The near-deadlock was partly produced because voters, apparently weary of New Zealand's economic woes and apathetic about both Luxon and Hipkins, chose to propel a new entrant group to Parliament for the first time in years.
Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Ms. Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government.

Ms. Wong's pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering had on Saturday's (November 7) results secured seven seats for Opportunity — enough to frustrate both left and right in a simple path to power.

articles.title: Vijayan demands withdrawal of circular allowing colleges to increase seats without Keralam Govt nod
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CPI(M) veteran said a September 11 circular issued by the Higher Education Department had made prior government approval mandatory for introducing new courses and increasing seats in government, aided and autonomous colleges

LoP in the Keralam Assembly Pinarayi Vijayan on Sunday (November 8, 2026) alleged that the State government's move to allow autonomous aided and self-financing colleges to increase seats without prior approval would lead to the commercialisation of education.
Demanding the immediate withdrawal of the government circular permitting the move, Mr. Vijayan said the decision had been taken under pressure from the managements of private colleges.

The CPI(M) veteran said a September 11 circular issued by the Higher Education Department had made prior government approval mandatory for introducing new courses and increasing seats in government, aided and autonomous colleges.

He contended that the government had now relaxed the norms, despite the existing provision ensuring strict scrutiny and regulation at the government level, by "succumbing to the misguided pressures of the managements".

"The current provision that no government no-objection certificate (NOC) is required for starting unaided courses and increasing seats in autonomous aided and self-financing colleges is shocking," the former CM said.

He said allowing colleges to increase seats at their discretion, without assessing the necessity and disregarding existing regulatory mechanisms, would pave the way for the commercialisation of education.
"This ill-conceived collusion is taking place despite the assurances given before the Supreme Court that self-financing courses would not be allowed in aided colleges on a large scale," he contended.
Mr. Vijayan questioned whose interests the government was protecting by granting such sweeping concessions immediately after representatives of college managements met the Higher Education Minister.

He alleged that doing away with annual inspections and allowing colleges to inform the government about seat increases only after the admission process was over amounted to "a clear conspiracy to sell seats by taking bribes by subverting the provisions of merit and reservation".
He claimed that such measures would effectively dismantle government regulation and undermine the educational rights of ordinary people, particularly the poor.

articles.title: Thane court sentences man to 20 years rigorous imprisonment for raping minor on promise of marriage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four prosecution witnesses, including the survivor, her mother and neighbour, were examined to prove the charges against the accused
A special court in Maharashtra's Thane district has sentenced a 35-year-old man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for repeatedly raping a minor girl after promising to marry her.

Additional Sessions Judge Premal S. Vithalani convicted the accused, Shrinivas Ashok Yelgonda, a painter, under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, noting that while the absence of violence and premeditation was a mitigating factor, the law mandated a minimum 20-year term.

According to the prosecution, the victim resided in the same housing society in Diva East as the accused, and the two became acquainted in June 2020 and subsequently developed a romantic relationship through phone chats.

Special public prosecutor Rekha Hiwrale stated that the accused first sexually assaulted the minor in November 2020 inside a neighbour's vacant apartment by promising to marry her, and later raped her on several occasions. The abuse came to light in February 2022 when a dispute arose after the accused reneged on his promise to marry her.
Four prosecution witnesses, including the survivor, her mother and neighbour, were examined to prove the charges against the accused.

The defence argued that there was an unexplained delay in registering the FIR in 2022, and that exact dates of the recurring assaults were missing. However, relying on the survivor's birth certificate and school leaving certificate, the court verified that she was a "child" under 18 years of age during the major part of the abuse timeline, rendering her legal consent immaterial.

"The evidence on record clearly establishes that the victim was under the bona fide impression that the accused would solemnise marriage with her, which led her to keep the relationship and the repeated physical intimacies concealed from her parents," the judge observed.
The subsequent deliberation by the family before approaching the police is both natural and understandable given the social stigma, honour, and future of an unmarried girl, the court said.
It also noted that there was no evidence of brutal force, physical injury or premeditated sexual predation.

"While the victim's minority under the age of 18 renders her consent legally ineffective and makes the conviction unavoidable, the romantic backdrop remains a vital and compelling mitigating factor in sentencing," it stated.

articles.title: Dangerous harmonies: Is there a hidden villain in India’s devastating electrical fires?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electrical causes are predominating in India’s recent fire incidents; while codes and guidelines are covering these increasingly, there are still major gaps such as taking into account harmonic currents put into the system by state-of-the-art electronics equipment
Just after 3.48 a.m. on May 3, 2026, fire ripped through a four-storey building in Vivek Vihar, East Delhi, killing nine. The suspected origin was an AC blast or short circuit.

Ten newborns died in an overcrowded Jhansi NICU in November 2024, a unit meant for 18 babies packed with 55. Three newborns in Amravati this August, dead not from flame but from smoke inhalation, even though the fire itself was out within 30 minutes. One newborn in Chhindwara two days before that. Ten patients at Cuttack’s SCB Medical College this March, when a short circuit in a trauma-ICU air-conditioner ignited an oxygen-rich ward at 3 a.m.

Fire accidents in India used to happen in industrial units, firecracker factories and mass gatherings. No more. The more devastating ones happen right in our neighbourhoods, in hospitals and high-rises. They are almost always triggered by electrical fires.

Delhi Fire Service attributes over 80% of the capital’s fires to electrical faults. Mumbai Fire Brigade, analysing 26,855 incidents over five years, attributes nearly three in four to the same cause. New Delhi alone saw a 37% rise in residential fires this year over last, with roughly 70% traced to short-circuiting, faulty wiring, overheating, and overloaded circuits. The National Crime Records Bureau recorded 7,566 fire accidents and 7,435 deaths in 2022, with short circuit consistently among the largest single causes.

Indian electricity demand hit 256.11 GW on April 25 this year, against air temperatures of 47 degrees, roughly double the early-2010s peak. A/Cs draw about 50 GW at peak. And projections place the A/C load at 180 GW in another 10 years. Indians bought more than 15 million air-conditioners in 2025 alone, and the International Energy Agency expects the installed base to climb from 93 million units in 2024 to 240 million by 2030.

Air-conditioners draw heavy current that electrical systems in older buildings are unable to withstand, resulting in the wiring burning up. What’s called an A/C blast is the overworked compressor in the refrigeration exploding due to sheer heat caused by overworking. Investigation into these fires has been hampered by shortage of certified fire forensic investigators. Too often, the causes are dismissed as blasts or short circuits. Root cause analysis and systemic remedies are rarely formulated.

An electrical circuit has three parts. The load is whatever draws current. It could be just a light or an air-conditioner. New Delhi alone saw a 37% rise in residential fires this year over last, with roughly 70% traced to short-circuiting, faulty wiring, overheating, and overloaded circuits. Indians bought more than 15 million air-conditioners in 2025 alone, and the International Energy Agency expects the installed base to climb from 93 million units in 2024 to 240 million by 2030.

Air-conditioners draw heavy current that electrical systems in older buildings are unable to withstand, resulting in the wiring burning up. What’s called an A/C blast is the overworked compressor in the refrigeration exploding due to sheer heat caused by overworking. Investigation into these fires has been hampered by shortage of certified fire forensic investigators. Too often, the causes are dismissed as blasts or short circuits. A loose joint nearby could make an overheated neutral become an ignition source ripping up ordinary insulation.

articles.title: Crew member missing as Indonesian water-bombing helicopter crashes
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A helicopter battling Indonesian wildfires crashed into a river on Sunday as it scooped water, an official told AFP , with two crew members rescued and one still missing.

The crash in Borneo Island's South Kalimantan province was the second in days involving a firefighting helicopter, after a military chopper plunged into the waters off Borneo on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), killing three people.

Two Australian nationals had survived Sunday's (November 8, 2026) incident and were "safe", said Berton Panjaitan, a spokesman for the national disaster mitigation agency, while the third member of the crew, an Indonesian, remained unaccounted for.
Dramatic video footage showed the firefighting helicopter being slowly dragged downward after filling its bucket from the Barito River, eventually plunging nose-first into the water.

The Southeast Asian archipelago has for months been struggling to control blazes that have burned through large swathes of Sumatra, Borneo and Papua islands, causing choking haze that drifted to neighbouring Malaysia, East Timor and Singapore.
"This incident occurred while the air fleet was conducting a water-bombing operation," spokesman Berton said of Sunday's crash.
"In footage captured by an amateur video, the helicopter appears to lose control while manoeuvring after scooping up water from the river with a bambi bucket."
The Eurocopter EC225LP Super Puma belonged to a company the disaster mitigation agency had contracted for water-bombing operations, he added.
On Wednesday, a helicopter carrying eight people crashed during a mission to fight fires in Tanjung Puting National Park, home to animals including critically endangered Bornean orangutans.
The incident occurred while the aircraft was scooping seawater for water bombing, according to an army statement, which added that the accident's cause was under investigation.

articles.title: Taiwan detains Communist Party leader over alleged Chinese sponsorship in election
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Authorities in Taiwan detained the leader of the island's Taiwan People's Communist Party, accusing him of running as a candidate for borough chief under the direction and sponsorship of China's Communist Party, local media reported on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Taiwan is set to hold elections for mayors and local area chiefs on November 28. While the races focus more on livelihood issues, the results could be a good indicator of the popularity of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party under the leadership of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te ahead of the presidential election in 2028.

According to Taiwan's Central News Agency, prosecutors said in a statement on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that an initial investigation showed Taiwan People's Communist Party chair Lin Te-wang also had directed another party member to run as a candidate for chief in another borough.
Prosecutors also alleged that Mr. Lin sought to buy votes by repeatedly recruiting voters to travel to mainland China, where they received hospitality, the report said.

While Mr. Lin's party is not influential on the democratic island, it was not his first legal trouble over his alleged links with China. He and another party leader had faced charges of Chinese infiltration and attempting to influence elections but were found not guilty in 2025, the Taipei Times reported.
Taiwan's Central News Agency said the prosecutors had received intelligence about foreign interference in the election and summoned 14 people and nine witnesses.

After questioning, the government lawyers strongly suspected that Lin and the other party member had committed a crime and were concerned the pair could flee or destroy evidence, so they filed applications to the local courts to detain them and bar them from being visited by others, it said.

The courts ruled in the prosecutors' favour for Lin but released the other member on a 50,000-Taiwan-dollar ($1,525) bail, the news agency said. The other people summoned were released during the investigation, it added.
China's Taiwan Affairs Office has not immediately commented.
Beijing views Taiwan as a breakaway province to be retaken by force if necessary, and claims of China's meddling are common in Taiwanese elections.

Authorities in Taiwan detained the leader of the island's Taiwan People's Communist Party, accusing him of running as a candidate for borough chief under the direction and sponsorship of China's Communist Party, local media reported on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Taiwan is set to hold elections for mayors and local area chiefs on November 28. While the races focus more on livelihood issues, the results could be a good indicator of the popularity of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party under the leadership of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te ahead of the presidential election in 2028.

According to Taiwan's Central News Agency, prosecutors said in a statement on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that an initial investigation showed Taiwan People's Communist Party chair Lin Te-wang also had directed another party member to run as a candidate for chief in another borough.

Prosecutors also alleged that Mr. Lin sought to buy votes by repeatedly recruiting voters to travel to mainland China, where they received hospitality, the report said.

While Mr. Lin's party is not influential on the democratic island, it was not his first legal trouble over his alleged links with China. He and another party leader had faced charges of Chinese infiltration and attempting to influence elections but were found not guilty in 2025, the Taipei Times reported.

Taiwan's Central News Agency said the prosecutors had received intelligence about foreign interference in the election and summoned 14 people and nine witnesses.

After questioning, the government lawyers strongly suspected that Lin and the other party member had committed a crime and were concerned the pair could flee or destroy evidence, so they filed applications to the local courts to detain them and bar them from being visited by others, it said.

The courts ruled in the prosecutors' favour for Lin but released the other member on a 50,000-Taiwan-dollar ($1,525) bail, the news agency said. The other people summoned were released during the investigation, it added.

China's Taiwan Affairs Office has not immediately commented.

Beijing views Taiwan as a breakaway province to be retaken by force if necessary, and claims of China's meddling are common in Taiwanese elections.

articles.title: Bangladesh Law Minister calls Hasina ‘convicted criminal’, says extradition request sent to India
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Indian govt previously acknowledged receiving Bangladesh's extradition requests for Ms. Hasina but has not announced any decision on handing her over

Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Sunday (November 8, 2026) described ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as a "convicted criminal" and said Dhaka has requested India to extradite her, according to local media reports.

Responding to questions from journalists after inaugurating a training workshop in Dhaka, Mr. Asaduzzaman said the government was taking all necessary legal steps to bring Ms. Hasina back from India and would follow due process.
"To me, she is a criminal. A criminal convicted by our tribunal. To us, this is her identity," he said, according to a report on bdnews24 website.
Asked about bringing Ms. Hasina back to Bangladesh, the Law Minister said the government would act in accordance with the law and would not be guided by emotion.

"Although the Law Ministry is not directly involved in this matter, the Ministry of Home Affairs is concerned, as it relates to the extradition treaty with India. The matter will be dealt with in accordance with the law, leaving no room for emotions. We have requested her repatriation under the treaty and through due process," Mr. Asaduzzaman was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency.
Bdnews24 also quoted Mr. Asaduzzaman as saying: "That is a matter for the Indian government. We have made requests to them under the extradition treaty."
"If they hand her over to us, we will hand her over in the due process, as required under the law," he added.

India has previously acknowledged receiving Bangladesh's extradition requests for Ms. Hasina but has not announced any decision on handing her over. The Ministry of External Affairs has said the requests are being examined as part of its established processes.
Ms. Hasina fled Bangladesh for India on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising that ended her 15-year rule. An interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus subsequently took charge.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Sheikh Hasina speaks to The Hindu : Bangladesh protests, India and her return plans

Although the police initially attempted to file a closure report citing an inability to identify the victim, a Special POCSO court judge rejected the move in February 2026 and ordered further investigation.

All the accused are currently lodged at the Puzhal Central Prison in Chennai.

During the ongoing investigation, accused driver Mr. Lazar was taken into one-day police custody for interrogation. Based on this inquiry, authorities identified a white car used in the crime and initiated subsequent action.

articles.title: Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota cremated in his native place Mansa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13

The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder 26 days ago triggered protests and a political row, were consigned to flames at his native place here on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
A large number of people had turned up when last rites were held after his body was brought here from Chandigarh, following a post-mortem at PGIMER on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
The cremation was held at Jhota’s fields on Chakerian Road.

Jhota was shot dead on October 13 in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town while he was hosting a Facebook Live session. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.
A number of people also turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.
Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse, saying his son gave up his life fighting against the scourge.
“I thank the joint action committee which stood by us all through,” he told reporters on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota’s murder.

Jhota’s body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday (November 6, 2026), after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives on Wednesday (November 4).
The anti-drug activist’s family, along with the JAC, had been sitting on a protest in Mansa seeking justice for the slain activist.

The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder 26 days ago triggered protests and a political row, were consigned to flames at his native place here on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

A large number of people had turned up when last rites were held after his body was brought here from Chandigarh, following a post-mortem at PGIMER on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

The cremation was held at Jhota’s fields on Chakerian Road.

Jhota was shot dead on October 13 in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town while he was hosting a Facebook Live session. A number of people also turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.

Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse, saying his son gave up his life fighting against the scourge.

“I thank the joint action committee which stood by us all through,” he told reporters on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota’s murder.

Jhota’s body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday (November 6, 2026), after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives on Wednesday (November 4).

The anti-drug activist’s family, along with the JAC, had been sitting on a protest in Mansa seeking justice for the slain activist.

articles.title: No concrete proof yet from Indonesia for claim over rescued orangutans: Odisha Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory

Neither Indonesia nor any other country has so far provided documentary evidence to establish ownership of five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odisha two months ago, state Forest Minister Ganesh Ram Singh Khuntia said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Khuntia said all five orangutans were doing well , and expressed the State's desire to retain them at Nandankanan Zoological Park.
"All five baby orangutans are doing well and growing. No one should disturb them. We want them to stay in Odisha, and visitors will get an opportunity to see them at Nandankanan Zoo," he said.

The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory.

"The Indonesian government has raised its claim as a routine matter. We will seek evidence to establish that the orangutans originated from their country. If they provide the proof, the animals may be handed over to them," Mr. Khuntia said.
He added that the State government had submitted details of the rescued animals to the Centre for necessary action.
"Odisha has a conducive environment for orangutans. So, we want them to stay here," he said.
The five baby orangutans were rescued from Bichitrapur forest in Balasore district on September 8 and subsequently shifted to Nandankanan Zoo, where they have been kept in quarantine.
Officials said the animals were housed in a temperature-controlled room and were gradually acclimatising to the local environment.

The State government has made arrangements for their comfort and to help them overcome stress. The animals have displayed a range of emotions, from playful behaviour and brief mood swings to anxiously clinging to one another, they said.

articles.title: H.D. Kumaraswamy alleges Hassan DC retained her post by paying bribe to district in-charge Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal

Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy has alleged that the Hassan Deputy Commissioner retained her post by paying ₹75 lakh to Excise Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also the in-charge Minister of Hassan district.

Speaking to presspersons in Hassan after visiting the historic Hasanamba temple in Hassan on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Kumaraswamy read out excerpts from a written script of what he described as a WhatsApp conversation between an unidentified person and Shashikiran, the personal assistant to the Hassan Deputy Commissioner. He said he received the contents of the conversation from an official who met him the previous night.

According to Mr. Kumaraswamy, the conversation was about seeking permission for three stone crushers. The personal assistant allegedly demanded ₹60 lakh to get the clearance. As the person on the other end bargained, Mr. Shashikiran is said to have listed the people with whom the amount had to be shared.

Mr. Kumaraswamy said the conversation also mentioned that Mr. Shivalinge Gowda wanted to transfer the incumbent Deputy Commissioner from Hassan. However, she allegedly managed to convince the Minister by paying ₹75 lakh through Arsikere Tahsildar Santosh.
The script of the purported conversation was also distributed to journalists. Mr. Kumaraswamy said it also referred to the Hassan MP and several officials of the district.
He demanded an investigation into the allegations and urged the police to seize the mobile phone from the person concerned for further examination.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who also visited the temple the same day, said the Deputy Commissioner had been doing a good job. “However, allegations are being made against her because she did not yield to their demands,” he said.

Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal. “I have not done anything wrong, I am not doing anything wrong, and I will never do anything wrong,” she said.

Ms. Kumari said that if any wrong message had been sent by her personal assistant or anyone in his section, proper action would be taken. She condemned the circulation of “false and baseless information”. “Let there be an inquiry. Those who have erred should face action,” she said.
She said a complaint would be filed with the cyber police, as spreading false information was a crime. “We will bring out the truth,” she added.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Guards did not specify the names or nationality of the tankers

Three oil tankers caught fire on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran regularly targets ships that transit without its authorisation, the Revolutionary Guards said in a statement.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

“Since the early hours of this morning, three non-compliant tankers have exploded and caught fire while they were sailing in the illegal channel in the Strait of Hormuz,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement.
The Guards did not specify the names or nationality of the tankers.
Also on Sunday, British maritime agency UKMTO reported that a tanker had caught fire in the strait — off the coast of Khasab, Oman — a day earlier.

“Military authorities reported the tanker is on fire which has resulted in the evacuation of the crew,” the agency said in a statement, also reporting another tanker struck by an “unknown projectile” on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Emirati state media said on Sunday that 22 people had been rescued from a burning vessel in the Gulf of Oman and were in stable condition. AFP was unable to confirm if the various reports referenced the same incidents.
Tehran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying that ships have caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.

articles.title: U.S. launches task force to disrupt land transit routes into Iran
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The restrictions would expand on a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports during the two countries' eight-month war, in which Tehran has also restricted passage through the critical Strait of Hormuz trade route, choking global energy supplies
The U.S. military has announced it will create a 20-member task force to find ways to disrupt land routes into Iran that it says are used for shipments of weapons and illicit materials.

The restrictions would expand on a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports during the two countries' eight-month war, in which Tehran has also restricted passage through the critical Strait of Hormuz trade route, choking global energy supplies.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Seventeen people, including two police officers and the gunman, were wounded in the attack, authorities said

Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday (November 8, 2026) ‌and police bolstered security after six people were killed in a mass ​shooting in Krakow that authorities said was likely inspired by far-right ideology.

Saturday’s ⁠(November 7) attack in the city’s historic main square shocked a country that has prided itself on being safer than many of its Western European neighbours, deepening public concern following a string of school stabbings ‌in October that officials linked to extremist content online.
Seventeen people, including two police officers and the gunman, were wounded in the attack, authorities said.
The ‌24-year-old suspect’s parents and sister were later found dead at their home, and ‌he ⁠remained in hospital in a critical condition, police and a local official ⁠said.

In Krakow, the old town’s main market square and the surrounding streets remained closed, with police allowing only essential workers to pass. Many nearby cafes were closed and flags at the ​city hall were at half-mast. Mourners ‌placed candles in several locations in the area.
The traditional trumpet call from St Mary’s church on the square was suspended for 12 hours to commemorate the dead, the first time this has happened since 1939, state news agency PAP reported.

In the capital, ‌Warsaw, police said on Saturday (November 7) they were strengthening security measures in busy ​areas popular with tourists. Barriers were installed on streets leading onto the Krakowskie Przedmiescie street in the historic heart of the capital.
In the suspect’s home ⁠town, Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, about 200 km (124 miles) north of Krakow, police said they had found the bodies of his parents and sister and that investigations were ongoing.

“Yesterday, before 22:00, we ‌discovered the bodies of three individuals — a 53-year-old man and two women, aged 52 and 21 — in an apartment located in a residential building in the centre of Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski,” police wrote on X.
Maria, a 20-year-old Warsaw cafe employee, said she “almost burst into tears” when she heard about the attack in Krakow.
