articles.title: PM Modi desperate, 'jhola-picking-up time' fast approaching: Congress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the Prime Minister has not spared the nation even on Deepavali day his "trademark abuse"

The Congress on Sunday (November 8, 2026) hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi after his "dimagi Naxals" (ideological supporters) jibe at political rivals, saying he is clearly distraught, disturbed and desperate, and his " jhola -picking-up time" is fast approaching.

The opposition party's dig came after Mr. Modi targeted political opponents, saying armed Maoists have been eliminated, but "dimagi Naxals" have infiltrated several political parties and organisations and are instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

"We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country," Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a CRPF camp in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with India's brave men and women in uniform.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the Prime Minister has not spared the nation even on Deepavali day his "trademark abuse". "He has once again spoken of what he calls 'dimagi naxals'. He has used a very solemn non-political occasion, donned the uniform of the security forces, and hurled invectives at his political rivals," Mr. Ramesh said on X.
This is a brazen assault on all institutional norms but when has that ever stopped this man, he asked.

It was on April 28, 2024 that he had said that those demanding a caste census were urban naxals, and later on April 30, 2025, he announced that a caste census will be carried out as part of Census 2027, Mr. Ramesh said.

Earlier, in September 2020, he had called those agitating against the three black farm laws as supporters of a naxal ideology, and later, on November 19, 2021, he withdrew those very laws, the Congress leader pointed out.
"The PM is clearly distraught, disturbed and desperate. Jhola-picking-up time is fast approaching," Mr. Ramesh said.
In his remarks in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, Mr. Modi said the government took decisions that "dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists".
The Maoist terror elimination was a victory of the country's right policies and strong political will, said Modi, dressed in a military-style camouflage uniform and a hat.

fullParagraphs: Incoming Democratic attorneys general could halt ⁠cooperation with federal immigration operations, fortify abortion access and file multistate challenges against the Trump administration's environmental and gun policies

Democrats flipped attorney general offices in five Republican-leaning states in the midterm elections, dealing a significant blow to the ‌conservative legal movement and erecting a new line of resistance against President Donald Trump's agenda.

The victories in ​Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Iowa and Kansas threaten to disrupt conservative legal strategy. Incoming Democratic attorneys general could halt ⁠cooperation with federal immigration operations, fortify abortion access and file multistate challenges against the Trump administration's environmental and gun policies.
“The Texas AG’s office has been operating as the private law firm of the MAGA movement," Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson said in an interview. “No more.”

The shift reflects broader ‌voter pushback in the midterms, in which Democrats made gains nationwide. But the practical fallout may be felt most immediately in State capitals, where attorneys general direct law enforcement priorities, issue legal guidance and challenge federal mandates.

"The ‌Republican state AG offices are the tip of the spear of the conservative legal movement," said Mike Davis, ‌an influential ⁠conservative lawyer. "Losing these offices is a major setback for key conservative causes."

Over the past decade, Republican attorneys general have advanced conservative causes by challenging federal regulations, restricting gender-affirming care, curbing diversity initiatives and ​expanding gun access.
The Texas office, in particular, served ‌as a command centre for conservative legal challenges, leveraging its resources and elite staff to sue Democratic administrations.

Mr. Johnson said he plans a review of initiatives launched by his predecessor, Ken Paxton, including legal actions targeting out-of-state abortion providers, claims linking over-the-counter medications to autism, and lawsuits challenging vaccine efficacy.
He’s also critical of the State’s current partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs ‌Enforcement (ICE) and plans to review whether it should continue.

“The Texas attorney general office was never conceived to ​be an extension of federal immigration enforcement,” he said. “And to the extent that they were detracting from the proper function of this office, we’re going to have a change of plans.”

articles.title: Assam OIL facility fire: death toll rises to four as another injured dies; four suspended
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident

The toll in the fire incident at an Oil India Ltd (OIL) facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district increased to four with another injured worker succumbing on Sunday (November 8, 2026), while the PSU has suspended all four of its personnel who were in charge of the site, officials said.
Three people who were also injured in the blaze on Friday (November 6, 2026) are undergoing treatment in a critical condition.
All the victims were employees of Spectron Engineering Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company engaged by OIL.
One person was killed in the fire on the day of the incident, while two died the next day.
A mechanical helper, Sailen Gogoi, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital here, died during the day, taking the toll to four, the official said.
A fire had broken out on November 6 after an explosion during maintenance work at OIL's intermediate tank farm (ITF) in Tengakhat, the public sector undertaking said in a statement.
An ITF is a facility where petroleum products are temporarily stored in tanks before being transferred for further processing or transportation.
Meanwhile, OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident, another official said.

The committee has put all four OIL employees who were in-charge of the ITF, including three officers, on suspension, he said. "They were placed under suspension until the investigation is over," the official added.
The PSU has announced an ex-gratia of ₹10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person.

articles.title: ‘Dimagi Naxals’ instigating people against Constitution: PM Modi as Maoists eliminated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Celebrating Diwali with CRPF personnel in Bastar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country must “identify and defeat” ideological supporters of Naxalism who have “infiltrated” parties and organisations

Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

“We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country,” Mr. Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with the men and women in uniform. The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.

“Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added. The government, he said, took decisions that “dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists”.

On Independence Day in August 2026, Mr. Modi had also referred to “dimagi Naxals”, saying the country had succeeded in removing armed Naxalism but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.

Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, Mr. Modi said it had not been easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 States were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill, thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, and there were around 2,000 Naxalite attacks annually, he said.

“This land had become soaked in the blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments. Between 2004 and 2013, more security personnel were killed every year than the number of Naxalites eliminated, he said.

“Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed. No country can function with such an approach towards its enemies... The lack of political will that the country faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” he said.

The morale of security forces began changing after 2014, Mr. Modi said, adding that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel lost his life while on duty over the past year. “This is a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will. This is a victory of your valour, courage and restraint,” he said.

articles.title: Delhi records ‘very poor’ air quality on Diwali with 376 AQI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 450, followed by RK Puram at 448, according to the Sameer app.
Delhi’s air quality was in the ‘very poor’ category on Sunday (November 8, 2026), but set to worsen after Diwali celebrations in the evening.
The average Air Quality Index (AQI) for the day settled at 376 in the ‘very poor’ category as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city and reduced visibility.
The air quality is forecast to turn ‘severe’ on Monday (November 9, 2026) following Diwali celebrations, combined with vehicular emissions, as well as the peak stubble-burning season.

Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Sunday (November 8, 2026), air quality was in the ‘severe’ category at 12 and in the ‘very poor’ category at 22. The worst AQI was recorded in Jahangirpuri at 463.

The city’s average AQI increased from 369 on Saturday to 376 on Sunday, remaining not far from the ‘severe’ threshold of 400. Several monitoring stations have already breached this mark, indicating deterioration in air quality across the capital.
According to the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) for Delhi, the air quality is likely to remain in the ‘severe’ category from November 9 for a few days.
ALSO WATCH Delhi air pollution: GRAP stage 3 kicks in, vehicle ban and school curbs announced

As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as ‘good’, 51 and 100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 as ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 as ‘poor’, 301 and 400 as ‘very poor’, and 401 and 500 as ‘severe’.

Weather and air quality experts have attributed the anticipated deterioration to unfavourable meteorological conditions, the onset of Deepavali-related celebrations and vehicular emissions, along with the peak period of stubble burning in neighbouring states.

Unfavourable meteorological conditions are further aggravating the situation. According to the EWS, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, coupled with an average wind speed of less than 10 kilometres per hour, is unfavourable for the effective dispersion of pollutants.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 08 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 450, followed by RK Puram at 448, according to the Sameer app.

Delhi’s air quality was in the ‘very poor’ category on Sunday (November 8, 2026), but set to worsen after Diwali celebrations in the evening.

The average Air Quality Index (AQI) for the day settled at 376 in the ‘very poor’ category as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city and reduced visibility.

The air quality is forecast to turn ‘severe’ on Monday (November 9, 2026) following Diwali celebrations, combined with vehicular emissions, as well as the peak stubble-burning season.

Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Sunday (November 8, 2026), air quality was in the ‘severe’ category at 12 and in the ‘very poor’ category at 22. The worst AQI was recorded in Jahangirpuri at 463.

The city’s average AQI increased from 369 on Saturday to 376 on Sunday, remaining not far from the ‘severe’ threshold of 400. Several monitoring stations have already breached this mark, indicating deterioration in air quality across the capital.

According to the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) for Delhi, the air quality is likely to remain in the ‘severe’ category from November 9 for a few days.

ALSO WATCH Delhi air pollution: GRAP stage 3 kicks in, vehicle ban and school curbs announced

As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as ‘good’, 51 and 100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 as ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 as ‘poor’, 301 and 400 as ‘very poor’, and 401 and 500 as ‘severe’.

Weather and air quality experts have attributed the anticipated deterioration to unfavourable meteorological conditions, the onset of Deepavali-related celebrations and vehicular emissions, along with the peak period of stubble burning in neighbouring states.

Unfavourable meteorological conditions are further aggravating the situation. According to the EWS, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, coupled with an average wind speed of less than 10 kilometres per hour, is unfavourable for the effective dispersion of pollutants.

articles.title: Revanth sets target of making one crore women millionaires by 2034
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Promises greater economic opportunities for SHG members; says women’s empowerment is central to his government’s policies

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy set a target of transforming one crore women into millionaires by 2034 by strengthening self-help groups (SHGs) and creating more opportunities for them in business and industry.

Interacting with women members of self-help groups at the Lagacharla Industrial Hub in Kodangal constituency on Sunday (November 8, 2026), he said nearly 70 lakh women were already members of SHGs and the government aimed to increase the membership to one crore by 2034 and make every member financially prosperous.

The Chief Minister, who celebrated his birthday with the women members of self-help groups, said he considered them his family and attributed his rise to the blessings and support of women. “I have received more from you than I ever asked for. I have nothing more to aspire for in life. My goal is to make one crore women millionaires,” he said.

Mr. Revanth Reddy said women were the backbone of families and that households prospered when women had control over financial decisions. His government was, therefore, making efforts to expand their role in economic activities and entrepreneurship.

He said women’s self-help groups had been entrusted with stitching school uniforms for students in government schools, while they were also being encouraged to operate petrol bunks, participate in solar power generation and run Indiramma canteens in the Secretariat and other government offices. Women were generating annual business worth ₹15 crore to ₹20 crore through some of these activities, he claimed.

The government had extended bank-linkage loans of ₹79,000 crore to women over the last 34 months, he said, complimenting Minister for Women and Child Welfare Danasari Anasuya (Seethakka) for her efforts in strengthening the SHG movement.

Referring to welfare measures, the Chief Minister said the government had sanctioned 4.5 lakh new pensions on Sunday (November 8), of which 3.5 lakh were for single women and widows. New pensions had also been sanctioned on a saturation basis for handloom and toddy-tapping workers, he added.

He said the Indiramma housing scheme and free electricity up to 200 units were providing support to women. Nearly 37 lakh women were travelling free on RTC buses every day, and the government was compensating the corporation for the scheme, helping it return to profitability.
Urging women to move beyond dependence on welfare schemes and become entrepreneurs and industrialists, he said the government would stand by them in their efforts to achieve economic independence.

He also called upon women to give priority to their children’s education, particularly higher education for girls. “The hardships you have faced should not be experienced by your children. Education alone can transform their lives,” he said, asking women to promise on his birthday that they would ensure higher education for their daughters.

articles.title: Israel Defence Minister says 'mission not complete' on Iran
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: "Concerning Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons — alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger," says Mr. Katz
Israel is not finished with Iran, its Defence Minister said Sunday (November 8, 2026), as he also warned Tehran's Lebanese ally Hezbollah to hold fire in any resumption of war.
Defence Minister Israel Katz renewed charges that Iran — attacked twice since last year in major Israeli-U.S. bombing campaigns — is pursuing nuclear weapons, a claim that Tehran denies.

"Concerning Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons — alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger," Mr. Katz said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is fighting for his political life, has repeatedly threatened new strikes against Iran in recent weeks.

But it remains unclear if he has the support of U.S. President Donald Trump, his close ally, who suffered a major rebuke from voters in elections on Tuesday (November 10), in part over anger against the war.

Israel's Channel 12 reported Friday that Mr. Netanyahu and the Mossad intelligence service attempted an operation against Iran on the eve of Israel's own October 27 election but that the United States found out and stopped it.
Mr. Netanyahu has ordered a multi-nation war since the unprecedented attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, by Hamas, the Palestinian militant group in Gaza backed by Iran's clerical state.

Israel has devastated Gaza and has invaded Lebanon, after Hezbollah fired on Israel in solidarity with Iran. Israel has also moved past a former ceasefire line to occupy part of historic adversary Syria after the fall in 2024 of longtime leader Bashar al-Assad.

"We will not withdraw from the security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, and if the terrorist organisation Hezbollah chooses to join Iran in an attack on Israel, it will suffer extremely severe blows," Mr. Katz said.
Mr. Netanyahu suffered losses in the October 27 election, with his rival Gadi Eisenkot tasked with forming a new government.

articles.title: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant relying on generators again after losing external power supply
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Zaporizhzhia, which produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel ‌cool, lost its off-site electricity supply after the Ferosplavna power line disconnected, the IAEA said

The Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine ​has lost its external electricity supply and is again ‌using backup generators for reactor cooling, the plant's ​management and the UN's nuclear watchdog said ⁠on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Zaporizhzhia, which produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel ‌cool, lost its off-site electricity supply after the Ferosplavna power line disconnected, the International Atomic ‌Energy Agency (IAEA) said.

"The cause and location ‌of ⁠the latest disconnection are not yet known," ⁠the IAEA said in an X post, adding that the plant currently has sufficient fuel reserves to operate a limited number ​of emergency diesel ‌generators for about two weeks.
The IAEA said on October 23 that the main Dniprovska power line remained unavailable.
In early September, a local ceasefire ‌brokered by the IAEA took effect to ​allow repairs to restore external power to Zaporizhzhia, which at that time had been ⁠without it since August 20.
Russia seized the nuclear plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, in the first ‌weeks of the war that began with Moscow's February 2022 invasion of its smaller neighbour.
Moscow and Kyiv have since regularly accused each other of military action that compromises nuclear safety.
The plant's Russian-installed management said the Ferosplavna line had been shut ‌down by "automatic protection", adding that radiation levels on the ​site and in the surveillance zone were normal.

"Staff at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant ⁠are monitoring all operational parameters of the equipment. All necessary ⁠measures to maintain the safe condition of the power units are being taken in ‌full," the plant's management said in a statement posted on the MAX messenger app.

The Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine ​has lost its external electricity supply and is again ‌using backup generators for reactor cooling, the plant's ​management and the UN's nuclear watchdog said ⁠on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Zaporizhzhia, which produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel ‌cool, lost its off-site electricity supply after the Ferosplavna power line disconnected, the International Atomic ‌Energy Agency (IAEA) said.

"The cause and location ‌of ⁠the latest disconnection are not yet known," ⁠the IAEA said in an X post, adding that the plant currently has sufficient fuel reserves to operate a limited number ​of emergency diesel ‌generators for about two weeks.

The IAEA said on October 23 that the main Dniprovska power line remained unavailable.

In early September, a local ceasefire ‌brokered by the IAEA took effect to ​allow repairs to restore external power to Zaporizhzhia, which at that time had been ⁠without it since August 20.

Russia seized the nuclear plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, in the first ‌weeks of the war that began with Moscow's February 2022 invasion of its smaller neighbour.

Moscow and Kyiv have since regularly accused each other of military action that compromises nuclear safety.

The plant's Russian-installed management said the Ferosplavna line had been shut ‌down by "automatic protection", adding that radiation levels on the ​site and in the surveillance zone were normal.

"Staff at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant ⁠are monitoring all operational parameters of the equipment. All necessary ⁠measures to maintain the safe condition of the power units are being taken in ‌full," the plant's management said in a statement posted on the MAX messenger app.

articles.title: UK Hindu family takes legal action after school objects to boy wearing tilak
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The parents of a nine-year-old boy have approached the UK High Court, alleging religious discrimination after he was prevented from wearing the sacred Tilak-Chandlo to school

The parents of a nine-year-old British Hindu boy, who was withdrawn from his primary school in London after it objected to him wearing a tilak on his forehead, have initiated legal proceedings in the UK High Court.

The boy, who belongs to the Swaminarayan faith tradition, had attended Vicar’s Green Primary School in west London since 2021 and worn his religious marking, known as the Tilak-Chandlo, without difficulty.
However, the school objected to the practice in late 2025, triggering a dispute that eventually led his parents to withdraw him from the school and pursue legal action.
“As parents, it has been heartbreaking to see our son go through this simply because he wanted to practise his faith,” the parents said in a statement released by their legal team this weekend.
“He had worn his Tilak-Chandlo to school for years without difficulty, and we never imagined that something so sacred to our family would become a source of distress,” they said.
“Our son was just an ordinary little boy who enjoyed learning and spending time with his friends. His religious marking did not hurt anyone or prevent him from being a good pupil.

“We have always taught our children to respect every religion, and we simply ask that the same respect be shown to ours. We hope that no other child will have to choose between their education and their faith,” they added.
The family is represented by Ashray Law, which has filed proceedings alleging religious discrimination under the UK’s Equality Act 2010 and breaches of rights protected by the Human Rights Act 1998.
The case, filed in the High Court of England and Wales, seeks £25,000 in damages. The proceedings are ongoing, and the allegations remain in dispute.
“This case goes beyond one child or one school. It raises important questions about religious freedom and equality in British education,” said Ambrish Limbachia, director of Ashray Law.

articles.title: Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water to be used for mist spraying in Kolkata; environmentalist slams move
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water will be mixed into mist spraying on special occasions, while environmentalist Somendra Mohan Ghosh says the city’s air needs cleaning at the source

West Bengal Municipal Affairs and Urban Development Minister Agnimitra Paul has said that, on special occasions, rose water will be mixed with the water normally used for mist spraying to control air pollution in the city.
The move drew criticism from an environmentalist, who argued that the city’s air needed to be cleaned at the source rather than through such cosmetic interventions.

In a Facebook post in Bengali, Ms. Paul said the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has regularly been spraying water mist at various locations across the city, particularly in areas where the Air Quality Index (AQI) is relatively high. This was being done under the direction of the State government to control air pollution in Kolkata and make the city’s environment cleaner.
The initiative is helping reduce the concentration of dust particles in the air and keep AQI levels somewhat under control, she said.
Alongside these measures, rose water will be mixed with the water used for mist spraying on special occasions and during various festivals, including Kali Puja, she said.

“This will not only help control dust particles in the air but also spread the pleasant fragrance of rose water throughout the surrounding environment... Our goal is to build a cleaner, fresher and fragrant Kolkata. We will continue our efforts to make the city more habitable,” Ms. Paul said in the post on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

“A few days ago, during my visit to London, I had observed that the AQI in several areas there was below 10, and in some places, even close to 1. This was truly astonishing. In contrast, Kolkata’s AQI rarely falls below 200 for most of the year,” she said.

This situation is a matter of concern for the health of all residents, and that is why the authorities are making continuous efforts, within their means, to improve the quality of air in the city, the Minister said.

Questioning Ms. Paul’s proposal, environmentalist Somendra Mohan Ghosh said on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that the city needs concrete measures to curb air pollution rather than cosmetic interventions.

articles.title: West Bengal to institute 'Seema Mitra' award for BSF, SSB, police personnel from 2027: Suvendu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 8, 2026) announced that his government would institute the 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 to recognise exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB, and state police personnel in securing the country's borders.

A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh.
"We will give the 'Seema Mitra' award from next year for BSF, SSB and West Bengal police personnel," Mr. Adhikari said.
The Chief Minister visited the border outpost to greet security personnel on the occasion of Diwali and Kali Puja.
The BSF guards the India-Bangladesh border, while the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is deployed along the country's frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan.
Mr. Adhikari apologised to the BSF and CRPF personnel for what he described as derogatory remarks and behaviour by the previous State government.

"I, as the Chief Minister of the State, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF," he said, targeting the erstwhile Trinamool Congress government.
He alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee government had failed to provide the required land to the BSF for fencing nearly 600 km of the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal.
Mr. Adhikari said the BJP government had handed over the required land to the BSF soon after assuming office and would provide any additional land needed for border fencing.
He said that his government will provide any additional requirement of land by the BSF in the border areas.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 8, 2026) announced that his government would institute the 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 to recognise exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB, and state police personnel in securing the country's borders.

A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh.

"We will give the 'Seema Mitra' award from next year for BSF, SSB and West Bengal police personnel," Mr. Adhikari said.

The Chief Minister visited the border outpost to greet security personnel on the occasion of Diwali and Kali Puja.

The BSF guards the India-Bangladesh border, while the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is deployed along the country's frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan.

Mr. Adhikari apologised to the BSF and CRPF personnel for what he described as derogatory remarks and behaviour by the previous State government.

"I, as the Chief Minister of the State, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF," he said, targeting the erstwhile Trinamool Congress government.

He alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee government had failed to provide the required land to the BSF for fencing nearly 600 km of the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal.

Mr. Adhikari said the BJP government had handed over the required land to the BSF soon after assuming office and would provide any additional land needed for border fencing.

He said that his government will provide any additional requirement of land by the BSF in the border areas.

articles.title: Turkey, Azerbaijan leaders vow unity after tensions
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Turkic-speaking allies describe their relationship as "one nation, two states" and, despite the friction, remain closely bound by military and energy ties

Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that their countries' alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours.
Tensions flared in September, when Baku revised school uniform regulations to prohibit clothing deemed incompatible with secular education, effectively barring Islamic headscarves in classrooms.
Mr. Erdogan's government has dismantled restrictions on hijabs in Turkey.

Azerbaijan's move sparked protests at home and drew criticism from Mr. Erdogan's Islamist-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP). Presidential adviser Oktay Saral demanded that Azerbaijan reverse the restrictions.
Baku also declared 31 Turkish nationals, including an Opposition lawmaker and party leaders, persona non grata over critical social media posts.

Mr. Erdogan subsequently dismissed Mr. Saral, but Mr. Aliyev stayed away from an October 30 summit of Turkic leaders in Ankara — despite a personal invitation from Mr. Erdogan. Instead, he sent Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Mr. Erdogan arrived in the country's Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago.
A guard of honour lined up at the airport, where Mr. Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva, welcomed Mr. Erdogan and his wife Ms. Emine.
"With the permission of Almighty God, our unity will endure forever," Mr. Erdogan told a joint press conference with Mr. Aliyev.
"This unity of hearts, which we describe with the motto 'One Nation, Two States,' is an everlasting torch that draws strength from our shared past and illuminates our future."

articles.title: Train collision in Egypt's Giza kills four, injures 88 others: Health Ministry
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza's Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt's worst-ever rail disaster
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday (November 8, 2026), derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities.
Egypt's railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
The Health Ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area.
State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident "with great concern", and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to "hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".
Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.
Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza's Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt's worst-ever rail disaster.
In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.
Egypt's 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

articles.title: Europe will be represented at U.S.-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi: France
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table
Europe will be represented at the upcoming U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
"The Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio .
His comment came after President Donald Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe".

Up to now, the talks scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) had been framed as a trilateral format at the level of officials, not leaders, from Ukraine, Russia and the United States.
The identities of who would take part have not been made public.

Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table.
Mr. Barrot said that, in the past, "there have been discussions, sometimes without the Europeans and sometimes with," but "this time they will participate".
He said, "France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard."
On Thursday (November 5, 2026), U.S., European, Ukrainian and NATO officials met in Brussels ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.
A NATO spokeswoman said they "sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine".

articles.title: Habitual offender arrested for murdering 65-year-old woman in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kengeri police have arrested a habitual offender for allegedly murdering a 65-year-old woman who was sleeping outside a temple and robbing her of cash and a gold ring in Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout.
The deceased, Narayanamma, was found dead in front of the Pataladamma Temple at Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout, Konasandra, within Kengeri police station limits, on November 3.
According to the police, Narayanamma had left her house due to family problems and had been sleeping outside the temple for the past few days.
A local resident who noticed her body informed her son, who arrived at the spot and identified her. The Kengeri police initially registered an unnatural death report based on his complaint.

However, following the post-mortem examination and information gathered during the investigation, police suspected that she had been murdered and robbed. A murder case was subsequently registered on Thursday.
During the investigation, police apprehended a suspicious person moving around Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout on Friday. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to the crime.
The accused reportedly told investigators that he had noticed Narayanamma sleeping alone and decided to rob her to arrange money to fund his vices.
In the early hours of November 3, he allegedly went to the spot, covered her mouth, assaulted her and robbed her of the cash she was carrying and a gold ring before fleeing, leaving her dead.

Police said the accused has a criminal history and was previously involved in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and robbery cases at Girinagar and Cottonpet police stations.
Further investigation and interrogation are under way, police said.

fullParagraphs: The Indian Olympic Association president alleged former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message seeking votes for four candidates ahead of Monday’s election

Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president P.T. Usha has lodged a complaint with the Electoral Officer alleging that former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message soliciting votes for a panel of four candidates in Monday’s (November 9, 2026) Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections.

Usha has urged the election authorities to examine the communication, establish the circumstances under which it was created and circulated, and seek an explanation from the persons concerned. She has also sought appropriate action under the applicable election rules if a violation is established, along with directions to ensure a level playing field for all candidates.

With polling scheduled from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 9, 2026, Usha has sought urgent intervention and a decision before voting begins. A screenshot of the WhatsApp message and a copy of the Model Code of Conduct were enclosed with the complaint.

articles.title: Revanth celebrates Deepavali with Indiramma house beneficiary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ministers, MLAs asked to spend festival with poor families who received houses; 2.21 lakh houses completed under scheme

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy along with Ministers and MLA celebrated Deepavali with a beneficiary of the Indiramma housing scheme at Parsapur village in Kodangal mandal on Sunday (November 8, 2026), in an initiative aimed at highlighting the government’s flagship housing programme for poor families.

The Chief Minister inaugurated the newly constructed house of Goripalli Sumitra and Srinivas, presented new clothes to the family, and had a traditional Deepavali meal of fine rice at their residence. Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar and Ministers Seethakka, Jupally Krishna Rao, Damodar Rajanarasimha and other public representatives joined the family for lunch.

The programme, titled ‘Maa Indiramma Intlo Deepavali’ (Deepavali in Our Indiramma Home), was conceived by Mr. Revanth Reddy to take the government’s housing initiative to the people and celebrate the festival with families who were allotted the houses.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and his Cabinet colleagues have lunch at the residence of a Indiramma house beneficiary in Kodangal constituency on November 8, 2026. Photo credit: Special Arrangement.

He had asked Ministers, MLAs and other elected representatives to spend Deepavali with beneficiaries of the scheme in their respective constituencies. The idea was to make the festival a celebration with poor families who had received permanent homes through government assistance, rather than confining the programme to official celebrations.

Later, the Chief Minister also inaugurated a science museum at Kosgi, a primary health centre at Balampet, police stations at Dudyala and Kodangal, a high school and junior college at Hakimpet and a new government junior college building at Doulatabad, all in the Kodangal constituency represented by him.

The Indiramma Housing scheme is the flagship scheme of the Revanth Reddy government. The latest figures announced by Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy recently revealed that around 2.21 lakh Indiramma houses had been completed across the State. The government has sanctioned 4.5 lakh houses in the first phase and another 2.5 lakh in the second phase. It has also taken up plans to construct one lakh houses in the Hyderabad urban region.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and his Cabinet colleagues present new clothes to a family of Indiramma house beneficiary in Kodangal constituency on November 8, 2026 as a part of Deepavali celebrations. Photo credit: Special Arrangement
The beneficiaries are picked up in an open lot without any interference of political leader, and the programmes are held in open spaces in the presence of all those who applied for the scheme.

The State has committed around ₹40,000 crore towards the two phases and the proposed urban housing programme. Separately, official housing department data available in October showed that ₹7,634 crore had been released to beneficiaries towards construction assistance.

articles.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing Dutch government on Gaza, Israel

fullParagraphs: Organisers of the “Red Line” demonstration called for stricter trade sanctions, a halt to arms sales, and an official declaration that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide

Tens of thousands of people, many of them dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in a mass demonstration aimed at pressing the Dutch government to take more decisive action against Israel over Gaza.

The organisers of the “Red Line” demonstrations in the Netherlands called for measures including stricter trade sanctions on Israel, officially declaring that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide, and halting all arms sales to Israel. The Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organisers, said in an online post that more than 200,000 people joined the march.

“What is happening there is inhumane,” said Mike van Dongen, as he walked in the huge throng. He was critical of the Dutch government’s actions. “As far as I’m concerned, they are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”

As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood on a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoed his cry as they passed.

Israel strongly rejects suggestions it is committing genocide in Gaza in its military campaign, which followed the attacks by Hamas-led militants in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. Militants killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostages.

Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and destroyed much of Gaza. More than 1,550 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed by the Israeli military since a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas began in October 2025, according to the territory’s Health Ministry.
The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, does not distinguish between civilians and militants, though it says women and children make up roughly half of the dead.

The campaign in Gaza has strained relations between the Netherlands and Israel. The Dutch Foreign Minister resigned last year after failing to secure new sanctions against Israel. Since then, a new minority coalition government has taken power and introduced an import ban on products from Israeli settlements, which the Dutch government and most of the international community consider illegal, a move that provoked a diplomatic spat with Israel.

Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who took part in a march last year but was not present on Sunday, defended his government’s actions at his weekly press conference on Friday (November 6, 2026). “Every single day and every single week, we do what we can to alleviate the terrible situation there,” he said.

He added that his administration was “exerting greater political and diplomatic pressure” on Israel to abide by its agreements on Gaza. At the same time, he said, the government was applying more pressure on Hamas and other organisations that continue to carry out “various operations that endanger the safety of ordinary Israelis.”

articles.title: Democrats eye Musk, Miller probes after midterm rout
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: California Representative Robert Garcia ‌said investigations will focus on Musk's involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency's firing of federal workers last year, and Miller's role in Trump's ‌hardline immigration crackdown

Tech megabillionaire Elon Musk and President ‌Donald Trump's newly appointed White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, ​will likely be targets of congressional probes when Democrats take control ⁠of Congress in January, a senior lawmaker said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

California Representative Robert Garcia, who is in line to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee next year after Democrats' sweeping midterm election victory, ‌said investigations will focus on Mr. Musk's involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency's firing of federal workers last year, and Mr. Miller's role in Mr. Trump's ‌hardline immigration crackdown.
"I think there's a lot of interest, not just from ‌our committee, ⁠but from committees across the Congress to speak to Mr. Musk," Mr. Garcia ⁠told CNN's "State of the Union."
Mr. Miller — whom Mr. Garcia called the architect of a "horrific, unjust" immigration policy — has been promoted to White House chief of staff, Mr. Trump said on Friday (November 6, 2026).
"Stephen Miller is at the centre ​of the major policy decisions that ‌are happening in the administration, and so it does deserve oversight and investigation," Mr. Garcia said.

The crackdown on immigration, which included operations in which two people were fatally shot in Minnesota by federal agents, has proven widely unpopular. A Reuters/Ipsos ‌poll in October found that only 37% approved of Mr. Trump's handling of immigration, ​down from 50% when he took office.

Voters delivered a historic rebuke to Republicans in Tuesday's (November 3, 2026) midterm election, but with Mr. Miller as White ⁠House chief of staff, the Trump administration is expected to continue its aggressive approach to immigration enforcement, amplify cultural conflicts and give no ground to a Democratic-controlled Congress, say officials ‌and experts who spoke to Reuters .

Hakeem Jeffries, who will become speaker of the U.S. House in January, said on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that Democrats would support a measure to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a congressional process that could remove him from office.
Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, has said he will reintroduce articles of impeachment against Mr. Hegseth soon. Mr. Jeffries said he is a "hard yes" on ‌backing that measure.

"Pete Hegseth has got to go... I believe there will be incredibly strong support for ​that resolution," Mr. Jeffries told ABC 's "This Week," citing the defense secretary's oversight of the unpopular Iran war launched by Mr. Trump in February, which has led ⁠to a spike in gas prices.

articles.title: Eisenkot warns of Israel crisis as he seeks to replace Netanyahu’s government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: isenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority

Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday (November 8, 2026) of forming a government , reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu's allies as he warned the veteran Prime Minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Mr. Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Mr. Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

"We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel," Mr. Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie, said at a ceremony at the Presidential office.
"We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps."

Mr. Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic Prime Minister — a community mostly descended from West Asian or North African Jews — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe.

articles.title: South Africa's ANC suffers worst election result as decline continues
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted

South Africa's African National Congress party faced its worst election results ever on Sunday (November 8, 2026) and a new low point on its gradual decline in popularity as voters rebuked it for a failure to deliver basic services like water and electricity in towns and cities.

The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted. The final results were expected late on Sunday (November 8, 2026), according to the Independent Electoral Commission.

The ANC remained the largest party by total share in an election involving hundreds of parties, but the Democratic Alliance that is its main Opposition had received around 25% of votes in the near-complete count.

That brought closer to reality the once-unthinkable notion that the ANC that led South Africa out of the white minority rule of apartheid and delivered freedom in 1994 under Mandela might one day not be its biggest party. It used to command 70% of the vote.

The ANC's popularity has declined for more than a decade. It won 45% support in the last local elections in 2021, the first time it had dropped below 50% in any election. In 2024, it then lost its Parliamentary majority for the first time in a national election, which brought about a coalition national government and a seismic shift in South African politics.

The ANC was on course Sunday (November 8, 2026) for a steep drop of about 15 percentage points from the last local elections and the loss of approximately one-third of its support from five years ago.
“If anyone has not heard what the people are saying in this election, then you are lost,” said ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula. “This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC.”
He said the results called for the ANC “to be humble, to hear our people and respect them,” and to “earn again through service and not through slogans the trust people have lent to others.”
DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said his party — which was around 20% points behind the ANC in the 2024 national election — had now “taken a big step forward” in its aim to be South Africa's biggest.
But, while the ANC's popularity has dropped sharply, no single party has overtaken it as the vote has fragmented among many parties on a local and national scale.

articles.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The devastating result leaves Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure

U.S. President Donald Trump vowed a political comeback on Sunday (November 8, 2026) after his Republican Party lost control of both houses of Congress in midterm elections that amounted to an unequivocal repudiation of his turbulent Presidency.

The devastating result leaves Mr. Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure, while opening the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress into the President, his family and senior members of his administration.

"America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election," Mr. Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote.
"But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!"
While the resounding election loss last Tuesday (November 3, 2026) has prompted soul-searching among Republican lawmakers, Mr. Trump has sounded defiant.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), he appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signalling a bare-knuckle fightback.
Democrats, meanwhile, have pledged to hold the Trump administration to account and fight against Mr. Miller, the architect of Mr. Trump's tough immigration policy.

Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to "lawyer up," Mr. Trump said on Saturday (November 8, 2026) he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to "extortion."
That stance stoked a war of words between top Republicans and Democrats on U.S. political shows on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Mr. Trump and now head of the Justice Department, vowed to actively defend Mr. Trump and senior members of his administration.

articles.title: Thick smog blankets Delhi on Deepavali night, AQI at 20 stations ‘severe’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days

A smoky haze hung over Delhi on Deepavali night, blurring streetlights and blanketing neighbourhoods as celebrations intensified across the capital, pushing air quality at 20 monitoring stations into the ‘severe’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index standing at 371 at 10 p.m..

The haze grew denser as the evening progressed, with smoke from firecrackers hanging over roads and residential neighbourhoods. The smell of burnt crackers lingered in the air, while visibility dropped in several parts of the capital and residents reported difficulty breathing.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Delhi air pollution: Capital sees ‘very poor’ AQI on Deepavali as GRAP 3 curbs continue

Despite restrictions on bursting firecrackers, several parts of Delhi continued to witness their use on Sunday evening (November 8, 2026), with reports of fireworks emerging from areas, including Pitampura, Burari, Mayur Vihar and parts of Lutyens’ Delhi.
Ahead of Deepavali, the Delhi government had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.
The District Magistrate (East), in an order, had permitted the bursting of green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m..

Residents reported that firecrackers were being burst in outer Delhi’s Pitampura and Burari, with the intensity particularly high in Burari. Similar reports came from Mayur Vihar, while people in the Bishambardas Marg area and Lutyens’ Delhi said fireworks continued, although the intensity had reduced slightly.

Of the 59 monitoring stations, 19 were in the 'severe' category at 7 p.m., seven in the 'poor' category, and the remaining 33 in the 'very poor' category. Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 460.
The city's average AQI for the day settled at 376 in the 'very poor' category, compared to 369 on Saturday, amid a layer of smog and reduced visibility.
The court prohibited bursting of firecrackers within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and other notified silence zones.

articles.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest.

“Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed.

According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation.

The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. articles.title: Did all the murders happen in the small house on the terrace?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Seven murders in Bengaluru have raised law and order concerns. Here’s a look at accused Indushekhar’s whereabouts and criminal history

Indushekhar lived with his wife Sunita and daughter in a small house, barely 500 sq. ft, on the terrace of a two-storey building, nestled among several commercial establishments, 50 metres from the famous Bhashyam Circle, Rajajinagar.

The building has commercial establishments on the ground floor, including a watch repair shop, a tea stall and a small condiments shop. The entire first floor was occupied by a small political party. Indushekar’s house is on the second floor, which also serves as the terrace.
Household appliances were crammed into the space, with several other household items scattered around. A board on the wall read, “Police Voice”.

Reaching the second floor itself through a very narrow staircase itself is a task. This has raised questions as to whether all seven murders were committed here in the house. However, the accused claimed that the murders took place inside his house. The location has raised several questions, as the building has very little space to move around.
However, the police investigation indicates a high probability that the murders took place there. “He may have cleaned the entire scene, but residues were found at the crime scene,” the officer said.

How did he transport the bodies down to the road into his car is a question that has left the police puzzled. He couldn’t have done it alone and that is where police suspect the role of the minor daughter. Given the lane mostly has commercial establishments, the police suspect that he could have shifted the bodies only during night time.

articles.title: Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State is drawing up a ₹20,000-crore project pipeline and a series of policy measures to prepare its cities for rising temperatures and erratic rainfall. The plan, which also includes waste reclamation, sewage treatment and digital monitoring of water supply, seeks to build climate resilience across urban local bodies

From bamboo bus shelters that offer shade and cooling to commuters, to the reclamation of waste dumps and the plugging of water supply leaks, Telangana is drawing up a broad plan to make its cities more resilient to climate change. The measures, backed by new urban policies and a project pipeline worth about ₹20,000 crore, are part of the State’s long-term Telangana Rising 2047 vision.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), said Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi said. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

Heatwaves and erratic rainfall are becoming increasingly evident across Telangana, though their impact varies by region. The government says this calls for location-specific interventions based on climate data. The challenge is significant: the State’s cities account for net emissions of about 66.56 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, with buildings, transport, wastewater, waste management and urban expansion among the major contributors.

Some interventions are already under way. Bamboo misting bus shelters in Khammam use a low-carbon building material while providing relief to commuters. Bio-mining of legacy waste dumps is aimed at reducing methane emissions and reclaiming land. The government is also working to reduce non-revenue water through leak detection, pipeline renewal and digital monitoring, besides expanding underground sewerage networks and reusing treated wastewater.
The bio-mining programme has helped avoid an estimated 5.6 lakh tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions and reclaimed about 418 acres for productive urban use, Ms. Sreedevi said.

To coordinate these efforts, a State Climate Centre for Cities has been established at the office of the Commissioner and Director of Municipal Administration. It will coordinate city-level climate action plans, maintain a climate data repository and provide technical support to municipalities.

Dedicated Climate Change Cells, city-specific action plans and nine Climate Action Officers are also planned for municipal corporations outside Hyderabad: Greater Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam, Nizamabad, Ramagundam, Nalgonda, Mancherial, Mahabubnagar and Kothagudem.

The Telangana Urban Climate Atlas, a climate intelligence platform, has been set up to help municipalities identify vulnerable zones, prioritise investments and track climate indicators. Capacity-building programmes have been conducted for representatives of 113 ULBs to strengthen preparedness and project planning.

A key intervention is the Cool Roof Policy, effective from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2028. It targets 300 sq km of cool roofs, including 200 sq km in the Hyderabad metropolitan region and 100 sq km in other urban local bodies. Cool roofs reflect about 80% of incoming sunlight, against 20% for conventional roofs. They can lower indoor temperatures by 2.1°C to 4.3°C and reduce air-conditioning costs by up to 20%. Full implementation is expected to save nearly 600 million units of electricity annually and generate a one-time carbon offset of about 30 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 07 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

The State is drawing up a ₹20,000-crore project pipeline and a series of policy measures to prepare its cities for rising temperatures and erratic rainfall. The plan, which also includes waste reclamation, sewage treatment and digital monitoring of water supply, seeks to build climate resilience across urban local bodies

From bamboo bus shelters that offer shade and cooling to commuters, to the reclamation of waste dumps and the plugging of water supply leaks, Telangana is drawing up a broad plan to make its cities more resilient to climate change. The measures, backed by new urban policies and a project pipeline worth about ₹20,000 crore, are part of the State’s long-term Telangana Rising 2047 vision.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), said Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi said. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

Heatwaves and erratic rainfall are becoming increasingly evident across Telangana, though their impact varies by region. The government says this calls for location-specific interventions based on climate data. The challenge is significant: the State’s cities account for net emissions of about 66.56 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, with buildings, transport, wastewater, waste management and urban expansion among the major contributors.

Some interventions are already under way. Bamboo misting bus shelters in Khammam use a low-carbon building material while providing relief to commuters. Bio-mining of legacy waste dumps is aimed at reducing methane emissions and reclaiming land. The government is also working to reduce non-revenue water through leak detection, pipeline renewal and digital monitoring, besides expanding underground sewerage networks and reusing treated wastewater.

The bio-mining programme has helped avoid an estimated 5.6 lakh tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions and reclaimed about 418 acres for productive urban use, Ms. Sreedevi said.

To coordinate these efforts, a State Climate Centre for Cities has been established at the office of the Commissioner and Director of Municipal Administration. It will coordinate city-level climate action plans, maintain a climate data repository and provide technical support to municipalities.

Dedicated Climate Change Cells, city-specific action plans and nine Climate Action Officers are also planned for municipal corporations outside Hyderabad: Greater Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam, Nizamabad, Ramagundam, Nalgonda, Mancherial, Mahabubnagar and Kothagudem.

The Telangana Urban Climate Atlas, a climate intelligence platform, has been set up to help municipalities identify vulnerable zones, prioritise investments and track climate indicators. Capacity-building programmes have been conducted for representatives of 113 ULBs to strengthen preparedness and project planning.

A key intervention is the Cool Roof Policy, effective from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2028. It targets 300 sq km of cool roofs, including 200 sq km in the Hyderabad metropolitan region and 100 sq km in other urban local bodies. Cool roofs reflect about 80% of incoming sunlight, against 20% for conventional roofs. They can lower indoor temperatures by 2.1°C to 4.3°C and reduce air-conditioning costs by up to 20%. Full implementation is expected to save nearly 600 million units of electricity annually and generate a one-time carbon offset of about 30 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

articles.title: Governor asks for status report on all public universities in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sudha Yadav, Governor of Karnataka and Chancellor of universities in the State, directed all public universities in the State to conduct a comprehensive review of their current operations and identify areas requiring improvement. The Governor instructed all Vice-Chancellors to prepare and submit a detailed report on the same. “This report should cover the current status of their respective universities, key achievements, challenges, shortcomings, and specific measures proposed for improvement,” she stated.

Addressing the Vice-Chancellors of various universities and officials from the Karnataka State Higher Education Council at Lok Bhavan, the Governor emphasised the need to strengthen the quality, transparency, accountability and overall performance of universities across the State.

“Emphasis must be placed on the effective implementation of the National Education Policy and the State Education Policy, strong coordination between industries and universities, as well as skill development, research, innovation and employability,” she said.
The Governor called upon all Vice-Chancellors and the Karnataka State Higher Education Council to work in coordination and collaboration to strengthen the higher education system in Karnataka.

articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam books row: political leaders raise concern over allegations, call for action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kamal Haasan demands the immediate withdrawal of the fake books from all libraries. M.H. Jawahirullah wants the formation of an independent committee to examine all books procured for the public library. Others, including Anbumani Ramadoss and K. Annamalai, want the government to take up a thorough investigation of the allegations

After writer Perumal Murugan wrote about alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore, Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) founder and Rajya Sabha Member Kamal Haasan said on Friday that “there can be no greater disgrace to the Tamil language than this”.

He pointed out that books containing fabricated information could cause immense damage in the long run. In a statement, he said the reputation of Tamil language would be irreparably damaged if people read, took notes, and incorporated the contents of (fabricated books) into speeches, written works, and research.

“Whoever is responsible for this has betrayed the Tamil language. I urge the Government of Tamil Nadu to immediately withdraw these fake books from all libraries and have them dumped on the streets and burnt. The publishing houses responsible for this must be sealed. We owe a debt of gratitude to writer Mr. Murugan for exposing this fraud,” Mr. Haasan said.
Manithaneya Makkal Katchi president and MLA M.H. Jawahirullah said allegations raised by Mr. Murugan had caused considerable shock and concern.
Manithaneya Makkal Katchi president M.H. Jawahirullah. | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ

He said: “It has come to light that 1,800 books published under the name of a publishing house called Akalvilakku Publications have been procured and placed on the library’s fourth floor. This publishing house, which is unfamiliar to serious readers, has raised suspicions that it may have been established specifically to supply books to the library. Furthermore, Mr. Murugan has alleged that books were produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence, without the proper application of technical expertise; that the authors’ names are either pseudonyms or fictitious; that the International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs) mentioned in the books cannot be found when checked online; and that the publisher’s address also appears to be unreliable,” he said.

Mr. Jawahirullah said, “An independent committee must be constituted to examine all books procured for the Periyar Arivulagam to date, including their publishers, authors, ISBNs, and pricing details, and a thorough inquiry must be conducted into the registration, addresses, owners, and activities of the suspicious publishing houses, including Agal Vilakku Publications.”

Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president and Virudhunagar MP B. Manickam Tagore alleged: “Everyone knows that the DMK government was replete with enormous corruption. No scheme was devoid of corruption. If there has been this level of corruption in the procurement of books, it is scary to think how much corruption would have been there in the construction of the building. The Tamil Nadu government should order an investigation.”
TNCC president B. Manickam Tagore. | Photo Credit: B. JOTHI RAMALINGAM
He added that all the books kept in Periyar Arivulagam should be audited and fabricated books should be removed.
