articles.title: Secret Service arrests man near White House after he said he heard voices telling him to kill Trump
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. officials say the suspect, Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, then went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation’s capital and kill the Republican President

The U.S. Secret Service said a suspect has been taken into custody and charged after officers found him in a vehicle near the White House with multiple guns, claiming he heard voices in his head telling him to kill President Donald Trump .
The arrest Thursday night (November 7, 2026) happened after Secret Service officers approached a man "acting suspicious" in a parked car, according to a Homeland Security statement.
U.S. officials say the suspect, Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, then went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation's capital and kill the Republican President.
Shortly after, officers discovered the suspect's vehicle had been reported stolen and he had three different firearms and dozens of rounds of ammunition.

This is the latest in a series of arrests the Secret Service and other law enforcement agencies have made against individuals who have threatened Trump or his family members' lives since he returned to office last year.

The statement described Chrinos as a migrant from Venezuela who is in the country illegally after entering the U.S. through Texas in March 2024. DHS said he has been charged and currently remains in U.S. Marshals Service custody.
The White House did not provide comment, instead referring to DHS and USSS.

"Thanks to our brave Secret Service officers, this illegal alien with three firearms in his vehicle was arrested near the White House before he could harm anyone," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in the statement.

articles.title: Jay Rockefeller, heir to famed dynasty and healthcare advocate in U.S. Senate, dies at 89
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jay Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty

John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, the progeny of one of America’s most famous and wealthiest families, who during three decades in the U.S. Senate sought expanded healthcare for the poor and excoriated President George W. Bush’s handling of ​the Iraq War, died on Friday (November 6, 2026) at his home in Washington, the Washington Post reported. He was 89.
His family did not provide a cause, the ‌newspaper added.

Mr. Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his ​five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as Governor of the poor coal-mining State.

Mr. Rockefeller voted ⁠in 2002 in favour of the Republican Bush’s measure authorising the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Mr. Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”
He was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty that included his uncle, New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
New York-born Jay Rockefeller’s life changed direction after he graduated from Harvard and served in a national service program in ‌impoverished rural West Virginia from 1964 to 1966.

When he was put in public office, he worked to increase healthcare access, ‌fight ⁠poverty, provide health benefits to coal miners and assist military veterans. As a senator, he had a role in shaping ⁠the programme created in 1997 under which the U.S. government helps States provide medical coverage for millions of uninsured children.

Mr. Rockefeller backed Democratic President Bill Clinton’s failed proposal for near-universal health insurance coverage in the 1990s and then fought for Democratic President Barack Obama’s successful quest for a healthcare overhaul law, signed in 2010.

In the debate over Mr. Obama’s measure, Mr. Rockefeller unsuccessfully ​sought to have the federal government offer a medical insurance ‌program to the general population — in addition to existing programs for the poor and elderly — as an alternative to private insurance plans that could be costly and exclusive.

“Championing those most in need has been my life’s calling and I will never stop fighting to make a difference for the people who mean so much to me,” Mr. Rockefeller said in 2013 when he announced at age 75 he would ‌not seek a sixth Senate term.

John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, the progeny of one of America’s most famous and wealthiest families, who during three decades in the U.S. Senate sought expanded healthcare for the poor and excoriated President George W. Bush’s handling of ​the Iraq War, died on Friday (November 6, 2026) at his home in Washington, the Washington Post reported. He was 89.

His family did not provide a cause, the ‌newspaper added.

Mr. Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his ​five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as Governor of the poor coal-mining State.

Mr. Rockefeller voted ⁠in 2002 in favour of the Republican Bush’s measure authorising the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Mr. Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”

He was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty that included his uncle, New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller.

New York-born Jay Rockefeller’s life changed direction after he graduated from Harvard and served in a national service program in ‌impoverished rural West Virginia from 1964 to 1966.

When he was put in public office, he worked to increase healthcare access, ‌fight ⁠poverty, provide health benefits to coal miners and assist military veterans. As a senator, he had a role in shaping ⁠the programme created in 1997 under which the U.S. government helps States provide medical coverage for millions of uninsured children.

Mr. Rockefeller backed Democratic President Bill Clinton’s failed proposal for near-universal health insurance coverage in the 1990s and then fought for Democratic President Barack Obama’s successful quest for a healthcare overhaul law, signed in 2010.

In the debate over Mr. Obama’s measure, Mr. Rockefeller unsuccessfully ​sought to have the federal government offer a medical insurance ‌program to the general population — in addition to existing programs for the poor and elderly — as an alternative to private insurance plans that could be costly and exclusive.

“Championing those most in need has been my life’s calling and I will never stop fighting to make a difference for the people who mean so much to me,” Mr. Rockefeller said in 2013 when he announced at age 75 he would ‌not seek a sixth Senate term.

fullParagraphs: ‘They knocked out — they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device — and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,’ says U.S. President Trump
President Donald Trump said the U.S. military on Friday (November 6, 2026) carried out new limited strikes on Iran, targeting an Iranian air defence system.
Iran state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in the crucial waterway for oil shipments.
Mr. Trump in an exchange with reporters described the military action as "minor".

"They knocked out — they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device — and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Mr. Trump told reporters shortly after arriving in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Friday (November 6) evening.

Mr. Trump did not offer further details about the target. U.S. officials have reported that most of Iran's air defence systems were destroyed or severely degraded during a June 2025 bombardment by Israel and in the early stages of the current conflict. U.S. officials have assessed that Iran would try to rebuild them and other military infrastructure over time.

The U.S. military also reported carrying out what it described as defensive strikes on Monday (November 2). Explosions were heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas.
Friday's (November 7) strikes are the first since Mr. Trump's Republican Party was dealt a stunning repudiation in Tuesday's (November 3) midterm elections in the U.S.

The electoral setback was stoked in part by voter dissatisfaction with Mr. Trump's execution of the conflict and elevated fuel prices, a byproduct of the war that's affected nearly every sector of the global economy.
In the days since Republicans' shellacking at the polls, Mr. Trump has vacillated between threatening to "destroy" Iran and suggesting a resolution to the war is near.

Earlier on Friday (November 6), officials from the two West Asian governments said Iran is reviewing proposals presented by chief mediator Qatar aimed at addressing differences with the U.S. about Tehran's nuclear programme.

articles.title: Keralam Child Development Centre gets ₹35-lakh grant to study autism-related parental grief
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Three-year project will examine chronic sorrow and coping mechanisms in ASD families.

The Child Development Centre (CDC), Thiruvananthapuram, has received an Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)-approved grant of ₹35 lakh for a three-year research project titled “Development and Validation of a Tool for Assessing Grief among Parents of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.”
The project, led by CDC director Deepa Bhaskaran, aims to develop and validate a culturally relevant tool to assess grief among parents of children with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD).

“The study will use focus group discussions and in-depth interviews involving parents of children with ASD, bereaved parents, professionals working with children with ASD, and members of the general population to understand the dimensions and cultural expressions of grief in the Indian context,” Dr. Bhaskaran said.

According to her, parents commonly experience shock, denial, fear, guilt, anger, sadness, and helplessness following their child’s diagnosis. The grief, described as chronic sorrow or non-finite grief, can recur at different stages of the child’s development, particularly when expected developmental milestones are not attained.

“The findings will help facilitate the identification of grief-related concerns among parents and support the development of appropriate grief counselling protocols and support group interventions, ultimately contributing to improved psychosocial well-being among families of children with ASD,” she said.
Inadequate social support compounds parental distress, she noted.

“There is a need for healthcare professionals to recognise and assess parents’ emotional well-being alongside the rehabilitation needs of children with autism. Early diagnosis, psychological support, and training for professionals to identify grief and help families develop coping strategies are vital,” she added.

articles.title: OpenAI to press ahead with data-centre expansion despite midterm sweep, CFO says
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly ‌to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry’s growth

OpenAI will press ahead with its US data-centre expansion plans despite a Democratic midterm sweep this week that has fuelled fears of tighter scrutiny ​of the facilities, its Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar told CNBC in an interview on Friday.

“When ‌I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how ​do we keep investing to meet customer demand,” Friar said. “We are ⁠going to keep building out those relationships with communities so we can get the compute we need,” she added.

One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly ‌to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry’s growth. It launched a charm offensive on Thursday to win ‌over communities as opposition to data centres becomes a rallying point for anxieties ‌about ⁠the technology.

As part of the efforts, OpenAI said, it will no ⁠longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites. It will also give residents access to construction plans and their potential effects.

Growing data-centre opposition was a crucial issue in the midterm ​elections. Democratic candidates, including Texas Governor-elect Gina ‌Hinojosa, made tighter scrutiny of the facilities a central campaign pledge. The Lone Star State is one of the fastest-growing data-center regions in the world.

Fears the Democratic sweep may slow construction of the facilities critical to the AI boom ‌wiped about $2.5 trillion off the US stock market on Thursday, as investors ​weighed the fallout for the chip, cloud and networking industries that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the spending frenzy.
Still, there are ⁠signs that tech giants remain committed to data-centre expansion plans despite the growing backlash.
Alphabet-owned Google said on Thursday it would invest $17 billion to build its first data centre ‌in Wyoming.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg News reported that ByteDance is considering expanding a data centre project in northeastern Brazil, a move that would strengthen its standing as Latin America’s leading builder of computing facilities.
Friar also told CNBC that OpenAI was raising fresh capital, pushing back against suggestions the ChatGPT maker had scaled back its fundraising ambitions amid the sharp AI stocks selloff.

fullParagraphs: After spending years waiting for an international call-up, Klinger sparkled in his brief stint with Australia. articles.title: Activists invade site of Microsoft's planned data centre in Amsterdam
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: "It's so many things, so many struggles that come together in this data centre," Geef Tegengas spokesman, Nathan Timmer, told AFP
Several hundred activists opposed to the construction of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam occupied the site on Friday, responding to a call for a two-day protest across Europe.
The collective Geef Tegengas, which campaigns for climate and justice, and the environmental group Fossielvrij entered the construction site in the Sloterdijk district, halting work for the day.
"It's so many things, so many struggles that come together in this data centre," Geef Tegengas spokesman, Nathan Timmer, told AFP.
"This thing will use as much energy as all of the households in Amsterdam combined... this thing will use a ridiculous amount of water."
Timmer, 30, also argued that the centre would be used "to facilitate AI warfare" and what he called the "genocide" in Gaza.
The activists made it on to the site by scaling barrier fences despite a police presence.
Once inside they shouted political slogans and sprayed anti-Microsoft messages on walls under construction.
Dutch news agency ANP reported that police arrested between 150 and 200 protesters. Other activists quit the site voluntarily.
AI data centres require large amounts of electricity, placing increased pressure on grids often still reliant on fossil fuels, and, in many cases, water to cool down hot computing equipment.
A backlash is growing worldwide against their environmental impact, and there are also concerns over noise, pollution, their appearance and how many jobs the facilities actually create.

articles.title: Assam CM encouraging protests against Judges in Zubeen Garg death case: Akhil Gogoi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sibsagar MLA says Himanta Biswa Sarma’s remarks amount to contempt of court
Sibsagar MLA and Raijor Dal president Akhil Gogoi has accused Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of encouraging people to protest against Judges and witnesses in the Zubeen Garg death case.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), the Chief Minister flagged a threat to his family after a group threatened to besiege his house over the case. He also said he would bring the threat by Zubeen Garg Nyay Dabi Samiti to the notice of the Supreme Court and the Gauhati High Court, as it could amount to an attempt to murder.
Mr Gogoi, who leads the Samiti, responded by saying the Chief Minister’s remarks amounted to contempt of court.

articles.title: Police seek lookout circular against Kochi doctor accused of sexual abuse
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kochi City police have decided to get a lookout circular issued against a 41-year-old doctor who has been booked for the alleged sexual assault of a woman. The police have intensified the search for Dr. Johnson Varghese, amid suspicions that he may have sexually abused more women.

Police sources said investigators had found visuals on Dr. Johnson’s phone allegedly showing him abusing at least 12 women. The phone was handed over to the police by the complainant, a 50-year-old woman.

“We are trying to get a lookout circular issued against the accused at the earliest to prevent him from leaving the country. The procedures for issuing the circular have been started,” a senior city police officer said.

The Infopark police registered the case against Dr. Varghese on Friday, a day after three people, including two actors, were arrested for allegedly assaulting and robbing him. He was booked based on a complaint filed by a relative of one of the accused in the case registered by the doctor.
Police sources said the doctor was accused of abusing the woman after giving her intoxicants.

The Kadavanthra police had on Thursday arrested two film actors and an accomplice for allegedly assaulting and robbing the doctor of valuables worth ₹3.25 lakh after being called to an apartment in Kochi for emergency medical care.
The hospital in Kochi where Dr. Johnson was employed dismissed him from service soon after he was booked for sexual abuse.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir to revisit love, loss and her decision to decline India’s top job
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘It was heartbreak and loss that threw me into the public world of politics. Up till then I had guarded my privacy fiercely,’ Sonia Gandhi said in her statement

Congress leader and Rajya Sabha Member Sonia Gandhi has a memoir coming out this fall in which she will reflect on the promise and the tragedy of marrying into India’s Nehru-Gandhi political dynasty and on her own career in government.
Publishing house Alfred A. Knopf announced on Tuesday (August 18, 2026) that Ms. Gandhi’s “Belonging: A Journey of Love” will be published on November 10.

“Much has been written about my family, but few narratives were able to reach into the truth of their motivations, their actions and even their very human failings,” Ms. Gandhi said in a statement issued through Knopf. “In many ways, this book is a homage to their humanness. My story also offers readers a unique perspective of the social and political changes I have witnessed for six decades in the beautiful country of my belonging.”

Ms. Gandhi, 79, is a native of Italy who was studying in Cambridge, England, when she met fellow student and future husband Rajiv Gandhi, grandson of India’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, and son of India’s first female Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi.

In Belonging , she writes of her life being upended when her mother-in-law was assassinated in 1984 and succeeded by Rajiv Gandhi, who was also murdered seven years later. She too would eventually enter politics and become the longest-serving president of the Indian National Congress Party while also turning down her party’s offer to become Prime Minister. Her party lost power to Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2014.
“It was heartbreak and loss that threw me into the public world of politics. Up till then I had guarded my privacy fiercely,” she said in her statement.

“Writing about my life did not come easily to me. It meant opening myself up, sharing moments and experiences I had always held deep inside,” she said. “Yet as I gradually removed myself from the political sphere and looked back at all I had seen, the thread of love and loyalty that wove through my story began to define itself, from the simplicity of my childhood in small-town Italy, to the complexity of my years in India as the wife of Rajiv Gandhi and the daughter-in-law of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.”

In Belonging , she writes of her life being upended when her mother-in-law was assassinated in 1984 and succeeded by Rajiv Gandhi, who was also murdered seven years later. She too would eventually enter politics and become the longest-serving president of the Indian National Congress Party while also turning down her party’s offer to become Prime Minister. Her party lost power to Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2014.

“It was heartbreak and loss that threw me into the public world of politics. Up till then I had guarded my privacy fiercely,” she said in her statement.

“Writing about my life did not come easily to me. It meant opening myself up, sharing moments and experiences I had always held deep inside,” she said. “Yet as I gradually removed myself from the political sphere and looked back at all I had seen, the thread of love and loyalty that wove through my story began to define itself, from the simplicity of my childhood in small-town Italy, to the complexity of my years in India as the wife of Rajiv Gandhi and the daughter-in-law of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.”

On his father Rajiv Gandhi’s birth anniversary, senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday (August 20, 2026) recalled the loss of his father and paid an emotional tribute to his mother Sonia Gandhi, saying he could imagine “Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia”.
Mr. Gandhi was referring to the upcoming memoir of his mother and Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

In a message on X , Mr. Gandhi said he had last seen his parents together more than 35 years ago and since then watched his mother “face everything life threw at you with never-ending courage and dignity”.
Only he and his sister, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, he said, knew “what you have been through, and how difficult your life after Papa truly was”.

Mr. Gandhi said he was proud that Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love , would be read by “millions of people who love you”, adding that he knew how difficult it had been for someone as private as her to tell her story.

The memoir, due to be released in November, recounts her journey from Italy to India, her marriage to Rajiv Gandhi, the deaths of Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi, her entry into politics after her husband’s assassination and her decision to decline the Prime Minister’s post in 2004.

At an event later in the day to mark his father’s birth anniversary, Mr. Gandhi shifted from the personal to the political, saying the growing assertion by students across the country could no longer be suppressed.

“The students are saying we have an expression and we believe in certain things as individuals. I am very proud now that millions of young students have understood this,” he said, adding that the “expression has suddenly come out and it cannot be stopped”.

The challenge, he said, was to convert this awakening into structural change, particularly in education. Invoking Mahatma Gandhi’s idea of swaraj , Mr. Gandhi said it was not merely “freedom” but “rule over oneself” and required an environment in which people could pursue their own conception of truth.

He questioned how swaraj could exist alongside an expensive education system, an unfair examination system, and an economy dominated by a handful of people. “How will that expression transform the education system of our country,” he asked.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and other top officials are monitoring the counting

The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), comprising Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Jana Sena Party (JSP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), registered a decisive victory in the MPTC elections in Bapatla district by winning 117 seats of the 273 MPTCs taken up for counting of votes.

According to the updates received till the last report came in on Saturday, the TDP secured 109 MPTC seats, while its alliance partner JSP won eight. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) secured 19 seats, while others won one. The BJP did not register a victory in the results declared so far.

Leader of the Opposition in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council Botcha Satyanarayana’s daughter, Botcha Anusha, was defeated in the Bondapalli ZPTC constituency, where Telugu Desam Party (TDP) nominee Pashala Neeraja won by a margin of 5,136 votes.

The result assumed significance as Bondapalli falls under the Gajapathinagaram Assembly constituency, represented by Minister for MSME Kondapalli Srinivas. Ms. Anusha is also in charge of the Bheemili Assembly constituency in Visakhapatnam district.

Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) president Y.S. Sharmila has congratulated former MLA and senior Congress leader Amanchi Krishna Mohan on the party’s performance in the Chirala Municipality elections, in which it won 10 of the 44 councillor seats.

In a statement, Ms. Sharmila praised Mr. Krishna Mohan, who is also the Bapatla District Congress Committee president and a member of the State Political Affairs Committee (PAC), for his efforts to strengthen the party in Chirala. The Congress contested 42 wards and secured second place in several others.

Describing the party’s performance as a moral victory, Ms. Sharmila said the results demonstrated the Congress’s potential to emerge as a political alternative, despite failing to capture control of the municipality. She thanked voters, party workers and elected councillors for their support and urged the newly elected councillors to function as an effective Opposition by consistently raising public issues and holding the ruling alliance accountable.

Maintaining that the MPTC and ZPTC elections have proved that the people of Andhra Pradesh are favouring development, Roads and Buildings Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy has said YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy should accept the people’s mandate. articles.title: Top U.S., China officials raise trade 'concerns' as APEC approaches
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and discussed economic and trade commitments over the last year

Top officials from Washington and Beijing held "frank" talks on their countries' testy trade relationship on Friday (November 6, 2026), ahead of an Asia-Pacific summit in China this month where their leaders are due to meet.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and discussed economic and trade commitments over the last year, both sides said.

The Americans stressed "the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments" and highlighted "concerns about recent Chinese actions", according to a statement released by the U.S. Treasury Department.

Mr. Lifeng, meanwhile, expressed "serious concerns over recent economic and trade restrictive measures imposed by the United States", according to a State media report shared online by Beijing's Commerce Ministry on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
The report did not specify which measures Mr. Lifeng was referring to, but added that the talks were "frank, in-depth and constructive".
Mr. Bessent "underscored that continued progress depends on concrete results and that the United States will closely assess China's implementation of the arrangement", said the Treasury.

The statement referenced China's commitments from an October 2025 meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Busan, South Korea, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
China is hosting this year's APEC gathering from November 18 to 19 in Shenzhen, which could also see a trilateral meeting with Mr. Trump, Mr. Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Beijing's Foreign Ministry said this week it was in contact with Washington and Moscow about the possibility.

The Busan agreement, which reflected calming tensions between the superpowers after they had exchanged tariff escalations earlier in 2025, required China to purchase U.S. soybeans this year and through 2028.

articles.title: Iran says forces 'stronger' than at beginning of war
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Islamic Republic’s armed forces, having gained experience from direct confrontation with United States and Israel, are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war, Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said

Iran said Saturday (November 7, 2026) its military has grown "stronger" since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran's nuclear programme.
Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the West Asia conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.
He also said Iran's forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," he said.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), the U.S. military said it was offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

articles.title: U.S. FBI and regulators issue warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial refrigerators
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The U.S. regulators warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems,” shortly after these hacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarkets
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and government regulators on Thursday (November 5, 2026) issued a warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial coolers and fridges.
The warning acknowledged that hackers were targeting vulnerabilities in unpatched or internet-linked refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.
Gaining control of these systems would enable hackers to adjust temperatures to dangerous extremes or run unauthorised defrost cycles, leading to the spoilage of inventory or even fire hazards.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Health and Human Services (HHS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DOT) warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems.”

The U.S. FBI-issued factsheet recommended that organisations with cold storage facilities de-link control system devices from the internet, enhance password security, apply patches to keep systems updated, and replace legacy devices that no longer receive security updates.

The notice came shortly after cyber attacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarket franchises, where some fridge temperatures were raised as high as 50 degrees Celsius in October.
Food and produce had to be thrown out at a mass scale, along with large quantities of melted ice.
The perpetrators behind the attacks have not yet been identified or apprehended.

“Industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems protect food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive products, making them attractive targets for malicious cyber actors. We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” said FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman.

The U.S. regulators warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems,” shortly after these hacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarkets

The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and government regulators on Thursday (November 5, 2026) issued a warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial coolers and fridges.

The warning acknowledged that hackers were targeting vulnerabilities in unpatched or internet-linked refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.

Gaining control of these systems would enable hackers to adjust temperatures to dangerous extremes or run unauthorised defrost cycles, leading to the spoilage of inventory or even fire hazards.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Health and Human Services (HHS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DOT) warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems.”

The U.S. FBI-issued factsheet recommended that organisations with cold storage facilities de-link control system devices from the internet, enhance password security, apply patches to keep systems updated, and replace legacy devices that no longer receive security updates.

The notice came shortly after cyber attacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarket franchises, where some fridge temperatures were raised as high as 50 degrees Celsius in October.

Food and produce had to be thrown out at a mass scale, along with large quantities of melted ice.

The perpetrators behind the attacks have not yet been identified or apprehended.

“Industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems protect food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive products, making them attractive targets for malicious cyber actors. We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” said FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman.

articles.title: FDA suspends 105 licences, cancels 7 across Maharashtra after pre-Deepavali checks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The FDA pre-Deepavali inspections found violations in hygiene, food storage, manufacturing practices, and licensing requirements

The Mumbai Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) suspended the licenses of 105 firms and cancelled the licenses of seven eateries across Maharashtra after inspections on November 4 and 5, according to a document from the agency. The FDA seized 39,485 kg of food products worth ₹1.35 crore from at least 69 establishments.

In Mumbai, licenses of 28 eateries were suspended. The license of one eatery, Rajdhani Biryani Centre, was cancelled. Companies Blink Commerce and Zepto had their licenses suspended. Across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, 2,396.6 kg of food products with a value of ₹13.87 lakh were seized. The items included sweets, ingredients, savouries, and food in packets.

The action followed inspections. The inspections found violations in hygiene, food storage, manufacturing practices, and licensing requirements. The inspections did not find records of health checks and training for food handlers.
The stock of Jetharam Chuniram Puniya (Malad) was seized. The owner manufactured food products without a license and sold them without labels.
The 44 kg of boondi laddus and kalakand from Jamnagari Sweets and Farsan (Vile Parle) were confiscated. The FDA cited the use of food color in contravention of the limits.
The FDA has warned vendors of sweets and manufacturers to follow the rules before Deepavali. It said it would continue checks before the festival.

Tukaram Mundhe, the FDA Commissioner, said the agency works to protect citizens from food that does not meet standards. He said it would not compromise on food quality or health, regardless of a business’s size or reputation.

articles.title: Sanskrit varsity suspension row: Prakash Raj says protesting students ‘are not Savarkars’ to tender apology
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The actor visits protest site, says he will join protesting students if they are not allowed to appear for their examinations

Actor and activist Prakash Raj said here on Saturday (November 7, 2026) that “the youth of the country are not Savarkars to write sorry petitions for raising questions and protesting for their rights.”

“This generation is not violent like your Godse. This generation protests with the strength of what Gandhi has taught them. This generation is asking questions with the right Babasaheb Ambedkar has given them,” he said after expressing solidarity with the relay fast organised by the suspended activists of the Students Federation of India (SFI) at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) at Kalady.

He was referring to the Syndicate decision to withdraw their suspension once they submitted an apology stating that they will not breach disciplinary norms in the future. Sixteen students were suspended in connection with the protests held at the campus on August 13, 2026 while the first meeting of the re-constituted Syndicate was underway.
The actor alleged that the university authorities and the Minister for Higher Education Roji M. John were showing “a dictatorial attitude” towards the protest.

“How long will everyone become like Narendra Modi and the Central government to stop the youth from protesting and asking questions? What have the students done?. They had issues with the basic necessities of the university. They have done a play as they come from the Department of Theatre. Is doing a play a crime in this country?” he asked.

He asked the authorities to show the evidence related to the allegations that the suspended students had physically assaulted Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas during their protest on August 13. “All this is drama. Let the theatre students perform the drama. Why are you doing the drama. Why are you writing the scripts? It is for them to write the scripts of their future,” he said.
The actor said he would join the protesting students if they were not allowed to appear for their examinations.

articles.title: New Zealand vote still too close to call as results trickle in

fullParagraphs: New Zealand’s election remained too close to call on November 7, as early results trickled in from across the country, with neither the governing National-Luxon coalition nor Labour falling short of a majority and minor parties weighing in, including a rising Opportunity Party

The outcome of New Zealand's election remained too close to call as early results began to roll in on Saturday (November 7, 2026), with none of the parties expected to secure a majority after a campaign dominated by worries over rising costs of living and the economy.
Kiwis are struggling to make ends meet — the price of basic goods remains stubbornly high, and unemployment is at its highest in more than a decade.
The war in West Asia and the subsequent global fuel shock have been widely blamed for the hit to New Zealand's trade-dependent economy.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon hoped his right-wing coalition could cling to power with promises of no new taxes, after three fractious years in office, two failed bids by his own National Party to oust him as leader and an economy in the doldrums.
Former Premier Chris Hipkins' centre-left Labour have promised help with living costs, from free doctor's visits and prescriptions to a cap on public transport fares.
He said on Friday (November 6) he was sure his party would "exceed expectations".
At a Labour event in Upper Hutt near Wellington bedecked with red balloons, party workers were quietly confident they had secured the largest number of seats.
And at a National gathering in the country's largest city of Auckland, cheers rose from the crowd as the party's candidates were shown to be ahead.
Police minister and National lawmaker Mark Mitchell told journalists it was "very close".
"When you reflect on what's happening globally, we certainly see lots of geopolitical uncertainty," he said.

The outcome of New Zealand's election remained too close to call as early results began to roll in on Saturday (November 7, 2026), with none of the parties expected to secure a majority after a campaign dominated by worries over rising costs of living and the economy.

Kiwis are struggling to make ends meet — the price of basic goods remains stubbornly high, and unemployment is at its highest in more than a decade.

He said on Friday (November 6) he was sure his party would "exceed expectations".

fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim to enter the U.S. Senate with his victory over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in midterm elections

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat on Tuesday (November 4, 2026), according to media projections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the chamber and preserving a crucial Democratic seat in the party’s fight for Senate control.

His victory denied Republicans the chance to fill the seat left vacant by retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. The 42-year-old former public health official ran on a progressive platform focused ⁠on lowering costs for working families and ⁠reducing corporate influence in politics.
His win marked a breakthrough for the Democratic Party’s progressive wing ‌in this closely contested midterm election cycle.

Abdul El-Sayed was born on October 31 , 1984, in Rochester Hills, Michigan, U.S.. He attended public schools, where he captained his high school football, wrestling and lacrosse teams. He was raised by his father, Mohamed, an Egyptian immigrant and his stepmom, Jackie, whose family has lived in Gratiot County, Michigan since the 1800s. Mr. El-Sayed earned his undergraduate degree with the highest distinction from the University of Michigan where he also played on the Wolverine men’s lacrosse team. He went on to earn a medical degree from Columbia University under an NIH-funded fellowship, as well as a second doctorate from Oxford University as Rhodes Scholer.
He lives in Ann Arbor with his wife, Dr. Sarah Jukaku and their two daughters.

Although trained as a physician, Mr. El-Sayed shifted his focus to public service after realising the political systemic issues that was deteriorating public health, according to his campaign website.

He rebuilt Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy and led Wayne County’s Department of Health. Human & Veterans Services, serving 1.8 million residents. His public service spans several achievements, including securing free eyeglasses for children, targeting major environmental polluters, making the life-saving Narcan universally accessible and pioneering a programme projected to cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 3,00,000 Michiganders, as per the website.

He authored Medicare for All: A Citizen’s Guide and served on former President Biden’s 2020 Unity Task Force for Healthcare to help develop policies aimed at lowering prescription drug costs. His public service earned him recognition as “Public Official of the Year” by the Michigan LCV and also a spot on Crain’s Detroit Business 40 Under 40 list.

Mr. El-Sayed won the U.S. Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. He launched his campaign to lower living costs and ensure government agencies serve working people rather than billionaires.

Mr. Rogers, 63, ‌a former Congressman and FBI agent, entered ​the race with strong backing from President Trump and national Republicans and sought ⁠to cast Mr. El-Sayed as a radical candidate sympathetic to Islamic extremism through alleged ties to the Muslim ‌Brotherhood, claims that Mr. El-Sayed denies and that remain unsupported by evidence. Democrats said the attacks on Mr. El-Sayed relied on Islamophobic tropes, according to Reuters.

articles.title: U.S. midterm election results: Senate, House and Governor shifts before and after
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Democrats surged to full control of Congress in the November 2026 U.S. midterm elections, flipping the Senate and House after winning net seats across key battlegrounds and sweeping into Republican strongholds. Here’s what changed between 2022 and 2026 midterms.

The November U.S. midterm elections saw a major shift in Washington’s power dynamic as Democrats captured full control of both chambers of the U.S. Congress, by crossing the 218-seat threshold needed for a majority.

In contrast to the 2022 midterms, where former President Joe Biden’s Democrats defied expected losses by holding the Senate and narrowly losing the House, the 2026 midterms saw Democrats gain full control of both chambers of Congress.

The almost dramatic swing towards Democrats, by the very same voters in the conservative bastion that propelled President Donald Trump to a second term just two years ago, is a result of widespread discontent over economic pressures including high living costs along with foreign policy decisions regarding the war with Iran. Voters elected Democratic candidates across the conservative strongholds and swing states creating a divided government under Mr. Trump.

In the 2022 midterms, pre-election predictions pointed toward a powerful “red wave” favouring Republicans due to surging inflation and low approval ratings for Mr. Biden. But the wave failed to fully materialise. Democrats defied the trends by retaining control of the Senate (reaching 50 seats after picking up Pennsylvania and holding Nevada), though Republicans narrowly flipped control of the House of Representatives with a slim majority.
In the 2026 midterms, the story was different. Democrats scored a sweeping victory over the ruling party, seizing control of both Senate and the House of Representatives.
In 2022 midterm elections, Democrats entered the election with a 50-50 split (with Vice-President Kamala Harris as the tiebreaker) and expanded their narrow control.

They gained a net seat by flipping Pennsylvania (where Democrat John Fetterman defeated Mehmet Oz) and secured a majority by holding Nevada (Catherine Cortez Masto), finishing with 50 seats to Republicans’ 49.

In 2026, Democrats captured full control of the 100-seat upper chamber by making historic inroads into Republican strongholds. The Democratic Caucus has currently secured 54 seats to achieve majority after defending its existing seats and winning key races, while the Republican Caucus has secured 44 seats. The counting is still under way.

Major wins include James Talarico gaining a Senate seat in Texas, Kansas electing its first Democratic Senator since the Great Depression and Democrats defeating Mr. Trump’s handpicked candidate in South Carolina (Democrat Annie Andrews ousting Republican Darline Graham).

In 2022, Republicans gained control of the House, gaining nine net seats to secure a narrow majority of 222 seats compared to the Democrats’ 213 seats, crossing the majority mark of 218 seats in the 435-seat chamber. This narrow margin of victory was potentially close to the 221–212 margin seen in 2001.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

articles.title: T.N. CM Vijay writes to PM Modi expressing concerns over inspection of Union govt. officials regarding Mekedatu dam project
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: CM Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressing his concerns regarding the site inspection conducted by the Union government officials in connection with the Karnataka government’s proposal to construct the Mekedatu dam.

He urged the Prime Minister that no statutory or administrative approvals be granted without the consent of the co-basin States, while emphasising the need to ensure the sustained water availability in the Cauvery basin of Tamil Nadu.
In his letter, Mr. Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka.

“The said proposal of Government of Karnataka to construct Mekedatu reservoir across Cauvery with a huge capacity of 67.16 TMC, just upstream of inter-State border between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, would not only prevent the flows due to Tamil Nadu but also prejudicially affect the monthly deliveries to the inhabitants of Cauvery Basin of Tamil Nadu, as stipulated by the Hon’ble Supreme Court,” Mr. Vijay said in his letter.

There have been frequent news reports on Karnataka Chief Minister’s meeting with the officials of Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for clearance of DPR of Mekedatu Project, without the concurrence of Tamil Nadu, which keep the farmers of the State in a state of perpetual anxiety , he said.

“Earlier, a team of officers of the Government of India reportedly visited the proposed Mekedatu Dam site, as per the statements emanating from the State of Karnataka. The anxious farmers of Tamil Nadu view the site visit as an indication of tacit movement on a project that would jeopardise their very livelihood. Such actions, the purported site inspection by Government of India officials, have deepened the worries of the farmers of Cauvery delta, who are already struggling in this deficit water year (2026–27), due to Karnataka’s denial to ensure Tamil Nadu’s due share even on a pro-rata basis,” Mr. Vijay said.

Mr. Vijay also referred to his earlier letter dated July 28, where in he requested the Prime Minister to ensure that no statutory or administrative approval be granted to the Mekedatu Project, unless it is demonstrably consistent with the Final Award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) and the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s Judgment.

The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly passed a unanimous Resolution on June 19, reiterating its demand on the proposed Mekedatu project and also filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court with a prayer to withdraw the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in December, 2025, on the preparation of DPR for irrigation and multi-purpose project proposals, exclusively for Cauvery basin, since the basin is held to be a deficit by the Tribunal in February, 2007. This matter is still pending in the Supreme Court of India, Mr. Vijay pointed out.

“It is vital that the rights of lower riparian States regarding both the quantum and regulated pattern of monthly releases remain fully protected and hence, consideration or examination of DPR of Mekedatu Project submitted by Karnataka or any unilateral technical evaluations or site inspections by central agencies at this juncture are highly inappropriate,” he said.

articles.title: A total of 28 illegal immigrants apprehended, expelled: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a post on X, Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity

“Police in Assam 's Sribhumi district apprehended and expelled 28 Bangladeshi nationals allegedly staying illegally in the State,” Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
In a post on X, Mr. Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity.

"Assam's patience with infiltration is over. Twenty-eight illegal migrants detected by Sribhumi Police were expelled. We will continue this mission with unwavering determination. No compromise on our borders. No compromise on the security and identity of Assam,'' he added.

Assam has an integrated checkpost in Sribhumi and a land customs station at Mankachar. Mr. Sarma had earlier said the State government is committed to an infiltration-free Assam. The Border Security Force has intensified its vigil along the 1,885 km Indo-Bangladesh border in the Northeast since the 2024 disturbances in Bangladesh. Assam Police has also maintained a high alert along the International Border to prevent illegal entry.

articles.title: Karnataka Police Complaints Authority member proposes seniority badges for police personnel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel

A member of the Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority, has urged the State Government to introduce special designations and insignia on police uniforms to recognise the seniority of personnel based on their years of service, irrespective of promotions.

In a letter dated November 5 to Minister for Home, IT-BT and E-Governance Priyank Kharge, Karnataka State Police Complaints’ Authority member Mohan Kumar Danappa proposed introducing three categories of seniority for police personnel, from constables to non-IPS officers.

According to his proposal, personnel completing five years of service should be designated as ‘Senior’, those completing 10 years as ‘Super Senior’, and those completing 15 years as ‘Most Senior’. He has suggested that distinct insignia corresponding to these designations be displayed on the right side of the chest, above the nameplate.

Mr. Danappa pointed out that although police personnel generally become eligible for promotion after five years of service, promotions are largely dependent on the availability of vacancies. As a result, many experienced personnel continue in the same rank for years without any formal recognition of their seniority and experience.
He said the proposed system would recognise their long service, enhance their sense of responsibility and ensure that experienced personnel receive due respect within the department and society.

Citing the practice of providing black collar patches to IPS officers after 10 years of service, he said similar arrangements were also followed in certain State police forces and Central Armed Police Forces.

He also referred to the State Government’s recent initiatives to replace British-era police caps and introduce lanyards in place of whistle chains, stating that recognising seniority through uniform insignia would be another significant reform to boost the morale of police personnel.
If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel, he said.
Mr. Danappa has requested the Home Minister to examine the proposal and issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities for its implementation.

articles.title: Bengaluru cab driver kills wife, six members of her family
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The murders are believed to have been carried out between October 16 and November 3, with the bodies dumped at multiple locations on Bengaluru’s outskirts, including one near the foothills of Nandi Hills in Chickballapur.

In a shocking murder spree in Bengaluru , a 52-year-old man allegedly killed his wife and six members of her family, including a seven-year-old boy, and disposed of the bodies over a span of 18 days, police sources said. An 11-year-old boy, who is also a relative of the accused, has been rescued.

The accused was allegedly assisted by his 17-year-old college-going daughter, whose exact role is yet to be established. Family disputes are believed to have been the motive for the murders, although the police have not ruled out any other angle and are interrogating the accused.

The prime accused, identified as Indushekar, a cab driver and YouTuber who also ran a monthly tabloid, has been arrested by the Rajajinagar police. The murders are believed to have been committed between October 16 and 31, while the last two bodies were reportedly disposed of on November 1 and 2.

A preliminary police investigation revealed that the accused, with the help of his daughter, invited the relatives to his house on the pretext of a non-vegetarian dinner or a party. “After dinner, when the relatives fell asleep, the accused used a grinding stone to kill the victims. There is also a suspicion that he may have spiked their food. However, the police are awaiting medical reports to ascertain the cause of death,” a source said.

According to the FIR, which also records the accused’s statements, the bodies were dumped at multiple locations on the city’s outskirts and elsewhere in the State, including Yercaud Ghat, Chamundi Hills, Nandi Hills, and Shiradi Ghat. He allegedly used his sedan car, that he used as a cab, to dispose of the bodies. So far, the police have been able to trace only one body, that of the seven-year-old boy.

The incident came to light after a family member of one of the deceased lodged a missing complaint at the Srirampura police station. Subsequent investigations led to Indushekar being detained, and his statements unravelled a series of horrific murders that allegedly took place at his house near Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar, north Bengaluru.

The deceased have been identified as Indushekar’s wife, Sunita (40); his mother-in-law, Roopavathi (65); his two brothers-in-law, Shivakumar (30) and Shankar (44); their wives, Divya (30) and Nalini (29); and Shivakumar’s son, Puneeth (7).

An investigator in the case told The Hindu that the accused had maintained that his wife and mother-in-law did not respect him and frequently verbally abused him, while her family supported them. “The accused claims to have been planning the murders for many months. A recent visit by his mother-in-law did not go well, which angered him,” the source told The Hindu.

articles.title: Vance distancing himself from Trump ahead of 2028 Presidential race: Ex-U.S. NSA Bolton
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Bolton described Vance's remarks as "very wrong" and a "big political mistake", saying the Republicans overlooked broader voter dissatisfaction with the economy, rising prices, and Trump's tariff policies

U.S. Vice President J. D. Vance is trying to distance himself from President Donald Trump by blaming the Republicans' midterm losses on the Iran war as he prepares for a potential 2028 Presidential bid, former U.S. national security adviser John Bolton has said.

In an interview with PTI Videos , Mr. Bolton described Mr. Vance's remarks as "very wrong" and a "big political mistake", saying the Republicans overlooked broader voter dissatisfaction with the economy, rising prices, and Mr. Trump's tariff policies.

"There's no doubt that part of the underlying reason for Mr. Vance’s statement was that this is the beginning of his 2028 nomination campaign. And he's trying something very politically risky here," he said.
Mr. Bolton argued that the Iran war was only one factor behind voter discontent, pointing out that Mr. Trump's tariffs had contributed to persistently high prices.
He said Mr. Trump had promised during the 2024 Presidential campaign to address economic concerns better than the Biden administration, but had failed to deliver after taking office.

"The voters took him at his word. They said we have more faith that Mr. Trump can handle these issues than Mr. Biden and Ms. Harris. So he gets elected, he comes in, and he doesn't do it. And if anything, he's causing more problems," the former U.S. NSA said.

Mr. Bolton also emphasised how the Iran war pushed up international oil and gas prices and increased energy costs for American consumers. "What they opposed was the higher price of gasoline. And Mr. Trump didn't even attempt to address that," he added.

He described the Democrats' strong midterm performance as a "stinging repudiation" of Mr. Trump, saying voters across party lines were tired of his leadership, though the results did not necessarily amount to an endorsement of the blue team.
He also said Mr. Trump was unlikely to fundamentally change his leadership style during the remaining two years of his term, despite the electoral setback.
"Trump's whole operating style for 10 years is: I don't work with anybody. I represent the people, and I'm going to do what I want to do," Mr. Bolton stated.

articles.title: The science behind sleep supplements - melatonin and magnesium
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Doctors warn that there is no replacement for natural solutions, and supplements cannot be taken over a long period

If a good night’s sleep has become your holy grail, who are the knights in shining armour you will employ to reach that chalice? Most people seem to be deploying melatonin and magnesium supplements, over the counter, but the question that remains is: are they effective, and if so, at what combinations or levels?

The consensus among most sleep specialists, is that both melatonin and magnesium (glycinate) can have an ameliorative impact – in the short term. Both these supplements, however, work differently – while melatonin is a key body clock signal, magnesium helps relax the body. When and how you take both supplements makes a great deal of difference to your hours of sleep and sleep quality as well.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh government hikes DA by 3% for employees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63%, up from 60%. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the State government said in a statement on November 7

The Uttar Pradesh government has hiked the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 3% for State government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on UGC pay scales.

Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63%, up from 60%. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the State government said in a statement on Saturday (November 7, 2026). A Government Order was also issued in this regard on Saturday.
The enhanced Dearness Allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the State.

“The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the State's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees,” the statement said.

fullParagraphs: Two women were arrested in separate cases for selling liquor procured through defence canteens at lower prices in Alwal, with excise officials seizing 163 bottles worth an estimated ₹2.11 lakh.

In the first case, the Malkajgiri Enforcement team, led by Assistant Commissioner Pradeep Rao, raided a house in Saraswathi Nagar, Lothukunta, following information about the sale of defence liquor. Officials seized 96 bottles from the house of Manyam Nagaprasanna and her husband Ram Anjaneyulu.

According to excise officials, Ram Anjaneyulu procured the liquor through defence canteens, while his wife Nagaprasanna sold it from their residence. A case was registered against both. Nagaprasanna was arrested and handed over to Alwal Excise Station, Assistant Commissioner Pradeep Rao said.

In another case, the State Task Force team, led by Inspector Ganapathi Reddy, raided a house in Soujanya Colony, New Bowenpally, and seized 67 defence liquor bottles from the possession of Musimi Lenka, 39. She was arrested and handed over to Alwal Excise Station, the inspector said.

articles.title: ‘Arrangements in place for festive rush,’ Railway Minister says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the Ministry was closely tracking railway station crowds over the Deepavali weekend.

Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the government’s “war room” set up for the festive rush was closely tracking crowds across 28 key stations in the Indian Railways network. “We are ensuring that there are additional trains and waiting areas in stations,” Mr. Vaishnaw said, displaying a live dashboard of crowd levels in the various railway stations in the country.

Over 18,000 additional trains had been arranged for this period, Mr. Vaishnaw said, adding that this was well above the 12,000 special trains arranged last year around the same period. The additional trains, Mr. Vaishnaw said, came thanks to an addition in tracks. “We have been constantly adding tracks at many stations,” he said, which was helping with more halts.

A large number of passengers stand in a long queue outside the railway reservation ticket counters to get tickets for their hometowns for the Chhath Puja and Deepavali festivals at Ahmedabad Railway Station, in Ahmedabad. File. | Photo Credit: ANI

The only station that has reached severe crowding by the Railway Ministry’s yardstick is New Delhi (NDLS), where Friday (November 6, 2026) evening saw massive crowds from 4 p.m. onwards. Mr. Vaishnaw said that the crowd was eased out by the additional trains within four hours, and that on Saturday (November 7, 2026) morning, no such crowd built up in the railway station.

Mr. Vaishnaw said that a First Information Report (FIR) had been filed against misleading claims of station crowding that allegedly used old footage, and instructed officials to have those clips taken down from social media.

articles.title: Rayaraddi inaugurates new college buildings in Aland
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayaraddi on Saturday inaugurated the Government Polytechnic College building, constructed at a cost of ₹8 crore, and the Government First Grade Degree College building, constructed at a cost of ₹5.26 crore, on the college campus in Aland.

The polytechnic building was constructed under the Technical Education Scheme for 2017-18, while the first grade college building was built under the Macro/Micro component of the Kalyana Karnataka Regional Development Board (KKRDB) scheme for 2023-24.

Mr. Rayaraddi said the State government had earmarked ₹55,000 crore, or 11.6% of its total Budget of ₹4.48 lakh crore, for the education sector. To improve the quality of higher education, the government would soon fill vacant teaching posts in colleges and universities on the basis of merit, he said.

“Committed to the development of Kalyana Karnataka, our government is allocating ₹5,000 crore annually to the KKRDB. The implementation of Article 371(J) had provided substantial reservation benefits to young people of the region in education and employment,” the Minister said.

Earlier, Mr. Rayaraddi laid the foundation stone for a post-matric boys’ hostel of the Backward Classes Welfare Department at Aland town. The hostel will be built at a cost of ₹5 crore under the joint initiative of the district administration and zilla panchayat, in association with the department and the KKRDB.

Karnataka State Policy and Planning Commission vice-chairman and Aland MLA B.R. Patil said the inauguration of the two college buildings marked an important step in strengthening higher education facilities in Aland taluk.

MP for Bidar Sagar Khandre stressed the need for further improvements in the education sector, including the construction of college buildings and the recruitment of qualified staff. He also said steps were being taken by the State and Central governments to ensure appropriate compensation and insurance benefits for people affected by the drought.

Government Polytechnic College principal Prakash Bure said around 240 students had enrolled in the institution. The new building would help provide quality technical education at an affordable cost and create better opportunities for students from economically poor families in rural areas, he said.

Legislative Council member Tippannappa Kamaknoor, Joint Director of the Collegiate Education Department Pandit Belamagi, backward classes welfare officer V. Ashok, Aland tahsildar Annarao Patil, Government First Grade College principal Premila Ambarao and others were present.

articles.title: Fishermen join hands with INCOIS to improve fishing forecasts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: FISH app enables fishers to take photographs of their catches, which are automatically tagged with location data. The information is transmitted to INCOIS servers, where it undergoes quality checks before being analysed by scientists and fish taxonomy experts

A new mobile application developed by the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) — Android-based app — Fisheries Information Source Hub (FISH), allows fishermen to upload geotagged photographs of their catches directly from the sea, which could transform the way fishing advisories are delivered in the country.

Scientists hope the data will help develop more accurate, species-specific fishing forecasts, enabling fishermen community to find target species more efficiently while supporting sustainable fisheries management.

India’s marine fisheries sector supports the livelihoods of nearly 3.8 million coastal residents. However, the sector faces growing challenges, including over-exploitation of coastal resources, declining catch rates in nearshore waters and significant income disparities between mechanised and small-scale fishers.

INCOIS presently issues daily Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories based on satellite observations of sea surface temperature and chlorophyll concentrations to help reduce search time and improve catch efficiency. But, developing forecasts for specific species requires large volumes of georeferenced catch data, which are not available through conventional fisheries monitoring systems.

To bridge this gap, INCOIS adopted a citizen-science approach making the fishing communities become active partners in scientific research. The FISH app enables fishers to take photographs of their catches, which are automatically tagged with location data. The information is transmitted to INCOIS servers, where it undergoes quality checks before being analysed by scientists and fish taxonomy experts.

“The results have been promising,” says Director T.M. Balakrishnan Nair. During its pilot phase in 2023-24, more than 1,000 fishermen installed the application, while submissions of useful geo-tagged catch photographs increased nearly 20-fold. By the end of 2024, INCOIS had received more than 1,000 validated geo-referenced images from several coastal states.

Available in 10 Indian languages, including Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Gujarati, Marathi, Odia and Bengali, the app has been designed to function even without internet connectivity. The fishermen can capture images at sea and upload them later when network access becomes available, said the director.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 07 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read
