FISH app enables fishers to take photographs of their catches, which are automatically tagged with location data. The information is transmitted to INCOIS servers, where it undergoes quality checks before being analysed by scientists and fish taxonomy experts

A new mobile application developed by the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) — Android-based app — Fisheries Information Source Hub (FISH), allows fishermen to upload geotagged photographs of their catches directly from the sea, which could transform the way fishing advisories are delivered in the country.

Scientists hope the data will help develop more accurate, species-specific fishing forecasts, enabling fishermen community to find target species more efficiently while supporting sustainable fisheries management.

India’s marine fisheries sector supports the livelihoods of nearly 3.8 million coastal residents. However, the sector faces growing challenges, including over-exploitation of coastal resources, declining catch rates in nearshore waters and significant income disparities between mechanised and small-scale fishers.

INCOIS presently issues daily Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories based on satellite observations of sea surface temperature and chlorophyll concentrations to help reduce search time and improve catch efficiency. But, developing forecasts for specific species requires large volumes of georeferenced catch data, which are not available through conventional fisheries monitoring systems.

To bridge this gap, INCOIS adopted a citizen-science approach making the fishing communities become active partners in scientific research. The FISH app enables fishers to take photographs of their catches, which are automatically tagged with location data. The information is transmitted to INCOIS servers, where it undergoes quality checks before being analysed by scientists and fish taxonomy experts.

“The results have been promising,” says Director T.M. Balakrishnan Nair. During its pilot phase in 2023-24, more than 1,000 fishermen installed the application, while submissions of useful geo-tagged catch photographs increased nearly 20-fold. By the end of 2024, INCOIS had received more than 1,000 validated geo-referenced images from several coastal states.

Available in 10 Indian languages, including Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Gujarati, Marathi, Odia and Bengali, the app has been designed to function even without internet connectivity. The fishermen can capture images at sea and upload them later when network access becomes available, said the director.

Scientists say the collected data could help create habitat suitability models and future species-specific advisories for commercially important fish, much like the Tuna advisory service already being operated by INCOIS.

Institute scientists Dhanya M. Lal, T.N.C. Karthik, Sneha Jha, Chennuri Sathish, Susmita Raulo, R. Premkumar, Sanjiba Kumar Baliarsingh, Alakes Samanta and Sudheer Joseph, who did a research on the app, noted that citizen-generated data can complement satellite observations and help fill crucial information gaps in fisheries research. fullParagraphs: Shreya N. Gowda of Thimlapura in Bhadravati town has topped the list of women candidates who qualified in the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination conducted by the Union Public Service Commission

Shreya N. Gowda of Thimlapura in Bhadravati town has topped the list of women candidates who qualified in the Shreya N. Gowda of Thimlapura in Bhadravati town has topped the list of women candidates who qualified in the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination conducted by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). The results were declared on November 5.conducted by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). The results were declared on November 5.

Ms. Shreya, daughter of J. Nagendra, an employee of the Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant in Bhadravati, and B.N. Asha, a lecturer at degree college in the town, secured the first rank in the examination. She is currently pursuing her engineering degree at the National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK), Surathkal.

Ms. Shreya had dreamt of joining the Indian Army since her school days. In 2021, following a Supreme Court order, women were allowed to take the NDA and NA entrance examinations. She was then in class 8. She completed her pre-university in Bengaluru, where she focused on preparing for the NDA and NA entrance examinations. She has been supported and encouraged by her parents and brother Nishchay N. Gowda.

“We are all happy that she has achieved what she aimed for,” said Mr. Nagendra. Ms. Shreya will soon begin her three-year training at Khadakwasla near Pune in Maharashtra. She will then undergo another year of training at the Indian Military Academy in Dehradun.

Several public representatives have congratulated her. In a post on social media, Revenue Minister G. Parameshwara described her achievement as a proud moment for Karnataka and an inspiration to young women across the State who aspire to serve the nation in the armed forces.
MP for Shivamogga B.Y. Raghavendra congratulated Ms. Shreya and also praised her parents for encouraging her to pursue her goal.

articles.title: Airstrike kills 22 people near Yemen's capital, Houthi official says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of November 7 strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital

Airstrikes hit homes in a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday (November 7, 2026), killing at least 22 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children, a spokesman for Yemen's Houthi-run Health Ministry said.

Speaking to The Associated Press , Anees Alasbahi accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes on al-Shariya. The AP could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia's Information Ministry did not immediately reply to an AP request for comment.

The toll reflected the rapid worsening of Yemen's civil war, where a years-long truce fell apart over the summer. Fighting has escalated between the Iranian-backed Houthis — who control Sanaa, the north, and the west of the country — and their Saudi-backed opponents based in the south and east.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), an airstrike in a market in southern Yemen killed at least 30 people, according to Houthi officials. The Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed military each blamed the other for that strike.

Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. Footage from the village showed the rubble of destroyed houses and dust filling the air as people hid in nearby agricultural fields.
Mr. Alasbahi said in a posting earlier on X that Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes hit several homes in al-Shariyah. Subsequent strikes targeted emergency responders, he told the AP .

In September, the Houthis made a lightning advance, capturing much of Yemen's Red Sea coast and strategic islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. They have also encircled the city of Taiz, a strategic gateway to southern Yemen. At the same time, they have stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, targeting oil and military infrastructure and shipping in the Red Sea.

Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of November 7 strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital

Airstrikes hit homes in a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday (November 7, 2026), killing at least 22 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children, a spokesman for Yemen's Houthi-run Health Ministry said.

Speaking to The Associated Press , Anees Alasbahi accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes on al-Shariya. The AP could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia's Information Ministry did not immediately reply to an AP request for comment.

The toll reflected the rapid worsening of Yemen's civil war, where a years-long truce fell apart over the summer. Fighting has escalated between the Iranian-backed Houthis — who control Sanaa, the north, and the west of the country — and their Saudi-backed opponents based in the south and east.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), an airstrike in a market in southern Yemen killed at least 30 people, according to Houthi officials. The Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed military each blamed the other for that strike.

Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. Footage from the village showed the rubble of destroyed houses and dust filling the air as people hid in nearby agricultural fields.

Mr. Alasbahi said in a posting earlier on X that Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes hit several homes in al-Shariyah. Subsequent strikes targeted emergency responders, he told the AP .

In September, the Houthis made a lightning advance, capturing much of Yemen's Red Sea coast and strategic islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. They have also encircled the city of Taiz, a strategic gateway to southern Yemen. At the same time, they have stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, targeting oil and military infrastructure and shipping in the Red Sea.

Iran said Saturday (November 7, 2026) its military has grown "stronger" since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran's nuclear programme.
Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the West Asia conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.
He also said Iran's forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," he said.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), the U.S. military said it was offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

articles.title: Alleged habitual offender sent to jail under KAAPA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ​The 40-year-old was already in judicial custody after allegedly stealing a two-wheeler parked outside a textile showroom in Pantheerankavu

A 40-year-old alleged habitual offender was sent to the Kannur Central Prison under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA) after being linked to scores of theft cases in the region.
​The man was identified as Mujeeb, a resident of Arappayil, Peringalam. He is listed as a known offender at the Kunnamangalam police station in Kozhikode.

The police said Mujeeb faces more than 35 cases across Kozhikode and Malappuram districts, with cases registered at stations including Kondotty, Karipur, Areekode, Edacherry, Koduvally, Atholi, Kunnamangalam, Pantheerankavu, Town, Nadakkavu and Vellayil. The allegations against him include snatching cash and jewellery, stealing vehicles parked in public places and breaking into locked shops.
He was already in judicial custody following his arrest for reportedly stealing a two-wheeler parked outside a textile showroom at Pantheerankavu on September 1.
​Mujeeb had previously served six months in preventive detention under Section 3(1) of KAAPA during 2024–25 before his release.

​The latest action was taken by the Kunnamangalam police owing to his repeated offences. Following a preliminary report by the local sub-inspector and a recommendation from Deputy Commissioner of Police (Kozhikode City) Padam Singh, District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty ordered his transfer to the Kannur Central Prison.

articles.title: NDA wins eight ZPTC seats in Palnadu district

fullParagraphs: Telugu Desam Party secures six seats and Jana Sena Party wins two in eight of the 10 ZPTC constituencies after vote counting on Saturday

The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), comprising the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Jana Sena Party (JSP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), secured all eight declared Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) seats in Palnadu district, with the TDP winning six and the JSP two.

According to the results available on Saturday, counting was completed in eight of the 10 ZPTC constituencies, while results in Muppalla and Sattenapalli mandals were awaited. The TDP registered victories in Dachepalle, Gurazala, Machavaram, Nekarikallu, Piduguralla and Rajupalem. The JSP won Krosuru and Nuzendla constituencies.

In the overall ZPTC tally, the TDP was leading in one additional constituency, bringing its total number of leads to seven. The JSP was leading in another constituency, taking its tally to three. The BJP and YSRCP had neither won nor led in any constituency.
Meanwhile, MPTC election results were yet to be declared by the district election authorities.

articles.title: Radial road from Shamshabad to Kodangal will be completed by Dec. 2027, says CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said the radial road connecting Shamshabad with Kodangal would be completed by December 2027 and it would enable people to reach Kodangal from the international airport in about 70 minutes, making the region attractive for domestic and foreign investors.

Addressing a meeting with nearly 100 industrialists at the launch of the Kodangal Rural Agriculture Region Economy (RARE) Industrial Hub on Saturday, he said, “Making Kodangal a great industrial hub is my responsibility and my dream. Kodangal is my identity and self-respect.”

He expressed satisfaction that some companies had already begun construction in the industrial hub, while several others had shown interest in setting up their units. He said Kodangal had strategic advantages because of its proximity to Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
Along with Kodangal, the areas of Chandanvelly, Sitarampur and Pargi were expected to witness significant industrial development in the coming years.

He said a 250-acre Kodangal Education Hub was being developed to establish educational institutions alongside the industrial infrastructure. Advanced Technology Centres were being established in all Assembly constituencies in the State with the support of Tata Technologies to provide skill training to students.
Representatives from the aerospace, defence, green technology, renewable energy, steel, copper, textile and agro-based industries attended the interaction.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said the radial road connecting Shamshabad with Kodangal would be completed by December 2027 and it would enable people to reach Kodangal from the international airport in about 70 minutes, making the region attractive for domestic and foreign investors.

Addressing a meeting with nearly 100 industrialists at the launch of the Kodangal Rural Agriculture Region Economy (RARE) Industrial Hub on Saturday, he said, “Making Kodangal a great industrial hub is my responsibility and my dream. Kodangal is my identity and self-respect.”

He expressed satisfaction that some companies had already begun construction in the industrial hub, while several others had shown interest in setting up their units. He said Kodangal had strategic advantages because of its proximity to Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.

Along with Kodangal, the areas of Chandanvelly, Sitarampur and Pargi were expected to witness significant industrial development in the coming years.

He said a 250-acre Kodangal Education Hub was being developed to establish educational institutions alongside the industrial infrastructure. Advanced Technology Centres were being established in all Assembly constituencies in the State with the support of Tata Technologies to provide skill training to students.

Representatives from the aerospace, defence, green technology, renewable energy, steel, copper, textile and agro-based industries attended the interaction.

articles.title: From strategic Eastern airbase, Rajnath calls for highest military preparedness
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Defence Minister calls upon the military to keep special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience, and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats

The security landscape around the country has become increasingly complex, and India’s armed forces must maintain the highest level of operational readiness to effectively counter any threats to national security, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday (November 7, 2026) told personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force station in West Bengal.

Delivering his message on the eve of Deepavali from the key airbase near the frontier with China in the Eastern sector, Mr. Singh, without naming any country, said the adversary now avoids direct confrontation but seeks to exploit certain "vulnerabilities". He called upon the military to keep special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience, and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats, according to the Defence Ministry.

"Often, the adversary avoids direct confrontation and instead seeks to exploit our vulnerabilities. Through social media, the adversary may attempt to sow doubt in the minds of the local population and our soldiers by spreading misleading information," Mr. Singh said. "In such a scenario, your role extends beyond that of an ordinary soldier," he added.

The Defence Minister emphasised that the security landscape has become "increasingly complex", with warfare extending beyond conventional engagements along the borders to encompass asymmetric operations, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone swarms, information operations, and narrative management.

Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important region and a crucial link in India's security framework, particularly for the northeastern region, Mr. Singh commended the courage and dedication of the defence personnel towards safeguarding national interests.

He stated that the Air Force personnel deployed in the region serve as a robust shield for the security of the eastern sector, and their preparedness is fundamental to maintaining stability in the region.

The Defence Minister underscored that discipline and courage remain indispensable, irrespective of technological advancements, stating that the conduct and restraint of the defence personnel shape the image of the military among local communities.

Lauding the soldiers for discharging their duties with these qualities, Mr. Singh urged them to strengthen their engagement with the local population, particularly in and around Bagdogra, and nurture the deep bond of trust and affection between the people and the defence forces.
"The more you engage with the local community, the weaker the adversary's conspiracies will become," he said.

Reaffirming the government's resolve to achieve ' Aatmanirbhar Bharat', Mr. Singh highlighted the growing contribution of Indian start-ups and industries in developing drones, anti- drone systems, and advanced military equipment. He appreciated the defence forces for embracing indigenous technologies and acquiring new skills in drone operations and cyber security and underlined the importance of making the military increasingly technology-driven to effectively address future security challenges.

articles.title: VISTAR: India’s shift towards a real-time, technology-driven statistical system | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: For an economy aspiring to become a developed nation by 2047, the statistical blind spots could translate into costly policy mistakes, misdirected investments and ineffective welfare schemes

India’s statistical requirements have outgrown the conventional survey-based architecture, requiring a more scientific and technological architecture to better capture key performance indicators of economy, even as it should avoid the growing risks of synthetic data.

Seeking to move official data collection beyond periodic surveys and administrative records, the VISTAR or Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research is a major overhaul of India’s official statistical system at the centre and state levels using interoperable datasets, bridging data gaps and generating timely, reliable socioeconomic indicators for evidence-based policymaking.

articles.title: Rajajingar murders: How did the accused transport bodies across locations without being caught?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Neither a patrolling vehicle nor a checkpoint caught the accused Indushekhar even as he crossed State borders

At least three trips with seven bodies in the car to four different locations, and one of them an inter-State journey. Yet, the accused in the alleged Rajajinagar murders, Indushekhar, was never detected. This has raised questions about the effectiveness of the nakabandi (checkpoints) and night patrolling system in the city.

Indushekar, prime accused in the case where he killed his wife and six others from her family , resided in a building near (barely 100 metres) the famous Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar. The junction is barely 3 km from Majestic, the city’s transport hub. It connects to Chord Road, one of the major roads in the city. The junction also provides connectivity between the central, western and southern parts of Bengaluru.
The accused allegedly brought the bodies down from the second floor and transported them to Mysuru, deep into the Western Ghats (Shiradi Ghat), to the Tamil Nadu border and to Chickballapur.

The alleged incidents unfolded over 15 days. Neither a patrolling vehicle nor a checkpoint detected the accused, even as he crossed State borders. The development comes amid frequent police checks at night across the city. In several instances, there have also been allegations of harassment during such checks.
A senior police officer told The Hindu that the accused’s movement with bodies in the car was among the questions on their investigation list, though it was not their immediate focus.

“A team has already been deployed to recreate all the movements of the accused and gather footage of his movements after October 16. We will verify whether he passed any checkpoints in the city and whether there was any negligence on the part of officers,” he said.
The officer stressed that the immediate focus was on recovering the bodies, as they were the prime evidence in the case. Any dereliction of duty could be investigated at a later stage.

The officer further said that they suspect the accused deliberately avoided stretches where checkpoints were set up. “We must also consider that all vehicles are checked at checkpoints. He may have passed through one,” the officer added.

“We also suspect that he avoided toll plazas. For a person who meticulously planned how to clean the crime scene thoroughly, he must have planned the routes in advance and executed the disposals accordingly,” the officer said.

The officer also pointed to a murder cover-up in a case reported in C.K. Acchukattu in 2025. The body was found dumped in a garbage pile. However, the accused had transported it from Madiwala to C.K. Acchukattu. What was even more surprising was that the accused had carried the body alone on a scooter.

The accused allegedly brought the bodies down from the second floor and transported them to Mysuru, deep into the Western Ghats (Shiradi Ghat), to the Tamil Nadu border and to Chickballapur.

The development comes amid frequent police checks at night across the city. In several instances, there have also been allegations of harassment during such checks.

A senior police officer told The Hindu that the accused’s movement with bodies in the car was among the questions on their investigation list, though it was not their immediate focus.

fullParagraphs: Students should dare to dream big, think independently and pursue ambitious goals to drive innovation and contribute to the vision of a self-reliant India, said Prof. Ramesh Srikonda, Director of the School of Planning and Architecture, Vijayawada.

Vice-Chancellor Dr. K.R.S. Sambasiva Rao urged students to make effective use of the university’s teaching and learning facilities and continuously upgrade their skills to become industry-ready professionals.
Organising convener and Dean D. Suneetha, CEO, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Registrar, Deans, Heads of Departments, faculty members and other dignitaries attended the celebrations.

articles.title: Bengaluru’s GBA launches phase 2 of ‘Ward One’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Saturday directed officials to prepare a comprehensive plan for the redevelopment of the K.R. Puram-Tin Factory Junction. The plan should focus on pedestrian safety, public transport integration and smoother traffic movement, he said.

The directions came during the launch of the second phase of the ‘Ward One’ campaign. The second phase has been launched across around 40 wards. The first phase covered 43 wards, with nearly 90% of the identified works completed, Mr. Gowda said.

On Saturday, the Minister inspected the K.R. Puram-Tin Factory Junction and reviewed the problems from ongoing metro and K-RIDE works and the pedestrian infrastructure, following which directions were issued.

The plan would be prepared jointly by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), Namma Metro officials, and Janaagraha, he said. The plan would cover road design, footpaths, bus bays, bus stops and traffic management. The Minister also called for scientifically redesigning the junction, improving road curves, and providing free left turns wherever necessary.

He directed metro officials to restore roads affected by the construction without delay. “Potholes on connecting roads must be repaired within a week. Roads at lower levels, which are prone to flooding, also need to be improved,” he told officials.
The campaign brings together various civic agencies to address potholes, damaged footpaths, garbage accumulation, construction waste, streetlights and drain desilting.

articles.title: No complete closure of Ballari Road for 18 months for elevated corridor work: BDA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period.

The Hebbal Flyover and Ballari Road corridor will not be completely closed for 18 months to facilitate the construction of the elevated corridor, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) clarified on Saturday (November 7). Meanwhile, the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) said vehicular movement would continue with limited lane restrictions and phased traffic diversions.

The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period. The elevated corridor is part of the BDA’s larger Integrated Tunnel and Elevated Corridor Project, aimed at easing congestion along the city’s crucial northern corridor connecting Bengaluru with Kempegowda International Airport. However, the project has also drawn considerable public criticism since it was announced.

The BTP sources said restrictions would apply only to the movement of heavy vehicles between 6 a.m. and 8 p.m., while other motorists would merely be “advised” to take alternative routes. Public transport vehicles and school buses would also be allowed to use the stretch.

The BDA said barricading would be restricted to a lane approximately 4.5 metres wide, affecting only one of the three existing lanes in each direction. The remaining two lanes and the service road would remain open to traffic.

The concern, however, is that the 4.5-metre-wide lane is part of one of the main carriageways and accounts for 35% of the traffic movement on the stretch at any given time. Consequently, the restrictions are likely to worsen congestion, irrespective of the timing of their implementation. At least 20% of the traffic will therefore need to be diverted to prevent gridlock along the stretch.
“Even without civic works, the stretch witnesses prolonged congestion during peak hours. So, with civic works, the need for traffic diversion is essential,” a police source said.

This makes the advisory to use alternative routes necessary. However, the identified alternate routes are also in poor condition. The BTP has now written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and the BDA, requesting them to asphalt the alternative routes to ensure the smooth movement of vehicles and prevent congestion.

“Routes through New BEL Road and R.T. Nagar Station Road are among those being considered for improvement. Officials have also been asked to identify bottlenecks, improve road surfaces, and install adequate signage and road markings,” the BDA said.

fullParagraphs: In a statement, the Hamas-run government media office said that about "70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day" of rains
Heavy rain on Saturday (November 7, 2026) flooded tens of thousands of displaced people's tents in war-devastated Gaza, Palestinian authorities said, leaving them without shelter.

Maryam Odeh, 34, who lives with her children in Deir al-Balah, said, "We no longer know how to protect our children. My children ask me where we will sleep tonight, and I have no answer".

articles.title: Ukraine says Russia ramps up strikes to pressure Kyiv at talks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Ukraine's Energy Ministry said "a massive attack on a number of energy facilities" had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding region

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday (November 7, 2026) accused Russia of intensifying strikes across the country to put pressure on Kyiv at upcoming talks after an overnight barrage triggered power cuts as temperatures drop.

The latest strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure came days before the trilateral U.S.-brokered meeting in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026), aimed at reviving stalled diplomatic efforts towards peace.

Ukraine's Energy Ministry said "a massive attack on a number of energy facilities" had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding region.

Mr. Zelenskyy said the timing of the aerial barrage showed that Russia had a "very particular view of diplomacy" as it struck ahead of "another joint effort with our partners to reinvigorate negotiations".

"By intensifying its attacks on Ukraine and our infrastructure at this very moment, Russia is trying to lay the groundwork for putting pressure on Ukraine's position and that of its partners," Mr. Zelenskyy said.

Moscow has battered Ukraine's energy grid and infrastructure throughout its four-and-a-half-year invasion, and Kyiv is now bracing for another harsh winter as temperatures begin to hover around freezing.
Mr. Zelenskyy also said Russia had, throughout the night, launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, among which, according to him, were KN-23 missiles manufactured and supplied by North Korea.
They hit "one of the key energy facilities that was damaged", Mr. Zelenskyy said.
Russia has turned to North Korea for support throughout invasion.
Earlier in the war, Pyongyang dispatched thousands of troops to help Russia fight back a Ukrainian counterattack in its western Kursk region.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed’s describes himself as ‘just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works’ and identifies as a progressive; his candidacy was backed by leading figures such as Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

In a country where, for more than a quarter of a century, the word “Muslim” has been used as an accusation in politics, Abdul El-Sayed’s election as the first Muslim member of the U.S. Senate breaks perhaps the thickest of glass ceilings in American public life. Dr. El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated the Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote, seven percentage points ahead of his rival.

It would be easy to dismiss this victory as merely a byproduct of the “blue wave” in the U.S. midterms, which carried Democratic candidates to wins even in Republican strongholds such as South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. But that would be a reductive reading. The odds Dr. El-Sayed faced make the win remarkable in its own right.

articles.title: As COP31 comes to Turkiye, satellites reveal a landfill methane problem
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Methane is the biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide (CO2) and is over 80 times more potent than CO2 in its first 20 years in the air. Sharp cuts could therefore slow warming relatively quickly

In the countryside west ​of Istanbul, trucks line up to empty mixed household waste from the city of 16 million people onto a vast landscape of decomposing rubbish, where landfill gas is captured to ‌generate electricity at a nearby plant.
But far above the seagulls circling the waste, satellites detect what the plant has failed to ​capture: methane escaping at a rate that ranks it among the world’s largest recorded landfill emitters.
Turkiye hosts COP31 in Antalya from November ⁠9 to 20 and has made methane reduction a priority for the climate summit.

Methane is the biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide (CO2) and is over 80 times more potent than CO2 in its first 20 years in the air. Sharp cuts could therefore slow warming relatively quickly.
Turkiye’s waste sector illustrates both the potential and the difficulty of achieving rapid ‌cuts.
The country is the world’s fifth-biggest emitter of methane from solid waste behind China, the United States, Russia and Brazil, according to data from non-profit emissions tracker Climate TRACE.

Satellite observations analysed by researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) identified 70 plumes from Turkiye’s 10 highest-emitting ‌waste sites, where average detected rates ranged from 841 kg to 7.4 metric tons an hour. Three were around Istanbul, while others were near Ankara, Izmir ‌and ⁠Antalya, where COP31 is being held.
Gas capture is widespread at Turkiye’s larger municipal landfills, indicating that collection systems alone do not prevent ⁠large releases.

Tia Scarpelli, waste sector lead for emissions-monitoring non-profit Carbon Mapper, said cutting landfill methane requires diverting organic material before it reaches dumps, while improving rates of capture.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 07 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 As COP31 comes to Turkiye, satellites reveal a landfill methane problem

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

Methane is the biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide (CO2) and is over 80 times more potent than CO2 in its first 20 years in the air. Sharp cuts could therefore slow warming relatively quickly

In the countryside west ​of Istanbul, trucks line up to empty mixed household waste from the city of 16 million people onto a vast landscape of decomposing rubbish, where landfill gas is captured to ‌generate electricity at a nearby plant.

But far above the seagulls circling the waste, satellites detect what the plant has failed to ​capture: methane escaping at a rate that ranks it among the world’s largest recorded landfill emitters.

Turkiye hosts COP31 in Antalya from November ⁠9 to 20 and has made methane reduction a priority for the climate summit.

Methane is the biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide (CO2) and is over 80 times more potent than CO2 in its first 20 years in the air. Sharp cuts could therefore slow warming relatively quickly.

Turkiye’s waste sector illustrates both the potential and the difficulty of achieving rapid ‌cuts.

The country is the world’s fifth-biggest emitter of methane from solid waste behind China, the United States, Russia and Brazil, according to data from non-profit emissions tracker Climate TRACE.

Satellite observations analysed by researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) identified 70 plumes from Turkiye’s 10 highest-emitting ‌waste sites, where average detected rates ranged from 841 kg to 7.4 metric tons an hour. Three were around Istanbul, while others were near Ankara, Izmir ‌and ⁠Antalya, where COP31 is being held.

Gas capture is widespread at Turkiye’s larger municipal landfills, indicating that collection systems alone do not prevent ⁠large releases.

Tia Scarpelli, waste sector lead for emissions-monitoring non-profit Carbon Mapper, said cutting landfill methane requires diverting organic material before it reaches dumps, while improving rates of capture.

Because Turkiye’s largest detected emissions were concentrated at a few sites, addressing those landfills could deliver disproportionate gains, Scarpelli said.

articles.title: Madras HC refuses to reject Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi’s election petition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice K. Kumaresh Babu dismisses an application filed by Thiruverumbur TVK MLA Vijayakumar alias Navalpattu Viji to reject the election petition

The Madras High Court has refused to reject an election petition filed by former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi of the DMK challenging the victory of TVK MLA Vijayakumar alias Navalapattu Viji from Thiruverumbur Assembly constituency in the 2026 election.

Justice K. Kumaresh Babu said the Election Commission of India’s instructions to not engage children in election campaigns had a statutory force and, hence, the veracity of the allegation levelled against the MLA of having engaged children for his campaign could be tested only during trial. The judge dismissed an application filed by the MLA to reject the petition.
Mr. Vijayakumar had won the seat by a margin of 8,705 votes. He had secured 89,837 votes as against 81,132 votes garnered by the election petitioner who was his nearest rival candidate.

articles.title: Bengaluru Metro conducts trial run of Blue Line train at Byappanahalli depot
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) conducted a trial run of a train on the test track at the Byappanahalli depot on Saturday as part of preparations for the much-awaited Blue Line.

The trial involved checking electrical systems, assessing the readiness of rolling stock and identifying possible infringements along the track. BMRCL is expected to move testing to the main line shortly. An official said that the testing would resume next week, subject to the availability of workers following Deepavali.
Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) has manufactured the driverless trainset for the Blue Line.

The Blue Line, comprising Metro Phases 2A and 2B, is a major infrastructure project connecting the city with Kempegowda International Airport. The K.R. Puram–airport stretch is 38.44-km long, while the K.R. Puram–Central Silk Board section covers 19.75 km.

articles.title: Mathematics key to AI’s advancement, says expert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mathematics forms the backbone of modern artificial intelligence (AI), with advanced AI capabilities, predictive power and logical reasoning deeply rooted in mathematical equations, frameworks and data algorithms, said Reheena Nasrin of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Addressing the valedictory session of a three-day international conference on “Computation Science and Intelligent Engineering”, organised by the Department of Mathematics in Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education (Deemed-to-be-University), she emphasised that strong mathematical foundations would remain essential for the future advancement of digital intelligence.

The final-day technical sessions featured lectures by eminent experts. G. Sobhalatha of Sri Krishnadevaraya University, Anantapur, spoke on ‘Lexicographic Product Graph’, while Bukke Kiran Naik, a scientist from the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Rourkela, delivered a lecture on ‘Intelligent Thermodynamics’, focusing on data-driven systems optimisation and energy-water nexus solutions.

Conference convener Charan announced that more than 200 research papers had been presented by academicians and researchers from reputed universities across India, reflecting the conference’s contribution to academic research and knowledge exchange. Certificates of participation and excellence were distributed to the paper presenters by the dignitaries.
The valedictory session was attended by Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao, Pro-Vice-Chancellor A.V. Ratna Prasad, dean D. Venkata Rao and registrar M. Ravichand.

Head of the Mathematics Department Ch. Baby Rani, senior faculty members K. Hemalatha, J. Siva Ram Prasad and M.V.D.N.S. Madhavi, other faculty members, department heads, research scholars and students also participated in the programme.

articles.title: Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight returns to Bengaluru after hijack threat note found onboard
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Flight 6E-451 had departed from Terminal 1 of KIA when cabin crew members found the note that said “This flight is going to hijack at 6.30, ignore and see the consequences”

A Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight made an emergency return to Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) in Bengaluru on Saturday (November 7, 2026) after a handwritten note on a hijack threat was discovered inside the lavatory shortly after take-off.
Flight 6E-451 had departed from Terminal 1 of KIA when cabin crew members found the note. The message reportedly read: “This flight is going to hijack at 6.30, ignore and see the consequences.”

The crew immediately alerted the pilot-in-command, who informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) and sought priority clearance to return to Bengaluru. Airport authorities declared a full emergency as a precautionary measure.
According to flight-tracking website Flightradar24, the aircraft remained airborne for 51 minutes before returning to KIA. | Photo Credit: Flightradar24
According to flight-tracking website Flightradar24, the aircraft remained airborne for 51 minutes before returning to KIA.

The aircraft landed safely and was moved to an isolated bay, where security agencies, including the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) and the Bengaluru police, cordoned off the area. All passengers were safely deboarded in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Bomb disposal personnel and dog squads were deployed to inspect the aircraft and passenger baggage as part of the security checks. Sources in Bangalore International Airport Ltd. (BIAL) told The Hindu that the aircraft was subjected to a thorough inspection following the threat. The checks did not reveal anything suspicious, and the aircraft was declared safe. “The threat was subsequently found to be a hoax, following which the emergency was lifted by the authorities,” the sources said.
Officials said that an investigation has been initiated to ascertain who left the handwritten note inside the aircraft.

In a statement to The Hindu , an IndiGo spokesperson said in line with Standard Operating Procedure, the relevant authorities were informed immediately and the pilots decided to return to origin to carry out the necessary security checks, as per protocol. The airline said it was providing refreshments and regular updates to passengers. The flight will resume its journey after receiving the requisite clearances. IndiGo said passenger and crew safety remained its utmost priority.

A Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight made an emergency return to Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) in Bengaluru on Saturday (November 7, 2026) after a handwritten note on a hijack threat was discovered inside the lavatory shortly after take-off.

Flight 6E-451 had departed from Terminal 1 of KIA when cabin crew members found the note. The message reportedly read: “This flight is going to hijack at 6.30, ignore and see the consequences.”

The crew immediately alerted the pilot-in-command, who informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) and sought priority clearance to return to Bengaluru. Airport authorities declared a full emergency as a precautionary measure.

According to flight-tracking website Flightradar24, the aircraft remained airborne for 51 minutes before returning to KIA. | Photo Credit: Flightradar24

According to flight-tracking website Flightradar24, the aircraft remained airborne for 51 minutes before returning to KIA.

The aircraft landed safely and was moved to an isolated bay, where security agencies, including the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) and the Bengaluru police, cordoned off the area. All passengers were safely deboarded in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Bomb disposal personnel and dog squads were deployed to inspect the aircraft and passenger baggage as part of the security checks. Sources in Bangalore International Airport Ltd. (BIAL) told The Hindu that the aircraft was subjected to a thorough inspection following the threat. The checks did not reveal anything suspicious, and the aircraft was declared safe. “The threat was subsequently found to be a hoax, following which the emergency was lifted by the authorities,” the sources said.

Officials said that an investigation has been initiated to ascertain who left the handwritten note inside the aircraft.

In a statement to The Hindu , an IndiGo spokesperson said in line with Standard Operating Procedure, the relevant authorities were informed immediately and the pilots decided to return to origin to carry out the necessary security checks, as per protocol. articles.title: Rajajingar murders: How did the accused transport bodies across locations without being detected?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Neither a patrolling vehicle nor a checkpoint detected the accused Indushekhar even as he crossed State borders

At least three trips with seven bodies in the car to four different locations, and one of them an inter-State journey. Yet, the accused in the alleged Rajajinagar murders, Indushekhar, was never detected. This has raised questions about the effectiveness of the nakabandi (checkpoints) and night patrolling system in the city.

Indushekar, prime accused in the case where he killed his wife and six others from her family , resided in a building near (barely 100 metres) the famous Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar. The junction is barely 3 km from Majestic, the city’s transport hub. It connects to Chord Road, one of the major roads in the city. The junction also provides connectivity between the central, western and southern parts of Bengaluru.
The accused allegedly brought the bodies down from the second floor and transported them to Mysuru, deep into the Western Ghats (Shiradi Ghat), to the Tamil Nadu border and to Chickballapur.

The alleged incidents unfolded over 15 days. Neither a patrolling vehicle nor a checkpoint detected the accused, even as he crossed State borders. The development comes amid frequent police checks at night across the city. In several instances, there have also been allegations of harassment during such checks.
A senior police officer told The Hindu that the accused’s movement with bodies in the car was among the questions on their investigation list, though it was not their immediate focus.

“A team has already been deployed to recreate all the movements of the accused and gather footage of his movements after October 16. We will verify whether he passed any checkpoints in the city and whether there was any negligence on the part of officers,” he said.
The officer stressed that the immediate focus was on recovering the bodies, as they were the prime evidence in the case. Any dereliction of duty could be investigated at a later stage.

The officer further said that they suspect the accused deliberately avoided stretches where checkpoints were set up. “We must also consider that all vehicles are checked at checkpoints. He may have passed through one,” the officer added.

“We also suspect that he avoided toll plazas. For a person who meticulously planned how to clean the crime scene thoroughly, he must have planned the routes in advance and executed the disposals accordingly,” the officer said.

The officer also pointed to a murder cover-up in a case reported in C.K. Acchukattu in 2025. The body was found dumped in a garbage pile. However, the accused had transported it from Madiwala to C.K. Acchukattu. What was even more surprising was that the accused had carried the body alone on a scooter.

articles.title: Nithya Raman | The urban planner
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Before entering U.S. politics, L.A.’s first South Asian Mayor-elect worked among the urban poor in Chennai, where she used data to expose gaps in slum resettlement and public facilities

After defeating Karen Bass, the incumbent Mayor of the second most populous city of the U.S., Nithya Raman wrote on X, “Los Angeles, I am deeply honored to be your next mayor.” A member of the city council since 2020, Ms. Raman has a track record of civic activism, advocating for affordable and increased housing. Entering the electoral race at the very last minute, she is now L.A.’s the first South Asian Mayor-elect as well as the first candidate to defeat an incumbent Mayor of the city since 2005.

Born in Keralam, Ms. Raman spent a part of her early childhood between Thiruvananthapuram and Thrissur. Her father, Venkataraman, used to work for Keltron, and her mother, Sudha, was a former employee of the Indian Overseas Bank. The family migrated to the U.S. when Ms. Raman was six. She graduated from Harvard University in 2003, and then got a master’s degree in urban planning from MIT. She became a U.S. citizen at 22.

fullParagraphs: While headlines scream Ossoff looks more presidential after his Senate win, he remains focused on his State while attacking Donald Trump and his family

There is something of an investigative journalist in Jon Ossoff, who served as managing director and chief executive officer of Insight: The World Investigates, a London-based investigative television production company. During his Senate campaign as Democratic candidate in Georgia and even before, he had been mounting a blistering campaign against corruption. It resonated with the voters struggling with rising food prices and unaffordable fuel.

Mr. Ossoff won the November 3 election against Republican Mike Collins, becoming the only incumbent Senate Democrat to defend a seat in a State President Donald Trump carried in 2024. Ever since his win in the 2021 Senate race in Georgia, the charismatic Mr. Ossoff has been making the lists of possible candidates for the Democratic ticket in the 2028 Presidential election. But, like Barack Obama before his 2004 Senate win and scores of others before him, Mr. Ossoff, now 39, who in 2021 became the youngest U.S. Senator since 1980, has been vehemently denying any such aspiration. The media, however, has been quick in spotting in him similarities with Mr. Obama, especially the former President’s speech delivery.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: Jon Ossoff | Ambition without ambition. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.

For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%. Non-monetary poverty indicators, as per OPHI’s Multi-dimensional Poverty Index, also recorded a sharp reduction in overall poverty numbers, i.e., from 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21.

articles.title: Willem Einthoven’s Nobel-winning discovery that laid the foundations of the modern ECG
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Willem Einthoven’s development of the string galvanometer transformed the recording of cardiac electrical signals and laid the foundations of modern electrocardiography
In 1924, Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine “for his discovery of the mechanism of the electrocardiogram (ECG)”.

His work made it possible to record the electrical activity of the heart with greater accuracy. By developing the string galvanometer and establishing a standard method for interpreting its recordings, Einthoven helped turn electrocardiography into an important tool for studying heart function. Today, the ECG is routinely used to investigate irregular heart rhythms, detect signs of reduced blood supply to the heart muscle and identify evidence of previous heart attacks.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Willem Einthoven’s Nobel-winning discovery that laid the foundations of the modern ECG. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Willem Einthoven’s development of the string galvanometer transformed the recording of cardiac electrical signals and laid the foundations of modern electrocardiography

In 1924, Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine “for his discovery of the mechanism of the electrocardiogram (ECG)”.

His work made it possible to record the electrical activity of the heart with greater accuracy. By developing the string galvanometer and establishing a standard method for interpreting its recordings, Einthoven helped turn electrocardiography into an important tool for studying heart function. Today, the ECG is routinely used to investigate irregular heart rhythms, detect signs of reduced blood supply to the heart muscle and identify evidence of previous heart attacks.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
